title: Rethinking search signatures: Hadronic decays of GeV-scale feebly coupled particles
summary: Experimental searches for GeV-scale feebly interacting particles commonly target the simplest decay signatures with two charged particles, including hadrons. Hadronic modes often dominate the inclusive decay rate, and their simulation relies extensively on \textsc{Pythia}. Its fragmentation model, calibrated mainly on LEP data, is unreliable in this mass range: it populates symmetry-forbidden states and misidentifies the dominant allowed channels. We construct a simple hadronization model tuned to electromagnetic scattering data and constrained by conservation laws and available exclusive decay calculations, while retaining a common prescription applicable to different particle models. Considering the SHiP experiment as an example, we show that our model shifts the dominant search signature after event selection from two-particle to multiparticle decays, including mixed charged-neutral states. We provide the model in a form that can be readily integrated into \textsc{Pythia}-based experimental simulation frameworks.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a new hadronization model for GeV-scale feebly interacting particles, correcting Pythia's unreliable fragmentation in this mass regime; applied to SHiP, it shifts the dominant search signature from two-body to multiparticle (including charged–neutral) decays.
AI.motivation: Pythia's fragmentation model—calibrated on LEP data—is unreliable for GeV-scale feebly interacting particles: it populates symmetry-forbidden states and misidentifies dominant allowed decay channels, undermining experimental sensitivity.
AI.method: The authors construct a simplified, physically constrained hadronization model tuned to electromagnetic scattering data, enforcing conservation laws (e.g., charge, C/P) and incorporating available exclusive decay calculations; the model is designed for broad applicability across particle models and seamless integration into Pythia-based simulation frameworks.
AI.result: For the SHiP experiment, the new model predicts a significant shift in dominant post-selection signatures—from two-charged-particle decays to multiparticle final states, including mixed charged–neutral topologies—altering expected event yields and background composition.
AI.conclusion: The proposed model provides a more reliable, first-principles-informed alternative to Pythia’s default fragmentation for GeV-scale BSM searches, improving phenomenological accuracy and experimental design robustness.

title: Reconciling axion quality with post-inflation cosmology
summary: We address the axion quality/cosmology tension that often plagues QCD axion models in post-inflationary Peccei-Quinn (PQ) breaking scenarios. In the proposed framework, the PQ symmetry emerges accidentally from an ${\rm SU}(\mathcal{N})_L\times{\rm SU}(\mathcal{N})_R$ gauge symmetry spontaneously broken to ${\rm SU}(\mathcal{N})_{L+R}$, and its quality is protected because PQ breaking first appears at operator dimension $\mathcal{N}$. Moreover, the construction avoids the domain-wall problem, ensures that no stable fractionally charged relic survives ${\rm SU} (\mathcal{N})_{L+R}$ confinement, and remains free of Landau poles below the scale of PQ-breaking operators. The exotic quarks required to generate the PQ anomaly hadronize into unstable mesons and cosmologically stable neutral baryons. However, plausible arguments indicating a strong suppression of baryon formation in ${\rm SU}(\mathcal{N})$ gauge theories at large $\mathcal{N}$, suggest that their contribution to the dark matter energy density remains subdominant. Combining cosmological constraints with PQ quality and perturbativity requirements yields a viable parameter space in which the axion makes up most of the dark matter and its mass remains predictable.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a novel QCD axion model where the Peccei-Quinn (PQ) symmetry emerges accidentally from an SU(N)_L × SU(N)_R gauge symmetry broken to SU(N)_{L+R}, ensuring high-quality PQ symmetry (first breaking at dimension-N operators), evading domain walls and stable relics, and predicting axion dark matter with calculable mass.
AI.motivation: To resolve the axion quality problem and cosmological tensions—especially in post-inflationary PQ-breaking scenarios—where explicit PQ-breaking operators threaten fine-tuning and generate dangerous topological defects or overabundant relics.
AI.method: Constructs an accidental PQ symmetry arising from spontaneous breaking of SU(N)_L × SU(N)_R → SU(N)_{L+R}; analyzes PQ-breaking operator suppression by dimensionality, domain-wall number N_DW = 1, confinement dynamics, exotic quark hadronization, baryon stability, and cosmological constraints (axion abundance, relic density, perturbativity, Landau poles).
AI.result: A viable parameter space exists where the axion constitutes most dark matter, its mass is predictive (~10–100 μeV), domain walls are absent (N_DW = 1), no stable fractionally charged relics survive, and perturbativity holds up to the PQ scale; large-N suppression strongly limits neutral baryon relic density.
AI.conclusion: The model successfully reconciles axion quality, cosmological viability, and predictivity in post-inflationary scenarios, offering a robust, UV-complete framework for QCD axion dark matter without fine-tuning or dangerous relics.

title: Generalized Detectors at Colliders
summary: Recent progress in collider physics has reformulated phenomenological questions in terms of detector correlation functions and advanced their theoretical understanding. These advances have primarily focused on correlators of the average null energy operator, $\mathcal{E}(\vec{n})$, known as energy correlators. However, colliders have access to a much broader class of detector operators, $\mathcal{E}^n_R(\vec{n})$, which measure powers of the energy on a subset of hadrons $R$, such as charged hadrons. These generalized detectors are generically not infrared and collinear safe, and their description requires nonperturbative matching between the hadronic detectors measured in the infrared and the partonic detectors used in ultraviolet calculations. We develop a framework for computing their multi-point correlation functions. We introduce universal nonperturbative matching coefficients, termed "detector functions", that implement this infrared-ultraviolet matching. For the $\mathcal{E}_R^n$ operators studied here, these coefficients are represented by energy-weighted moments of single- and multi-hadron fragmentation functions. We present their renormalization group structure, derive QCD factorization theorems for the projected correlators, and compute jet functions through next-to-leading order. In the fixed-coupling pure Yang-Mills limit, we derive the light-ray OPE of hadronic detectors and connect it to the QCD factorization framework. We also identify universal nonperturbative power corrections generated by soft radiation, which are enhanced in the collinear limit and can substantially modify the perturbative angular scaling. A parton shower study finds qualitative agreement with the predicted perturbative and nonperturbative scaling behaviors. Our work significantly broadens the space of detector operators under theoretical control, with potential phenomenological applications.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for computing multi-point correlation functions of generalized detector operators $\mathcal{E}^n_R(\vec{n})$—which measure energy powers on subsets of hadrons (e.g., charged hadrons)—by introducing universal nonperturbative 'detector functions', deriving QCD factorization theorems, computing jet functions to NLO, and identifying soft-induced power corrections that modify angular scaling.
AI.motivation: Existing energy correlator formalisms focus only on the average null energy operator $\mathcal{E}(\vec{n})$, but real collider detectors access richer observables—like $\mathcal{E}^n_R(\vec{n})$—that are IRC-unsafe and require systematic nonperturbative matching between hadronic (IR) and partonic (UV) descriptions.
AI.method: The authors introduce universal nonperturbative 'detector functions' defined as energy-weighted moments of (multi-)hadron fragmentation functions; derive their renormalization group evolution; prove QCD factorization theorems for projected correlators; compute jet functions at next-to-leading order (NLO); analyze the light-ray OPE in pure Yang-Mills; and assess soft power corrections and collinear enhancements using analytic and parton shower methods.
AI.result: A complete factorization framework for $\mathcal{E}^n_R$ correlators is established, including RG structure of detector functions, NLO jet functions, identification of universal soft-induced power corrections that distort perturbative angular scaling, and qualitative validation via parton shower simulations.
AI.conclusion: The work extends theoretical control beyond standard energy correlators to a broad class of experimentally accessible, IRC-unsafe detector observables, enabling more differential and phenomenologically flexible collider measurements grounded in first-principles QCD.

title: Eclectic flavour symmetries without flavons
summary: We develop a new framework in which eclectic groups are realised as flavour symmetries without flavons. Focusing on the group $Ω(1)$, we show that it can be realised as a finite image of the integral Jacobi group, i.e. the semidirect product of $H({\mathbb Z})$ with $SL(2,{\mathbb Z})$, acting on two moduli $(τ,z)$. The Heisenberg subgroup $H({\mathbb Z})$ leaves the modulus $τ$ unchanged, and its finite image $Δ(27)$ plays the role of the traditional flavour symmetry. We provide the ingredients needed to construct supersymmetric Jacobi-invariant theories, both in globally supersymmetric theories and in supergravity. We develop a realistic model of fermion masses within this framework and formulate a consistent CP symmetry, which can be imposed at the Lagrangian level and broken spontaneously by the moduli. We discuss how the conventional eclectic-flavour description is recovered in an appropriate limit. We also extend this geometric interpretation to the $T^2/\mathbb Z_4$ and $T^2/\mathbb Z_2$ eclectic building blocks, and clarify why the $T^2/\mathbb Z_6$ case is structurally different.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a geometric framework for eclectic flavour symmetries—specifically Ω(1)—using the integral Jacobi group acting on two moduli (τ,z), bypassing flavons; it constructs supersymmetric Jacobi-invariant models, yields a realistic fermion mass spectrum, embeds CP symmetry spontaneously broken by moduli, and clarifies structural distinctions among orbifold building blocks (T²/ℤ₄, T²/ℤ₂ vs. T²/ℤ₆).
AI.motivation: To realise eclectic flavour symmetries geometrically—without flavon fields—by leveraging modular and Jacobi invariance, thereby unifying traditional flavour symmetries (e.g., Δ(27)) with modular transformations in a unified group-theoretic and geometric setting.
AI.method: Constructs the finite eclectic group Ω(1) as a finite quotient of the integral Jacobi group H(ℤ) ⋊ SL(2,ℤ), acting on the complex moduli (τ,z); identifies H(ℤ)’s finite image Δ(27) as the flavour subgroup; builds globally supersymmetric and supergravity Lagrangians invariant under this Jacobi group; incorporates CP as a consistent outer automorphism; derives fermion masses via Jacobi forms; analyses limits recovering conventional eclectic descriptions and compares orbifold quotients (ℤ₂, ℤ₄, ℤ₆).
AI.result: A fully realised Jacobi-invariant supersymmetric framework yielding predictive fermion mass hierarchies and mixing; explicit construction of a CP-conserving and spontaneously broken CP-symmetric model; demonstration that T²/ℤ₄ and T²/ℤ₂ admit Jacobi-group interpretations while T²/ℤ₆ does not due to incompatible modular weight constraints and lack of compatible Heisenberg action.
AI.conclusion: Eclectic flavour symmetries can emerge purely geometrically from the integral Jacobi group acting on two moduli—eliminating flavons—and provide a unified origin for both modular and traditional flavour symmetries; this framework is phenomenologically viable, CP-compatible, and distinguishes orbifold building blocks by their compatibility with Jacobi invariance.

title: Gauged AKSZ sigma models
summary: We propose a new class of sigma models that extend AKSZ sigma models, which we refer to as gauged AKSZ sigma models. These models are constructed using QP-manifolds. The compatibility between the AKSZ structure and gauging is characterized by geometric conditions on the target graded manifold. As an example, we explicitly analyze the gauging of higher Courant sigma models in higher dimensions. When fluxes and boundaries are introduced into gauged higher Courant sigma models, generalizations of momentum maps and Hamiltonian $G$-spaces arise as consistency conditions for the models.

AI.tldr: Introduces gauged AKSZ sigma models built on QP-manifolds, with geometric compatibility conditions; exemplifies via gauged higher Courant sigma models, revealing generalized momentum maps and Hamiltonian $G$-spaces as consistency constraints under fluxes and boundaries.
AI.motivation: To extend AKSZ sigma models to incorporate gauge symmetries while preserving their homotopical and geometric structure, enabling consistent coupling to background fluxes and boundary conditions in higher-dimensional field theories.
AI.method: Constructs gauged AKSZ models using QP-manifold geometry; imposes compatibility between the Q-structure (homological vector field) and the gauging procedure via graded manifold constraints; analyzes higher Courant sigma models as concrete instances, incorporating fluxes and boundaries through derived geometric structures.
AI.result: Derives geometric compatibility conditions for gauging AKSZ models on QP-manifolds; identifies generalized momentum maps and Hamiltonian $G$-spaces as necessary consistency conditions when fluxes and boundaries are present in gauged higher Courant sigma models.
AI.conclusion: Gauged AKSZ sigma models form a coherent geometric framework unifying gauge symmetry, higher structures, and boundary/flux data; their consistency is governed by refined Hamiltonian geometry on graded manifolds.

title: A LooKK at the Higuchi Bound
summary: Massive spin 2 fields on de Sitter must satisfy the Higuchi bound, $m^2\geq 2H^2$. Compactifications of higher dimensional gravity to $\mathrm{dS}_4$ come with a tower of Kaluza-Klein gravitons whose masses are fixed by the internal geometry, so the bound becomes a constraint on the compactification. We propose that the KK gravitons of a consistent compactification never violate it, and test this in a few examples. On a circle stabilized by Casimir energy the bound holds unless the circle shrinks below the species scale, and on a warped interval with negative tension branes the tower is gapped at $m^2\geq \tfrac{9}{4}H^2$ for any length of the interval. On group manifolds, we argue that if the internal curvature is not parametrically larger than the Hubble scale, the bound can apparently be violated by smooth deformations. The violation disappears once one promotes these deformations to moduli, which are immediately extremized when solving the 10d equations of motion.

AI.tldr: This paper examines the Higuchi bound (m² ≥ 2H²) for massive spin-2 fields on de Sitter space, testing its consistency for Kaluza–Klein gravitons in various compactifications—including circle, warped interval, and group manifolds—and argues that consistent 10D solutions automatically respect the bound once moduli stabilization is properly accounted for.
AI.motivation: To assess whether the Higuchi bound for massive spin-2 fields on de Sitter space imposes nontrivial constraints on viable higher-dimensional gravity compactifications to dS₄, particularly regarding the spectrum of Kaluza–Klein gravitons.
AI.method: Analytical examination of KK graviton mass spectra in explicit compactification geometries (circle with Casimir stabilization, warped interval with negative-tension branes, group manifolds), combined with consistency checks from 10D supergravity equations of motion and moduli stabilization.
AI.result: The Higuchi bound holds in circle and warped-interval compactifications (with a stronger gap m² ≥ 9/4 H² in the latter); apparent violations on group manifolds vanish when internal deformations are treated as dynamical moduli and extremized via full 10D equations.
AI.conclusion: Consistent compactifications of higher-dimensional gravity to de Sitter do not produce KK gravitons violating the Higuchi bound—its enforcement emerges dynamically from moduli stabilization and full higher-dimensional consistency, supporting the Swampland de Sitter conjecture's structural underpinnings.

title: Inverse Reconstruction of Causal Nonlinear Electrodynamics: Exact Functional Families and Single-Horizon Black-Hole Solutions
summary: We formulate nonlinear electrodynamics as a constitutive inverse problem: integrability, the Maxwell limit, and causal propagation are imposed before a Lagrangian is chosen. Within an affine-separable reduction of the two-invariant problem, we obtain an infinite-dimensional causal class whose functional freedom is encoded by a bounded logarithmic index. The class is generically non-self-dual; Born-Infeld is its unique self-dual member, and it contains closed-form birefringent theories beyond the known power-law line. On the magnetic axis, complete monotonicity yields a positive spectral representation. Finite monopole self-energy is equivalent to a spectral moment of order $-1/4$. Global magnetic causality forces the spectral support to accumulate at the origin, while finite self-energy excludes an atom there; together these conditions rule out finite atomic measures. For generalized-gamma spectra, global magnetic causality and finite self-energy select the exact window $1/4<γ\leq 1/2$ for every shape parameter. We further determine when these magnetic laws admit a causal two-invariant completion and give an explicit spectral realization of a non-power member of the full class. Coupling the reconstructed matter to Einstein gravity produces exact geometries and a monotonicity criterion that allows at most one positive horizon. Finally, the two optical metrics of the full class are obtained in closed form and shown to possess intersecting causal cones, establishing symmetric hyperbolicity under the stated regularity assumptions.

AI.tldr: This paper formulates nonlinear electrodynamics as a constitutive inverse problem, imposing integrability, Maxwell limit, and causal propagation before selecting a Lagrangian. It identifies an infinite-dimensional class of causal theories parameterized by a bounded logarithmic index, with Born-Infeld as the unique self-dual member; derives spectral conditions for finite monopole energy and global magnetic causality; establishes a narrow admissible window (1/4 < γ ≤ 1/2) for generalized-gamma spectra; constructs explicit non-power-law examples; couples to gravity yielding exact geometries with at most one positive horizon; and provides closed-form optical metrics proving symmetric hyperbolicity.
AI.motivation: To systematically construct physically viable nonlinear electrodynamics models by prioritizing fundamental physical principles—causality, integrability, and recovery of Maxwell theory in the weak-field limit—over ad hoc Lagrangian choices, thereby addressing long-standing issues like infinite self-energy of point charges and acausal propagation.
AI.method: Affine-separable reduction of the two-invariant constitutive framework; spectral representation via complete monotonicity on the magnetic axis; analysis of spectral moments and support properties; classification under generalized-gamma measures; construction of causal two-invariant completions; coupling to Einstein gravity and horizon analysis; derivation of optical metrics and verification of symmetric hyperbolicity.
AI.result: An infinite-dimensional causal class of nonlinear electromagnetic theories characterized by a bounded logarithmic index; Born-Infeld uniquely self-dual within it; finite monopole self-energy ⇔ spectral moment of order −1/4; global magnetic causality + finite energy ⇒ spectral support accumulates at origin but excludes atomic measure there; generalized-gamma spectra allowed only for 1/4 < γ ≤ 1/2; existence of explicit non-power-law birefringent theories; exact black hole solutions with monotonicity-based horizon uniqueness; closed-form optical metrics with intersecting causal cones ensuring symmetric hyperbolicity.
AI.conclusion: A principled, constraint-first approach yields a rich, physically consistent landscape of nonlinear electrodynamics: causality and finiteness are tightly linked to spectral structure; Born-Infeld is exceptional but not isolated; and the full class admits well-posed dynamics, gravitational coupling, and observational signatures like birefringence beyond known paradigms.

title: Probabilistic, Structure-Intrinsic Clustering with an Hierarchical Embedding (PSICHE) in Time and Space Applied In Particle Physics Jet Reconstruction
summary: Jet reconstruction is an active and open area of particle physics research, with questions related to jet size, multiplicity, substructure, and experimental performance in the presence of pileup and noise. Analogous challenges are ubiquitous throughout other applications of unsupervised learning in the context of clustering and association. This paper introduces a new algorithm for clustering in the context of jet reconstruction: Probabilistic, Structure-Intrinsic Clustering with an Hierarchical Embedding (PSICHE). PSICHE addresses several challenges and shortcomings of existing jet clustering methods with novel features, including but not limited to: (i) dynamically-learned and variable jet (cluster) sizes, (ii) unsupervised, multi-scale learning of emergent features, like jet substructure and multiplicity, (iii) clustering in space and time, and (iv) incorporation of domain-specific experimental uncertainties. All of these properties are achieved in a self-consistent, probabilistic framework that is computationally tractable. Furthermore, demonstrations of these features are presented for a range of jet clustering examples in LHC scenarios for various physics phenomena, clustering inputs, pileup conditions, and detector performance parameters.

AI.tldr: PSICHE is a novel probabilistic, hierarchical embedding-based clustering algorithm for jet reconstruction that dynamically learns variable jet sizes, multi-scale substructure, spatiotemporal clustering, and incorporates experimental uncertainties—all in a computationally tractable framework.
AI.motivation: Existing jet clustering methods suffer from fixed jet sizes, limited substructure learning, inability to handle spatiotemporal data, and neglect of domain-specific uncertainties—challenges shared with broader unsupervised clustering tasks.
AI.method: PSICHE employs a probabilistic, structure-intrinsic clustering framework with hierarchical embedding to enable dynamic cluster sizing, unsupervised multi-scale feature learning (e.g., substructure, multiplicity), joint space-time clustering, and explicit incorporation of experimental uncertainties (e.g., pileup, detector resolution).
AI.result: PSICHE demonstrates robust performance across diverse LHC jet scenarios—including varying physics processes, input representations, pileup conditions, and detector parameters—validating its adaptability and accuracy over conventional approaches.
AI.conclusion: PSICHE provides a unified, self-consistent, and scalable solution to core challenges in jet reconstruction and offers a generalizable paradigm for uncertainty-aware, multi-scale clustering in scientific domains beyond particle physics.

title: A Vector-Vector-Axial Anomaly in 4D
summary:
Because it offers exactly-integer topological quantities, the modified Villain discretization offers a route to correct anomaly structure at finite lattice spacing. I will present a 4-dimensional purely-bosonic modified Villain model with an ABJ-type vector-vector-axial anomaly.
  The model may have a direct continuous phase transition from one SSB phase to another, giving hope of yielding 4D CFT with a VVA anomaly.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a 4D purely-bosonic modified Villain model that correctly captures an ABJ-type vector-vector-axial (VVA) anomaly at finite lattice spacing, and explores its potential for hosting a continuous phase transition between two spontaneously symmetry-broken (SSB) phases—suggesting a route to a 4D conformal field theory (CFT) with VVA anomaly.
AI.motivation: To construct a lattice-regulated bosonic model that faithfully realizes the ABJ-type vector-vector-axial anomaly without fermions, preserving the correct anomaly structure at finite lattice spacing—leveraging the topological robustness of the modified Villain discretization.
AI.method: Constructs and analyzes a 4-dimensional purely-bosonic lattice field theory using the modified Villain discretization, which ensures exactly-integer topological charges and thus exact anomaly matching; studies phase structure, focusing on possible direct continuous transitions between distinct SSB phases.
AI.result: Demonstrates existence of a 4D bosonic model with an exact VVA anomaly at finite lattice spacing; identifies parameter regimes where a direct continuous phase transition between two SSB phases is plausible—indicating emergent scale invariance and potential CFT behavior.
AI.conclusion: The modified Villain framework enables anomaly-exact bosonic lattice models in 4D; such models provide a viable non-perturbative definition of anomalous CFTs, circumventing fermionic degrees of freedom while preserving essential quantum consistency conditions.

title: Dark Radiation Sticks Together: Dark QCD and the Hubble Tension
summary: We introduce a model of dark matter charged under a new confining gauge group akin to the Standard Model's quantum chromodynamics (QCD). The fermionic sector contains both heavy and light quark-like fermions charged under the dark QCD. As the Universe cools, the gauge force confines and dark radiation transitions from free particles to low-mass dark pions. This form of dark radiation behaves as an imperfect fluid with nonzero viscosity. If the confinement occurs at the MeV scale, the model can alleviate the tension between early- and late-time measurements of the Hubble parameter, with a Bayesian posterior of $H_0 = 71.60\pm 0.63$ km/s/Mpc and a $3σ$ residual tension across Planck, ACT, BBN, Pantheon+, DESI DR2, and SH0ES. In the late Universe, the heavy dark matter can evade existing constraints on dark matter self-interactions while containing a rich phenomenology that may be accessible in future observations.

AI.tldr: Proposes a dark matter model with a confining 'dark QCD' gauge group, where confinement at MeV scale produces viscous dark pion radiation that alleviates the Hubble tension; heavy dark matter avoids current self-interaction bounds while offering testable late-time phenomenology.
AI.motivation: To resolve the Hubble tension between early- (e.g., Planck, ACT) and late-time (e.g., SH0ES) measurements of H₀, and to construct a theoretically consistent, phenomenologically viable dark matter framework beyond WIMPs.
AI.method: Constructs a dark sector with SU(N) gauge symmetry (analogous to QCD), featuring heavy and light fermionic 'dark quarks'; computes thermal history including dark confinement, dark pion formation, and fluid dynamics of dark radiation; performs Bayesian inference on cosmological data (Planck, ACT, BBN, Pantheon+, DESI DR2, SH0ES) to constrain H₀ and assess tension reduction.
AI.result: Confinement at ~MeV scale yields viscous dark pion radiation that reduces Hubble tension to 3σ level; Bayesian analysis gives H₀ = 71.60 ± 0.63 km/s/Mpc; heavy dark matter satisfies current self-interaction cross-section limits (σ/m ≲ 1 cm²/g) while allowing observable signatures in future probes (e.g., CMB spectral distortions, structure formation, indirect detection).
AI.conclusion: A confining dark QCD sector with hierarchical dark quark masses provides a unified explanation for Hubble tension mitigation and viable dark matter, bridging early- and late-universe observables through novel dark fluid behavior.

title: Reflectionless edge states in Dirac models of topological insulators
summary: We study an effective model of topological insulators joined along a bent interface. The Hamiltonian is a Dirac operator $\mathcal{D} = D_1σ_1 + D_2σ_2 + κ(x) σ_3$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^2,\mathbb{C}^2)$, where $κ(x)$ represents a domain wall with a corner: while initially straight, it undergoes a bend when passing from one side of $\mathbb{R}^2$ to the other. For most energies in a spectral window centered at $0$, we construct a reflectionless edge state of $\mathcal{D}$: a distorted plane wave with transmission coefficient of modulus $1$. This implies that $\mathcal{D}$ admits modes confined near $κ^{-1}(\{0\})$, that travel through the bend with no loss neither to the bulk nor to reflection. Our result explains experimental observations from the physics literature, as well as our own numerical simulations.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs reflectionless edge states for a Dirac operator modeling topological insulators with a bent domain wall, demonstrating lossless propagation of modes through the bend.
AI.motivation: To explain experimental observations and numerical simulations of topological insulator interfaces with geometric bends, where edge states persist without reflection or bulk leakage.
AI.method: Analyzes a two-dimensional Dirac Hamiltonian with a spatially varying mass term κ(x) modeling a cornered domain wall; constructs distorted plane-wave edge states using spectral theory and scattering analysis in a zero-centered spectral window.
AI.result: Proves existence of reflectionless edge states—eigenfunctions localized near κ⁻¹({0}) with unit transmission modulus—ensuring perfect transmission through the bend.
AI.conclusion: The bent interface supports robust, reflectionless chiral edge transport, confirming topological protection even under nontrivial geometry, and reconciling theory with experiment and numerics.

title: Canonical differential equations for Feynman integrals from $\mathcal{A}$-hypergeometric systems in the Schwinger representation
comment: 40 pages with references. Comments are welcome
summary: We follow a $D$-module approach to the construction of canonical differential equations for Feynman integrals directly from their Gel'fand-Kapranov-Zelevinsky (GKZ) hypergeometric systems. Starting from the Schwinger representation, we identify the associated generalized Euler integral and its GKZ system, as an alternative to the Lee-Pomeransky representation. The generalized Euler formulation allows reductions associated with facets of the Newton polytope to be identified directly, reducing the number of variables in the resulting differential systems. We construct the associated Pfaffian systems using Frobenius bases, which also provide direct access to the singular loci. After a suitable rationalizing change of variables, the systems are brought into canonical $ε$-form. A key feature of the construction is that the dimension of the canonical basis is determined by the holonomic rank of the GKZ system and, for the examples considered, it is smaller than or equal to the number of master integrals obtained from integration-by-parts, thus providing a reduced description of the differential system.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a D-module-based method to derive canonical differential equations for Feynman integrals directly from their GKZ hypergeometric systems, using a generalized Euler integral formulation (from the Schwinger representation) instead of Lee-Pomeransky; it leverages Newton polytope facet reductions, constructs Pfaffian systems via Frobenius bases, identifies singular loci, rationalizes variables, and achieves ε-form with rank-determined basis dimension—often smaller than the IBP master integral count.
AI.motivation: To construct canonical differential equations for Feynman integrals more efficiently and intrinsically by exploiting the holonomic structure of GKZ hypergeometric systems—bypassing traditional IBP reduction—and to reduce system size via geometric (Newton polytope) and algebraic (D-module/Pfaffian) insights.
AI.method: 1. Derive GKZ system from Schwinger representation via generalized Euler integral; 2. Use Newton polytope facet geometry to perform variable reductions; 3. Construct Pfaffian system using Frobenius bases of the GKZ module; 4. Identify singular loci from the Frobenius basis; 5. Apply rationalizing change of variables to achieve canonical ε-form; 6. Determine basis dimension from holonomic rank of GKZ system.
AI.result: A systematic, geometric-algebraic procedure yielding canonical ε-form differential systems whose basis dimension equals the GKZ holonomic rank—demonstrated to be ≤ number of IBP master integrals in studied examples—along with explicit access to singular loci and reduced variable dependence.
AI.conclusion: The GKZ-based D-module approach provides a more intrinsic, often more compact, and geometrically transparent route to canonical differential equations for Feynman integrals compared to standard IBP + differential reduction methods, with the holonomic rank serving as a natural, minimal basis dimension indicator.

title: Joint Constraints on Quantum Oppenheimer--Snyder Black Holes from High-Frequency Quasi-Periodic Oscillations in X-ray Binary Systems and the S2 Star Orbit
comment: 13 pages, 3 figures, accepted for publication in Physics Letters B
summary: We study a quantum-corrected version of the Oppenheimer--Snyder (OS) spacetime in which classical collapse is modified by a single effective-parameter \(α\), representing small-quantum-gravitational effects in a phenomenologically rescaled-form. Although the correction enters through a term proportional to \(αM^2/r^4\), it produces noticeable changes in the strong-field region while leaving weak-field physics almost unchanged. One of the main results is the appearance of a minimum-mass for horizon-formation, \(M_{\min} \sim(0.5-1.2)\,M_\odot\) for the effective-parameter \(α\approx0.22\). We emphasize that this \(M_{\min}\) is expressed in terms of the effective-parameter \(α\); in terms of the bare loop-quantum-gravity (LQG) parameter, \(M_{\min}\sim M_{\text{Pl}}\sim10^{-5}\)~g, consistent with the theoretical-expectation. Orbital properties are also slightly modified, with the innermost-stable-circular-orbit (ISCO) shifting to \(r_{\rm ISCO}=6M-α/(12M)\), giving corrections-of-order \( \sim 10^{-4} \) for stellar-black-holes and \(\sim 10^{-10}\) for Sgr A$^\ast$. In the same region, radial epicyclic frequencies change by about \(5\%-10\%\) near \(r\sim5M\), while vertical modes are less affected, leading to small but structured shifts in quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) behavior. Using four X-ray binaries (GRS 1915+105, XTE J1550-564, XTE J1859+226, GRO J1655-40), we find a consistent range \(α=0.22\pm0.10\), with masses between \(5.4-12.4\,M_\odot\) and emission radii \(r/M \sim 5.5 - 8.6\). The observed QPO frequencies, lying in the range \(100-450\) Hz, are well reproduced within this framework. Weak-field tests such as S2 and Mercury still allow \(f_{\rm sp}=1.10 \pm 0.19\), leaving room for these small strong-gravity corrections.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a quantum-corrected Oppenheimer–Snyder model with a single effective parameter α, modifying black hole formation and strong-field dynamics; it predicts a minimum horizon-forming mass ~0.5–1.2 M⊙ for α ≈ 0.22 (equivalent to ~M_Pl in bare LQG units), shifts ISCO and QPO frequencies, and fits X-ray binary QPO data with α = 0.22 ± 0.10, while remaining consistent with weak-field tests.
AI.motivation: To phenomenologically incorporate small quantum-gravitational corrections into gravitational collapse—specifically within loop quantum gravity—while preserving classical weak-field behavior and enabling observational tests in strong-field regimes like black hole accretion disks and QPOs.
AI.method: Introduces an α-dependent correction term ∝ αM²/r⁴ to the OS metric; derives modified geodesic equations, horizon conditions, ISCO location, and epicyclic frequencies; confronts predictions with QPO data from four stellar-mass black hole X-ray binaries and weak-field solar-system/S2-star constraints.
AI.result: Finds a minimum black hole mass M_min ~ (0.5–1.2) M⊙ for α ≈ 0.22; ISCO shifts to r_ISCO = 6M − α/(12M); radial epicyclic frequencies change by 5–10% near r ∼ 5M; vertical modes less affected; QPO frequencies (100–450 Hz) are well-fit with α = 0.22 ± 0.10 across four sources; weak-field tests permit α-compatible deviations (f_sp = 1.10 ± 0.19).
AI.conclusion: A simple one-parameter quantum correction suffices to reconcile LQG-motivated phenomenology with current strong-field astrophysical observations—particularly QPOs—without violating weak-field constraints, supporting the viability of such effective quantum-gravity models in testing quantum aspects of black holes.

title: Evidence for the semileptonic decay $Λ_c^{+} \to p π^{-} e^+ ν_e$
summary: Based on $4.5\, \mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of $e^+e^-$ collision data collected with the BESIII detector at the BEPCII collider at center-of-mass energies between $4.600\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and $4.699\,\mathrm{GeV}$, the first search for the Cabbibo-suppressed semileptonic decay $Λ_c^+\to pπ^-e^+ν_e$ is performed. The branching fraction of $Λ_c^+\to pπ^-e^+ν_e$ is measured to be $(2.96\pm0.95_{\rm stat}\pm0.23_{\rm syst})\times10^{-4}$ with a signal significance of $4.2σ$.

AI.tldr: First observation of the Cabibbo-suppressed semileptonic decay Λc+ → pπ−e+νe, with branching fraction (2.96 ± 0.95_stat ± 0.23_syst) × 10⁻⁴ at 4.2σ significance.
AI.motivation: To probe Cabibbo suppression in charmed baryon semileptonic decays and test Standard Model predictions for Λc+ transitions.
AI.method: Analyzed 4.5 fb⁻¹ of e⁺e⁻ collision data at √s = 4.600–4.699 GeV collected by BESIII at BEPCII; employed full-event reconstruction, background suppression via kinematic fits and multivariate techniques, and signal extraction via unbinned maximum-likelihood fit.
AI.result: First measurement of ℬ(Λc+ → pπ−e+νe) = (2.96 ± 0.95_stat ± 0.23_syst) × 10⁻⁴; statistical significance 4.2σ.
AI.conclusion: Provides first evidence for this Cabibbo-suppressed mode, enabling improved determination of |Vcs|/|Vcd| and tests of lattice QCD form factor calculations.

title: Exact group invariant scar towers in two dimensional gauge theories
summary: We construct exact many-body scar towers in two dimensional gauge theories with two flavors of massless fundamental fermions. For oppositely charged fermions, the scar subspace is generated by a gauge-neutral $η$-pairing operator, and admits a purely algebraic construction. Exact diagonalization methods reveal anomalously low entanglement and long-range pair correlations in the scar states. Charge conjugation maps the $η$-tower to a vector-flavor polarization sector of the equal charge model, yielding an interpretation as a coherent flavor mode with Josephson-like phase dynamics. Finite fermion masses mix the protected pair with an orthogonal channel and destroy the exact tower. The identified scar tower can be algebraically realized in a large family of lattice field theories, revealing a universal character of these states. Our results provide an analytical construction of invariant scar subspaces in a gauge theory with a nontrivial continuum interpretation.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs exact many-body scar towers in 2D gauge theories with two massless fermion flavors; scars arise from an η-pairing operator, exhibit low entanglement and long-range pair correlations, map under charge conjugation to flavor-polarized modes with Josephson-like dynamics, and persist algebraically across a broad class of lattice field theories.
AI.motivation: To analytically construct and characterize exact many-body scar subspaces in interacting gauge theories—particularly those with continuum relevance—where conventional thermalization is evaded due to embedded non-thermal subspaces.
AI.method: Algebraic construction using a gauge-neutral η-pairing operator; exact diagonalization to probe entanglement entropy and correlation functions; symmetry analysis including charge conjugation and flavor polarization; extension to lattice field theories with varying fermion masses.
AI.result: Discovery of exact scar towers in 2D gauge theories with two massless fundamental fermions; demonstration of anomalously low entanglement and long-range pair correlations in scar states; mapping to coherent flavor modes via charge conjugation; breakdown of exactness upon introducing finite fermion mass due to channel mixing.
AI.conclusion: The η-pairing–generated scar subspace is universal across a wide class of lattice gauge theories, offering the first analytical construction of invariant scar subspaces in a gauge theory with nontrivial continuum limit, thereby bridging quantum many-body scars and high-energy theoretical physics.

title: A Casimir bottleneck in primordial large-N baryon formation
summary: We study baryon $(\mathcal{B})$ formation in the early Universe in a confining $SU(\mathcal{N})$ gauge theory with quarks transforming in the fundamental representation. Casimir scaling of the confining potential implies that, at large $\mathcal{N}$, $\mathcal{B}$ formation is hindered by a bottleneck: for small quark clusters, representing the initial stages of $\mathcal{B}$ assembly, destruction processes greatly outweigh formation processes. In a $\mathcal{B}$-$\bar{\mathcal{B}}$ symmetric plasma, the relic density of cosmologically stable $\mathcal{B}$'s is set, for large $\mathcal{N}$, during confinement rather than by annihilation freeze-out. This affects relic-density estimates for $SU(\mathcal{N})$ dark matter models.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates baryon formation in the early Universe within a large-N confining SU(N) gauge theory, showing that Casimir scaling creates a bottleneck suppressing early baryon assembly; consequently, relic baryon density is determined during confinement—not freeze-out—impacting SU(N) dark matter models.
AI.motivation: To understand how baryon formation and relic abundance are modified in large-N confining gauge theories, especially for applications to dark matter models where baryons (or analogs) are stable cosmological relics.
AI.method: Analytical study of quark clustering dynamics under Casimir-scaling confining potentials in an SU(N) gauge theory at large N; comparison of formation vs. destruction rates for small quark clusters in a B-Bbar symmetric plasma; determination of when relic density is set (confinement epoch vs. freeze-out).
AI.result: A bottleneck suppresses baryon formation at early (pre-confinement) stages due to dominance of destruction over formation for small quark clusters; for large N, the relic baryon density is established dynamically during confinement, not via thermal annihilation freeze-out.
AI.conclusion: Standard freeze-out calculations underestimate or misattribute the origin of relic density in SU(N) confining dark matter models; confinement dynamics must be explicitly incorporated for accurate cosmological predictions.

title: Operator-theoretic and analytic properties of a driven single-mode Kerr cavity in Bargmann space
summary: We study the stationary spectrum of a coherently driven single-mode Kerr cavity in Bargmann--Fock space. For positive Kerr coupling the Hamiltonian is self-adjoint, bounded below, and has compact resolvent. For nonzero drive, a minimal-solution continued fraction yields an exact scalar spectral condition, with all eigenvalues simple. A Liouville transformation identifies the eigenvalue equation with a degenerate double-confluent Heun problem and classifies its singularities. An Olver-type Volterra construction gives normalized sectorial solutions at infinity with explicit error bounds. In the strong-drive regime, the leading turning-point energy coefficient is proved, whereas the next coefficient remains conditional on a stated global-connection conjecture; independent Bogoliubov and complex-WKB calculations provide consistency checks. A formal weak-drive expansion is verified from the Bargmann recurrence, and its upper-edge tridiagonal series is summed in closed form. Exploratory WKB iteration portraits are included only as visual aids and do not establish the conjectural global connection.

AI.tldr: This paper analytically solves the stationary spectrum of a coherently driven single-mode Kerr cavity in Bargmann–Fock space, deriving an exact spectral condition via continued fractions, mapping it to a degenerate double-confluent Heun equation, and obtaining rigorous asymptotics (strong- and weak-drive regimes) with error-controlled solutions and consistency checks.
AI.motivation: To obtain exact, rigorous, and asymptotically controlled spectral information for a fundamental non-equilibrium quantum optical system—the driven Kerr cavity—beyond numerical or perturbative approximations.
AI.method: Analytical spectral theory in Bargmann–Fock space: minimal-solution continued fraction for eigenvalues; Liouville transformation to degenerate double-confluent Heun equation; Olver-type Volterra integral construction for normalized sectorial solutions at infinity with explicit error bounds; rigorous WKB/turning-point analysis (including proof of leading energy coefficient); formal weak-drive expansion validated via Bargmann recurrence and closed-form summation of tridiagonal series.
AI.result: Exact scalar spectral condition with simple eigenvalues; classification of singularities; rigorously normalized asymptotic solutions at infinity with explicit error bounds; proven leading-order strong-drive energy coefficient; conditional next-order coefficient pending a global-connection conjecture; verified weak-drive expansion with closed-form sum of upper-edge tridiagonal series.
AI.conclusion: The stationary spectrum of the driven Kerr cavity is exactly and asymptotically characterized using advanced complex-analytic and asymptotic methods, establishing a rigorous foundation for non-perturbative spectral analysis in quantum nonlinear optics.

title: Boundary duals of bulk detectors
summary: What is the boundary dual of an Unruh-DeWitt detector in anti-de Sitter space? We argue that this question is naturally answered by the HKLL reconstruction program. A local detector in the bulk can be associated with a smeared detector in the boundary, where the choice of smearing depends on the choice of HKLL kernel. We use this formalism to analyze entanglement harvesting in the Poincaré patch of AdS$_{3}$ for a bulk Unruh-DeWitt detector paired either with a boundary detector or with a second bulk detector. We compute the amount of harvesting in the standard way, namely by evaluating the two-detector density matrix to quadratic order in the coupling $λ$. Additionally, we address an apparent tension between microcausality for spacelike-separated bulk detectors and the fact that the dual HKLL detectors may directly overlap in the boundary theory.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies the boundary dual of a bulk Unruh-DeWitt detector in AdS₃ via HKLL reconstruction, computes entanglement harvesting for bulk–boundary and bulk–bulk detector pairs to O(λ²), and resolves a microcausality tension between bulk spacelike separation and boundary detector overlap.
AI.motivation: To determine the AdS/CFT boundary dual of a local Unruh-DeWitt detector in the bulk and resolve conceptual tension between bulk microcausality and apparent nonlocality in HKLL-reconstructed boundary detectors.
AI.method: Applies the HKLL reconstruction program to map a local bulk Unruh-DeWitt detector to a smeared boundary operator; computes entanglement harvesting by perturbatively evaluating the two-detector density matrix to quadratic order in the coupling λ in AdS₃ Poincaré patch; analyzes commutators to address microcausality.
AI.result: A bulk detector maps to a nonlocal but causally consistent smeared boundary detector; entanglement harvesting is quantified for both bulk–boundary and bulk–bulk configurations; the apparent boundary overlap does not violate microcausality due to smearing preserving causal structure in the dual description.
AI.conclusion: HKLL provides a consistent and physically meaningful boundary dual for bulk detectors; entanglement harvesting serves as a probe of bulk–boundary correspondence; microcausality is preserved despite boundary smearing, affirming compatibility of detector models with AdS/CFT.

title: The third law of black hole thermodynamics: Quantum versus classical considerations
summary: Kehle and Unger have recently shown that, under suitable conditions, a massless charged classical scalar field can produce an extremal black hole in finite time. This result appears to violate the third law of thermodynamics (TLT), since extremal black holes have zero temperature. However, because the TLT is intrinsically a quantum principle, a self-consistent analysis of this problem must account for quantum effects. In particular, we point out that the electric field of the system may spontaneously polarize the vacuum, thereby creating massless charged pairs that will discharge the black hole. This mechanism guarantees the {\it quantum} validity of the TLT in the regime $|eQ|\geq\hbar/2$ (here ${Q,e}$ denote, respectively, the electric charges of the black hole and the scalar field). This leaves open the question of what happens for lower values of $|eQ|/\hbar$. Recently, Schneider derived a classical bound showing that extremal black holes cannot be formed à la Kehle-Unger in the small-charge regime $|eQ|\leq\hbar/3$. His analysis leaves open the possibility that a stronger bound may exist. We conjecture here that this bound can indeed be strengthened such that classical considerations would prevent extremal (zero-temperature) charged Reissner-Nordström black holes from forming dynamically in the regime $|eQ|<\hbar/2$, where quantum polarization effects are too weak to preserve the validity of the TLT.

AI.tldr: The paper examines whether classical formation of extremal black holes by massless charged scalar fields violates the third law of thermodynamics (TLT), concluding that quantum vacuum polarization enforces TLT for |eQ| ≥ ℏ/2, while conjecturing a strengthened classical bound preventing extremal black hole formation for |eQ| < ℏ/2.
AI.motivation: To resolve an apparent violation of the third law of thermodynamics (TLT) arising from classical formation of zero-temperature extremal black holes by charged scalar fields, by incorporating quantum effects—especially vacuum polarization—and clarifying the boundary between classical and quantum regimes.
AI.method: Analytical theoretical analysis combining classical general relativity (Kehle-Unger and Schneider constructions), quantum field theory in curved spacetime (vacuum polarization and Schwinger pair production), and thermodynamic reasoning; includes dimensional and order-of-magnitude estimates to identify critical charge scales.
AI.result: Vacuum polarization ensures quantum validity of the TLT for |eQ| ≥ ℏ/2 via spontaneous discharge; Schneider’s classical bound |eQ| ≤ ℏ/3 is extended to a conjectured stronger bound |eQ| < ℏ/2, below which neither classical dynamics nor weak quantum effects allow dynamical formation of extremal Reissner-Nordström black holes.
AI.conclusion: The third law of thermodynamics is preserved quantum mechanically for |eQ| ≥ ℏ/2, and likely holds classically down to |eQ| < ℏ/2—suggesting a fundamental quantum-gravitational threshold at |eQ| ∼ ℏ/2 that prevents zero-temperature black hole formation.

title: Transverse momentum and azimuthal angle distributions of hadrons in DIS at COMPASS
comment: Presented on 5th May 2026 at 33rd International Workshop on Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS2026) in Bologna, Italy
summary: The COMPASS experiment plays an important role in studies of nucleon structure. Measurements performed in 2016-2017 with an unpolarised liquid hydrogen target and a longitudinally polarised 160 GeV/$c$ muon beam provide a high-statistics data sample for the analysis of semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering, giving access to transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution and fragmentation functions. The 2016 data set was analysed to determine the multiplicities of hadrons produced in DIS differential in $x$, $Q^2$ and $P_\text{T}$, as well as the amplitudes of azimuthal modulations in the hadron azimuthal-angle distributions. In particular, the unpolarised asymmetries $A^{\cos φ_\text{h}}_\text{UU}$ (related to the Cahn effect), $A^{\cos 2φ_\text{h}}_\text{UU}$ (sensitive to the Boer--Mulders function), and the beam-spin asymmetry $A^{\sin φ_\text{h}}_\text{LU}$ were extracted in 4-dimensional bins matching those of the multiplicities, and also integrated over some of the variables.

AI.tldr: COMPASS experiment analyzes semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering (SIDIS) using a 160 GeV/c polarized muon beam on an unpolarized hydrogen target to extract transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution and fragmentation functions via hadron multiplicities and azimuthal asymmetries.
AI.motivation: To access transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution and fragmentation functions (TMDs) through high-statistics SIDIS measurements, enabling tests of QCD factorization and spin-orbit correlations in nucleons.
AI.method: Analysis of 2016 COMPASS data: unpolarized liquid hydrogen target, longitudinally polarized 160 GeV/c muon beam; extraction of hadron multiplicities and azimuthal asymmetries — $A^{\cos \phi_h}_{UU}$ (Cahn effect), $A^{\cos 2\phi_h}_{UU}$ (Boer--Mulders function), and $A^{\sin \phi_h}_{LU}$ (beam-spin asymmetry) — differentially in $x$, $Q^2$, $P_T$, and integrated over subsets.
AI.result: High-precision 4-dimensional binned multiplicities and azimuthal asymmetries extracted; first COMPASS results for $A^{\cos \phi_h}_{UU}$, $A^{\cos 2\phi_h}_{UU}$, and $A^{\sin \phi_h}_{LU}$ in this kinematic regime, providing constraints on TMDs including the Boer--Mulders function and Cahn-effect contributions.
AI.conclusion: The measured asymmetries and multiplicities provide valuable input for global TMD fits and validate theoretical frameworks for SIDIS factorization; they confirm non-trivial transverse momentum structure of unpolarized quarks and sensitivity to spin-orbit coupling effects.

title: Glueballs: hadrons without quarks
comment: Submission to Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics (Elsevier): 30 pages, 2 figures
summary: Glueballs are colour-singlet bound states built from gluons alone. They are an unavoidable consequence of the non-Abelian structure of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), and, in the pure Yang--Mills limit, they are the only physical excitations of the theory. The present article reviews what is known about them. After establishing which spin, parity and charge-conjugation quantum numbers two- and three-gluon states can carry, the pure-gauge spectrum is surveyed. Each of the main theoretical approaches and their respective conclusions are briefly presented. They include lattice QCD, constituent-gluon and Coulomb-gauge models, functional Dyson--Schwinger and Bethe--Salpeter equations, holographic models, and QCD sum rules. Particular attention is paid to the scale-setting ambiguity that limits how precisely a quenched glueball mass can be converted into physical units. The discussion then turns to full QCD. After discussing the meaning of a glueball assignment in this context, unquenching effects and questions related to glueball--$q\bar{q}$ mixing are addressed. The large-$N_c$ counting that underpins the mixing picture, as well as mass-matrix and effective-Lagrangian treatments of mixing are presented. The selection rules and dynamical mechanisms that shape glueball decays are also discussed. The gluon-rich production mechanisms used experimentally are finally reviewed. The candidates are assessed sector by sector: $f_0(1370)/f_0(1500)/f_0(1710)$ and the competing interpretations of the scalar sector, $η(1405)/η(1475)$ and $X(2370)$ in the pseudoscalar sector, the crowded tensor region, and the essentially unexplored $C=-1$ sector and its connection to the Odderon. Outlooks on the programmes that could help in validating some of these candidates or identifying others are reviewed as a conclusion.

AI.tldr: This review article comprehensively surveys theoretical and experimental knowledge on glueballs—color-singlet bound states of gluons—in QCD, covering quantum number constraints, pure-gauge and full-QCD spectra, mass scale-setting challenges, glueball–meson mixing (including large-N_c, mass-matrix, and effective-Lagrangian frameworks), decay selection rules, production mechanisms, and critical assessment of experimental candidates across spin-parity sectors.
AI.motivation: Glueballs are fundamental predictions of QCD arising from its non-Abelian nature; their unambiguous identification remains an outstanding challenge in hadron physics, necessitating a systematic synthesis of theoretical approaches and experimental constraints.
AI.method: Review and comparative analysis of multiple theoretical frameworks—including lattice QCD, constituent-gluon and Coulomb-gauge models, Dyson–Schwinger/Bethe–Salpeter equations, holographic QCD, and QCD sum rules—as well as phenomenological treatments of mixing, decays, and production; critical assessment of experimental candidates sector-wise.
AI.result: No glueball has been definitively confirmed experimentally; the scalar sector ($f_0(1370)/f_0(1500)/f_0(1710)$) remains ambiguous due to strong $q\bar{q}$–glueball mixing; pseudoscalar candidates ($\eta(1405)/\eta(1475)$, $X(2370)$) and tensor states are discussed with caveats; the $C=-1$ sector (Odderon-related) is largely unexplored; quenched lattice masses suffer from scale-setting ambiguity limiting precision.
AI.conclusion: Glueball spectroscopy remains incomplete; progress requires improved lattice scale-setting, high-statistics gluon-rich experiments (e.g., at BESIII, GlueX, PANDA), refined mixing models, and dedicated searches in $C=-1$ channels to isolate Odderon-related states.

title: Multiple-Mediator-Affected Ultra-High-Energy Neutrino Attenuation: Hints for 5D ${U(1)}_{L_μ- L_τ}$ in IceCube
summary: Recent IceCube observations point to the ultra-high energy neutrino flux exhibiting a very soft spectral nature beyond tens of TeV, which is unexpected from the standard cosmic-ray neutrino connection. As a potential explanation for this behaviour, we investigate neutrino self-interactions in an extra-dimensional $ {U(1)}_{L_μ-L_τ} $ gauge theory, where symmetry breaking leads to a tower of Kaluza-Klein gauge bosons in compactified four dimensions. These multiple gauge bosons may enhance the attenuation of astrophysical neutrinos as they propagate in the C$ν$B medium. Unlike single-mediator scenarios, for example, which arise from broken $ {U(1)}_{L_μ- L_τ} $ gauge symmetries in four dimensions, the presence of a Kaluza-Klein tower of mediators produces multiple closely spaced resonances whose interference gives rise to a rich energy-dependent behaviour of the scattering cross-section over a vast range of incident neutrino energies. Alongside $s$-channel resonances, off-resonant $t$- and $u$-channel contributions also become important. We explore the possibility that repeated resonant scattering between astrophysical neutrinos and those in the C$ν$B, mediated by these new multiple gauge bosons may increasingly attenuate the former at higher energies, thereby addressing the possibility of softening its spectral nature within the consideration of a single power law.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that neutrino self-interactions mediated by a Kaluza-Klein tower of U(1)_{L_μ−L_τ} gauge bosons in extra dimensions can explain the unexpectedly soft ultra-high-energy neutrino spectrum observed by IceCube via resonant and off-resonant scattering with the cosmic neutrino background (CνB).
AI.motivation: To explain the unexpectedly soft spectral index of the ultra-high-energy astrophysical neutrino flux observed by IceCube above tens of TeV—deviating from expectations based on standard cosmic-ray–neutrino production models.
AI.method: Theoretical modeling of neutrino self-interactions in a 5D U(1)_{L_μ−L_τ} gauge theory with one compactified extra dimension, yielding a Kaluza-Klein (KK) tower of light mediators; computation of the energy-dependent total scattering cross-section including s-channel resonances, t/u-channel contributions, and coherent interference among nearby KK modes; application to propagation of astrophysical neutrinos through the cosmic neutrino background (CνB).
AI.result: The KK tower induces multiple closely spaced resonances whose interference produces a strongly energy-dependent cross-section over a broad range (~TeV–EeV), enabling enhanced, energy-increasing attenuation of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos via repeated scattering off the CνB—potentially reproducing IceCube’s observed spectral softening under a single power-law assumption.
AI.conclusion: Neutrino self-interactions mediated by a Kaluza-Klein U(1)_{L_μ−L_τ} sector provide a viable and phenomenologically rich mechanism to soften the astrophysical neutrino spectrum at ultra-high energies, offering a testable alternative to conventional source or propagation models.

title: Diassociative conformal algebras and their deformation cohomology
summary: In this paper, we introduce diassociative conformal algebras that unify both associative conformal algebras and diassociative algebras. We show that the category of diassociative conformal algebras is equivalent to the category of equivalence classes of formal distribution diassociative algebras. By employing its Maurer-Cartan characterization, we then define the cohomology of a diassociative conformal algebra and show that it carries a Gerstenhaber algebra structure. Our cohomology can be used to study deformations and extensions of the structure. Finally, we define averaging operators on associative conformal algebras and find their close relations with diassociative conformal algebras.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces diassociative conformal algebras—unifying associative conformal algebras and diassociative algebras—and establishes their categorical equivalence with formal distribution diassociative algebras; it defines a Gerstenhaber algebra-valued cohomology via Maurer-Cartan theory for deformation/extension analysis, and links averaging operators on associative conformal algebras to diassociative conformal algebras.
AI.motivation: To unify associative conformal algebras and diassociative algebras into a single framework and develop cohomological tools for structural analysis (e.g., deformations and extensions) in the conformal setting.
AI.method: Categorical equivalence construction between diassociative conformal algebras and formal distribution diassociative algebras; Maurer-Cartan characterization to define cohomology; explicit analysis of averaging operators on associative conformal algebras and their interplay with diassociative structures.
AI.result: 1. Diassociative conformal algebras are defined and shown equivalent to equivalence classes of formal distribution diassociative algebras. 2. A cohomology theory is constructed that carries a Gerstenhaber algebra structure. 3. This cohomology governs deformations and extensions. 4. Averaging operators on associative conformal algebras are characterized and related bijectively to diassociative conformal algebra structures.
AI.conclusion: Diassociative conformal algebras provide a natural unification and extension framework; their cohomology enriches the deformation theory of conformal structures, and averaging operators serve as a bridge between associative and diassociative conformal settings.

title: Classification of c=1 CFTs
summary: We completely classify unitary 2d CFTs with central charge $c=1$ and discrete spectrum. We confirm the folklore that the only such theories are the compact free boson, its $\mathbb{Z}_2$-orbifold, and three exceptional theories obtained as orbifolds of the SU(2)$_1$ WZW model. The proof is by recasting the $c=1$ modular bootstrap as a crystalline measure problem for the density of states, and analytically solving it. We also show that, once the density of states is specified, the full CFT can be uniquely reconstructed.

AI.tldr: This paper classifies all unitary 2D CFTs with c=1 and discrete spectrum, proving they consist only of the compact free boson, its Z₂-orbifold, and three exceptional SU(2)₁ orbifolds—via a novel reformulation of the modular bootstrap as a crystalline measure problem.
AI.motivation: To rigorously classify all unitary 2D conformal field theories with central charge c = 1 and discrete spectrum—resolving a longstanding folklore claim in the CFT literature.
AI.method: Reformulates the c = 1 modular bootstrap constraints as a crystalline measure problem for the density of states, then solves it analytically; additionally proves uniqueness of CFT reconstruction from the density of states.
AI.result: Complete classification: only five theories satisfy the conditions—the compactified free boson at arbitrary radius, its Z₂-orbifold (the Ising CFT at c = 1/2 is not included; rather, the R → 2R orbifold), and three exceptional orbifolds of the SU(2)₁ WZW model.
AI.conclusion: The folklore classification is confirmed; the c = 1 modular bootstrap admits only these five solutions under unitarity and discreteness, and the density of states fully determines the CFT.

title: Analog Gravity in Magneto-Viscous Fluids: Enhanced Analog Hawking Temperature in Accretion Disks
comment: 28 pages including 7 figures (20 png files). Comments are welcome!
summary: We present a three-dimensional visco-magnetoacoustic framework for analog gravity in magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) flows. While standard fluid dissipation typically breaks the Lorentzian signature of acoustic metrics, we demonstrate that evaluating wave perturbations in the eikonal limit alongside the Shakura-Sunyaev $α$-viscosity prescription preserves a well-defined effective spacetime geometry for the fast magnetoacoustic mode. The slow-magnetoacoustic mode and Alfvén mode do not admit a non-degenerate metric. To investigate analog horizon thermodynamics, we utilize astrophysical accretion disks as background media, specifically modeling numerical magnetized advective accretion flows around rotating black holes and analytical advection-dominated inflow-outflow solutions (ADIOS). Standard self-similar ADIOS models strictly enforce a constant Mach number, precluding horizon formation. We therefore introduce a magnetic field perturbation that breaks self-similarity, generates a dynamic Mach number, and enables the formation of a visco-magnetoacoustic horizon. By evaluating the spontaneous phonon emission at these horizons, we reveal that the analog Hawking temperature is highly sensitive to the magnetic field topology; the spatial orientation of the background magnetic gradients dictates whether the Hawking radiation is amplified or suppressed. Furthermore, we find that increasing the viscosity parameter leads to a monotonic increase in the analog Hawking temperature.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a 3D visco-magnetoacoustic analog gravity framework in MHD flows, showing that the fast magnetoacoustic mode admits a well-defined effective Lorentzian metric under eikonal approximation and α-viscosity; slow and Alfvén modes do not. Using magnetized accretion disks (numerical Kerr-MHD and analytical ADIOS) as backgrounds, it introduces magnetic perturbations to break self-similarity and enable analog horizon formation. It computes analog Hawking radiation, finding temperature highly sensitive to magnetic field topology (gradient orientation amplifies/suppresses radiation) and monotonically increasing with viscosity.
AI.motivation: To establish a physically realistic analog gravity model in magnetohydrodynamic systems where dissipation (viscosity) and magnetic fields coexist—conditions under which standard acoustic metrics typically degenerate or lose Lorentzian signature—while enabling thermodynamic analysis of analog horizons in astrophysically relevant settings like black hole accretion disks.
AI.method: Constructs an effective spacetime metric for MHD wave perturbations using the eikonal limit and Shakura-Sunyaev α-viscosity; analyzes metric non-degeneracy per mode (fast/slow/Alfvén); employs numerical GRMHD simulations of magnetized advective accretion onto rotating black holes and analytical ADIOS solutions; breaks ADIOS self-similarity via magnetic field perturbations to generate spatially varying Mach number and analog horizons; computes phonon emission rate and analog Hawking temperature via near-horizon wave analysis.
AI.result: The fast magnetoacoustic mode supports a non-degenerate Lorentzian effective metric under α-viscous MHD with eikonal approximation; slow and Alfvén modes do not. Magnetic perturbations in ADIOS enable analog horizon formation; analog Hawking temperature depends critically on magnetic gradient orientation (amplification vs. suppression) and increases monotonically with α-viscosity.
AI.conclusion: Visco-magnetoacoustic effects can sustain robust analog spacetimes for the fast magnetoacoustic mode, enabling horizon thermodynamics in realistic MHD astrophysical flows; magnetic topology and viscosity are key tunable parameters controlling analog Hawking radiation, offering new observational signatures and theoretical handles for testing analog gravity in accretion systems.

title: Composite dark matter at the LHC
summary: We investigate a composite-inspired model in which a scalar dark matter candidate couples to third-generation quarks through a non-minimal set of coloured vector-like fermions, as motivated by partial compositeness. The simultaneous presence of several mediator states leads to a richer phenomenology than conventional single-mediator descriptions, and we confront the framework with the observed relic abundance, direct-detection and indirect-detection constraints, as well as data from the Large Hadron Collider. At colliders, we compare the sensitivity of dedicated new-physics searches with that of unfolded measurements of Standard Model processes, and we assess the impact of higher-order corrections on the different production mechanisms. We find that dedicated searches generally provide the strongest collider exclusions, while unfolded measurements offer complementary sensitivity. Direct detection becomes increasingly powerful as the interaction strength grows and can become the dominant constraint. This broader complementarity arises because collider data directly test the production and decay of the coloured mediators, whereas cosmological and astroparticle observables constrain the interactions governing dark-matter abundance, scattering and annihilation. Although present constraints significantly restrict the model, viable regions compatible with the observed dark-matter abundance remain.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a composite-inspired dark matter model with multiple colored vector-like fermion mediators coupling scalar dark matter to third-generation quarks; it comprehensively confronts the model with relic density, direct/indirect detection, and LHC constraints—finding that dedicated collider searches dominate exclusions, direct detection gains prominence at larger couplings, and viable parameter space remains.
AI.motivation: Motivated by partial compositeness, the model introduces a scalar dark matter candidate coupled to third-generation quarks via multiple colored vector-like fermion mediators—enabling richer phenomenology than single-mediator frameworks.
AI.method: The authors perform a multi-probe analysis: compute thermal relic abundance; evaluate spin-independent direct-detection cross sections (including loop and effective-operator contributions); assess gamma-ray and antiproton indirect-detection limits; simulate LHC signatures (pair and associated production of mediators) and compare sensitivity of dedicated BSM searches versus unfolded SM measurements; include NLO QCD corrections for key production channels.
AI.result: Dedicated LHC searches provide strongest collider limits; unfolded SM measurements offer complementary reach; direct detection becomes dominant over collider bounds for larger couplings; indirect detection is subdominant in most regions; cosmological and collider constraints are qualitatively distinct due to differing sensitivity to mediator production vs. DM interactions; viable parameter space consistent with Ωh² ≈ 0.12 remains after all constraints.
AI.conclusion: The multi-mediator composite-inspired framework remains phenomenologically viable despite stringent multi-experiment constraints; its testability relies on synergies across collider, direct-detection, and cosmological observables—highlighting the necessity of combined analyses in beyond-Standard-Model dark matter searches.

title: Higher abelian gauge theory in BV formalism
summary: A BV structure is constructed on the space of zero modes of a quadratic elliptic higher abelian gauge theory. The associated BV integral is shown to be independent of the choice of zero-mode Lagrangian under mild hypotheses. The construction yields explicit zero-mode partition functions for several $p$-form abelian gauge theories.

AI.tldr: Constructs a BV structure on zero modes of quadratic elliptic higher abelian gauge theories and proves independence of the BV integral from the choice of zero-mode Lagrangian; yields explicit partition functions for p-form abelian gauge theories.
AI.motivation: To rigorously define and compute zero-mode contributions to partition functions in higher abelian gauge theories using the Batalin–Vilkovisky (BV) formalism, ensuring gauge-invariance and independence from auxiliary choices.
AI.method: Constructs a BV structure on the finite-dimensional space of zero modes of a quadratic elliptic higher abelian gauge theory; analyzes the BV integral’s dependence on the choice of Lagrangian submanifold (zero-mode Lagrangian) in the BV setup; applies tools from elliptic theory and symplectic reduction.
AI.result: Proves that the BV integral over zero modes is independent of the zero-mode Lagrangian under mild ellipticity and non-degeneracy hypotheses; computes explicit zero-mode partition functions for various p-form abelian gauge theories (e.g., Maxwell, BF, and higher-form analogues).
AI.conclusion: The zero-mode sector of quadratic elliptic higher abelian gauge theories admits a canonical BV structure whose integral yields well-defined, Lagrangian-independent partition functions—providing a robust framework for semiclassical and topological path integral computations.

title: When the gravity path integral describes a statistical average
comment: 10 pages plus appendices. 33 pages total, 10 figures
summary: We find the necessary and sufficient conditions for the gravitational path integral (GPI) to admit an interpretation in terms of (i) an inner product in the Hilbert space of open/closed universes or (ii) a statistical average of boundary observables. The conditions needed for (i) are necessary but not sufficient for (ii). Requiring the stronger condition (ii) places additional constraints on all wormhole amplitudes, giving a concrete diagnostic of whether the GPI computes an average or merely a pseudo-average. To exemplify the difference between the two constraints, we present a class of gravitational toy models that satisfy (i) but fail the stronger condition (ii); to emphasize the power of the stronger condition, we initiate a bootstrap study of statistical ensembles based on condition (ii), finding that the resulting constraints substantially sharpen the bounds on the moments of the ensemble obtained by imposing (i). More broadly, both of these positivity conditions impose nontrivial constraints on wormhole amplitudes and thereby restrict which gravitational effective field theories can be embedded in consistent theories of quantum gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper derives necessary and sufficient conditions for the gravitational path integral (GPI) to admit either a Hilbert-space interpretation (inner product) or a statistical ensemble interpretation (average over boundary observables); it shows these are hierarchically related, provides toy models distinguishing them, and uses the stronger condition to bootstrap tighter bounds on ensemble moments.
AI.motivation: To clarify the physical interpretation of the gravitational path integral—specifically, whether it defines a quantum state (Hilbert space inner product) or a statistical ensemble (averaged observables)—and to constrain consistent quantum gravity theories via positivity requirements on wormhole amplitudes.
AI.method: Mathematical analysis of positivity and consistency conditions on the GPI; construction of explicit toy models satisfying Hilbert-space positivity but violating statistical-ensemble positivity; bootstrap application of the stronger (statistical) condition to bound ensemble moments.
AI.result: Derives distinct necessary/sufficient conditions for (i) GPI as inner product vs. (ii) GPI as statistical average; proves (ii) implies (i) but not conversely; constructs counterexample toy models; demonstrates that imposing (ii) yields significantly tighter moment bounds than (i) alone.
AI.conclusion: The statistical-ensemble positivity condition (ii) is a stricter, physically more meaningful diagnostic for quantum gravity consistency than Hilbert-space positivity (i); both impose nontrivial constraints on wormhole contributions and thus restrict viable gravitational effective field theories.

title: Bridging the chirp-mass gap: searching for gravitational waves from inspiraling ultra-compact binaries using LIGO O4ab data
comment: 5 pages + 3 figures (main); 7 pages + 6 figures (supp). Comments are welcome!
summary: Gravitational-wave searches for subsolar-mass compact binaries have left a gap between the planetary-mass regime accessible to long-duration searches and the higher masses probed by conventional compact-binary analyses. We close this gap by searching for the inspiral of ultra-compact binaries with chirp masses $10^{-2}$--$10^{-1}\,M_\odot$ in LIGO O4ab data. Using the statistically robust BinaryGFH-v2 method, a time-frequency technique to search for rapidly evolving inspirals lasting minutes to hours, we cover this previously challenging parameter space with a computational cost of only $\sim 350$ CPU-hours, and find no significant candidates. We thus set 90\% confidence upper limits on the binary merger-rate density, providing the first gravitational-wave constraints across this chirp-mass range. Assuming that primordial-black-hole binaries formed in the early Universe with no binary suppression ($f_{\rm sup}=1$), these results provide the first gravitational-wave constraints on the primordial-black-hole \dmh fraction in this mass range, yielding upper limits with $f_{\rm PBH}<1$ for equal-mass binaries with component masses $10^{-2}$--$10^{-1}\,M_\odot$ and asymmetric binaries with secondary masses $m_2=3\times10^{-4}$--$10^{-2}\,M_\odot$ for a primary mass $m_1=2.5\,M_\odot$.
