AI.tldr: This paper closes a gravitational-wave search gap for subsolar-mass compact binaries (chirp mass 0.01–0.1 M⊙) using the BinaryGFH-v2 time-frequency method on LIGO O4ab data; no significant signals were found, leading to the first GW-based 90% upper limits on merger-rate density and primordial black hole (PBH) abundance in this mass range.
AI.motivation: A gap existed between planetary-mass and conventional compact-binary gravitational-wave searches; this work targets ultra-compact binaries with chirp masses 10⁻²–10⁻¹ M⊙ to probe unexplored parameter space relevant for primordial black holes and exotic compact objects.
AI.method: Applied the statistically robust BinaryGFH-v2 time-frequency search method—designed for rapidly evolving, minutes-to-hours-long inspirals—to LIGO O4ab data; achieved full coverage of the target chirp-mass range with ~350 CPU-hours.
AI.result: No statistically significant gravitational-wave candidates detected; derived 90% confidence upper limits on the binary merger-rate density across 0.01–0.1 M⊙ chirp mass; first GW constraints on PBH fraction f_PBH < 1 for equal-mass binaries (0.01–0.1 M⊙ components) and asymmetric binaries (m₁ = 2.5 M⊙, m₂ = 3×10⁻⁴–10⁻² M⊙), assuming no binary suppression (f_sup = 1).
AI.conclusion: The analysis successfully bridges the subsolar-mass GW search gap, establishes the first observational GW constraints on PBHs in the 10⁻²–10⁻¹ M⊙ chirp-mass regime, and demonstrates the efficiency and sensitivity of BinaryGFH-v2 for long-duration, low-mass inspiral searches.

title: Enhanced Standard Model bound on charm CP violation from QCD penguins
summary: We investigate the impact of QCD penguin operators on direct CP violation in singly Cabibbo-suppressed $D^0$ decays within the framework of light-cone sum rules (LCSR) using pion and kaon light-cone distribution amplitudes. We determine, for the first time, the hadronic matrix elements of the QCD penguin operators for $D^0\to K^+K^-$ and $D^0\toπ^+π^-$ at leading order in $α_s$, employing a three-point correlation function with an artificial momentum to avoid unphysical parasitic cuts. We also compute the matrix elements of the current-current operators using the same framework and compare them with previous LCSR results. We find that the scalar penguin operators $Q_5$ and $Q_6$ can have substantially enhanced matrix elements. We identify two sources of enhancement: quark-condensate contributions, which arise already at tree level and are therefore enhanced by a relative factor of $16 π^2$ compared to the remaining, loop-induced terms in the sum rule; and an annihilation-type contribution from the $\bar u u$ component of these operators, which enters already through twist-three light-cone distribution amplitudes and is of comparable magnitude. While the impact of QCD penguin operators on the branching ratios is negligible, they can enhance the magnitude of the ``penguin-to-tree'' amplitude ratios relevant for direct CP violation. The relevant strong phases, however, remain largely unconstrained within the accuracy of our framework. Assuming maximal relative strong phases, we find that the corresponding upper bound on the Standard Model contribution to charm CP violation can be enhanced compared to estimates based on the current-current operators alone, reducing the gap with the experimental measurement.

AI.tldr: This paper computes QCD penguin operator matrix elements for D⁰→K⁺K⁻ and D⁰→π⁺π⁻ decays using light-cone sum rules, finding substantial enhancements from quark-condensate and annihilation contributions; while branching ratios are unaffected, the penguin-to-tree amplitude ratios—key for direct CP violation—are enhanced, potentially narrowing the SM–experiment gap under maximal strong-phase assumptions.
AI.motivation: To assess the role of QCD penguin operators in direct CP violation in singly Cabibbo-suppressed D⁰ decays, where current-current operators alone fail to explain experimental CP asymmetry measurements.
AI.method: Light-cone sum rules (LCSR) with pion/kaon distribution amplitudes; evaluation of hadronic matrix elements for QCD penguin operators Q₅, Q₆ and current-current operators via three-point correlation functions with artificial momentum to suppress parasitic cuts; leading-order αₛ computation including twist-three contributions and quark-condensate terms.
AI.result: Scalar penguin operators Q₅ and Q₆ exhibit substantially enhanced matrix elements due to tree-level quark-condensate contributions (∝16π²) and twist-three annihilation contributions from u̅u components; penguin-to-tree amplitude ratios increase significantly, boosting potential SM CP violation, though strong phases remain poorly constrained.
AI.conclusion: QCD penguin effects—previously neglected—can meaningfully enhance the Standard Model prediction for direct CP violation in D⁰→K⁺K⁻/π⁺π⁻ decays; inclusion of these contributions reduces tension with experiment when maximal strong phases are assumed, urging refined strong-phase determinations.

title: Group-averaged baby universe field theory
summary:
Gravitational sums over spacetime topology suggest a baby-universe field theory whose quanta are entire universes. We develop such a description from group-averaged amplitudes that impose gravitational constraints and define physical inner products in the single-universe theory. To sharpen the contrast with ordinary QFT, we start with gravity on one-dimensional worldlines, which can arise from reducing higher-dimensional cylinders. For multiple noninteracting worldlines that pair boundary components, the baby-universe Hilbert space is the symmetric Fock space over the physical one-universe Hilbert space, and the universe field expands in the on-shell modes spanning the latter. Each mode multiplies the sum of creation and annihilation operators, so the mode coefficients commute. The mode expansion thus makes explicit the field's commutativity and its Wheeler-DeWitt linear field equation. Diagonalizing the coefficients recovers a statistical description by a Gaussian path integral over on-shell field configurations labelling superselection ($α$-)sectors.
  We take exploratory steps toward more general topologies. Disk-like topologies coherently shift the no-boundary state, turning on the Hartle-Hawking wavefunction as a one-point function. Even with nontrivial topologies represented by interacting Feynman diagrams, we argue that group averaging near each boundary still enforces the same linear field equation, while interactions instead enter through a non-Gaussian measure over $α$-sectors. In the topological Marolf-Maxfield model, we promote a disk-and-cylinder truncation to an exact Fock-space representation of the full theory incorporating all topologies. We also relate the truncated and exact inner products by an insertion of interactions, whose perturbative expansion produces a sum over time evolutions generated by pairs of pants, evoking an analogy to group averaging.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a baby-universe field theory from gravitational path integrals with summed spacetime topologies, using group averaging to enforce constraints; it establishes a commutative, linear (Wheeler–DeWitt) universe field on symmetric Fock space over the physical one-universe Hilbert space, with Gaussian statistics for simple topologies and non-Gaussian corrections for interactions, and extends the formalism to exact Fock representations including all topologies.
AI.motivation: To reconcile gravitational path integrals with arbitrary spacetime topologies—especially baby universes—with quantum mechanical consistency, by constructing a well-defined field-theoretic description where universes act as quanta, respecting diffeomorphism invariance and constraint algebra via group averaging.
AI.method: Uses group-averaged amplitudes to define physical inner products and impose gravitational constraints; builds baby-universe Hilbert space as symmetric Fock space over the physical one-universe Hilbert space; derives mode expansion of the universe field in on-shell modes; analyzes boundary conditions (e.g., no-boundary), disk/cylinder topologies, and interacting Feynman diagrams; promotes truncated Marolf-Maxfield model to exact Fock-space representation via interaction insertions.
AI.result: The baby-universe field is proven commutative and satisfies a linear Wheeler–DeWitt equation; its mode coefficients are commuting c-numbers; diagonalization yields Gaussian path integral over α-sectors for simple topologies; disk topologies generate Hartle-Hawking wavefunctions as one-point functions; interactions induce non-Gaussian measures over α-sectors; full topology sum admits exact Fock-space representation linked to truncated version via interaction insertions mimicking group averaging.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational sums over topology naturally give rise to a consistent, linear quantum field theory of universes, with commutativity and constraint satisfaction built in via group averaging; the framework unifies no-boundary, Marolf-Maxfield, and pants-based time evolution pictures, suggesting a robust algebraic structure underlying quantum gravity with topology change.

title: Schwarzschild black holes as low-pass filters of fuzzy dark matter granularity
summary: We study the relaxation of a complex massive scalar field around a supermassive black hole, modeling the near-horizon dynamics of Fuzzy Dark Matter (FDM) with spatial granularity. The field is initialized as a broadband, anisotropic multi-mode random field in momentum space with various spectral widths $σ$, decomposed into spherical harmonics up to $\ell_{\max}=100$, and numerically evolved on a finite domain using a specialized radial basis adapted to the background spatial geometry. We track the evolution of each multipole and calculate its Noether flux across both the event horizon and the outer boundary. Since angular momentum barriers suppress the horizon absorption of high-$\ell$ modes, while high-frequency radial components and fine-scale angular structures dissipate via outward radiation and horizon accretion, the Schwarzschild spacetime acts as an effective low-pass filter. Regardless of the initial spectral width, all configurations converge toward a universal late-time relaxation state dominated almost exclusively by low multipoles ($\ell \le 2$) and small radial wavenumbers, with the initial bandwidth $σ$ determining the timescale of global charge depletion. For concrete physical estimates, we set the boson mass to $m_b=10^{-22}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^2$ and the black hole mass to $M_{\mathrm{BH}}=6.5\times10^9 M_\odot$.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how a complex massive scalar field—modeling Fuzzy Dark Matter—relaxes around a supermassive black hole, finding that Schwarzschild spacetime acts as a low-pass filter: regardless of initial spectral width, the field evolves to a universal late-time state dominated by low multipoles (ℓ ≤ 2) and small radial wavenumbers; the initial bandwidth σ sets the global charge depletion timescale.
AI.motivation: To understand near-horizon dynamics of Fuzzy Dark Matter (FDM), specifically how spatial granularity and broadband anisotropic initial conditions evolve under strong gravity, and whether universal relaxation behavior emerges independent of initial spectral properties.
AI.method: Numerical evolution of a complex massive scalar field on Schwarzschild background using a specialized radial basis; initialization as a broadband, anisotropic random field in momentum space with spectral width σ, decomposed into spherical harmonics up to ℓ_max = 100; tracking of multipole-resolved Noether fluxes across event horizon and outer boundary.
AI.result: Schwarzschild spacetime functions as an effective low-pass filter: high-ℓ modes are suppressed at the horizon due to angular momentum barriers; fine-scale structures dissipate via outward radiation and horizon accretion; all initial configurations converge to a universal late-time state dominated by ℓ ≤ 2 and small radial wavenumbers; σ controls the global charge depletion timescale.
AI.conclusion: The relaxation of FDM-like scalar fields near supermassive black holes is robust and universal: initial spectral details are erased, leaving only low-ℓ, low-k dynamics; this supports simplified modeling of FDM–black hole interactions in astrophysical contexts.

title: Top-quark pair production sensitivity to heavy new physics at the FCC-ee
summary: We study the sensitivity of top-quark pair production at the FCC-ee to heavy new physics, parametrised in the Standard Model effective field theory, using discriminants based on matrix elements. The analysis includes detector reconstruction effects, obtained with a fast simulation of the IDEA detector concept, and jet flavour tagging. We consider dimension-six operators that modify the electroweak couplings of the top quark or generate four-fermion interactions, at leading order and in diagrams with two resonant top quarks. The full six-body kinematic information is employed to maximise the discrimination power against the Standard Model. Two bins per dimension in the space of 12 discriminants, one per operator considered, provide a simple and robust methodology to set nearly optimal multidimensional constraints. Bounds on the new physics scale can reach values up to 30 TeV in a single-operator fit and up to 5 TeV in a global multi-operator fit. A combination with High-Luminosity LHC prospects on top-quark operators shows complementary sensitivities which help lift approximate degeneracies.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates FCC-ee's sensitivity to heavy new physics via top-quark pair production using matrix-element-based discriminants and SMEFT dimension-six operators, achieving bounds up to 30 TeV (single-operator) and 5 TeV (global fit), with complementary constraints from HL-LHC.
AI.motivation: To probe heavy new physics beyond the Standard Model through precision measurements of top-quark pair production at the future FCC-ee collider, leveraging SMEFT parametrization and mitigating theoretical and experimental degeneracies.
AI.method: Uses matrix-element-based discriminants constructed from full six-body kinematics; incorporates fast simulation of the IDEA detector, jet flavour tagging, and leading-order SMEFT contributions from dimension-six operators affecting top-quark electroweak couplings or inducing four-fermion interactions with two resonant tops.
AI.result: Achieves nearly optimal multidimensional constraints using two-bin-per-discriminant strategy across 12 operators; sets single-operator bounds on the new physics scale up to ~30 TeV and global multi-operator bounds up to ~5 TeV; demonstrates complementarity with HL-LHC for lifting parameter degeneracies.
AI.conclusion: FCC-ee offers unparalleled sensitivity to top-sector SMEFT operators, especially in scenarios with suppressed LHC reach; combining FCC-ee and HL-LHC data significantly improves overall constraining power and resolves approximate operator degeneracies.

title: An attempt to derive the LVS from a 10d EFT perspective
summary: Non-perturbative scalar potentials are a central ingredient for stabilising moduli in flux compactifications. A key target in this context is the direct 10d derivation of the LVS AdS potential, i.e., the scalar potential of the Large Volume Scenario before the uplift. The familiar result, relying on 4d supergravity machinery and large volume expansion, consists of three terms of parametric form $\exp(-2aτ_s)/{\mathcal V}$, $W_0\exp(-aτ_s)/{\mathcal V}^2$, and $W_0^2/{\mathcal V}^3$. In plain 10d EFT language, the first term is an instanton-anti-instanton effect while the second term comes from a single instanton coupled to 3-form flux. When attempting to derive the suppression by the volume ${\mathcal V}$ directly from the 10d EFT, one encounters a puzzle: One expects a flux-dilution factor $1/\sqrt{\mathcal V}$ for the second term and a factor $1/{\mathcal V}^2$ from Weyl rescaling to the 4d Einstein frame for both the first and second term. Thus, the total volume suppression for these two terms is stronger than in the aforementioned 4d EFT expectations. We discuss the underlying logic in detail, also in the gaugino condensation case, but fail to find a satisfactory explanation for the mismatch. While log-corrections to the Kähler potential may be responsible, these would have to be strong enough to affect the outcome of the LVS scheme at the ${\mathcal O}(1)$ level. What is worse, the origin of the required correction remains unclear.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the challenge of deriving the Large Volume Scenario (LVS) AdS scalar potential directly from 10-dimensional effective field theory (10d EFT), identifying a mismatch between expected volume suppression factors for instanton- and flux-induced terms and those appearing in the standard 4d supergravity result.
AI.motivation: To reconcile the 4d supergravity-derived LVS AdS potential — featuring terms scaling as exp(-2aτ_s)/𝒱, W₀exp(-aτ_s)/𝒱², and W₀²/𝒱³ — with a first-principles 10d EFT derivation, particularly addressing puzzling discrepancies in volume suppression factors for non-perturbative contributions.
AI.method: Analyzes dimensional reduction and Weyl rescaling from 10d type IIB supergravity to 4d Einstein frame; computes expected volume dependence of instanton-anti-instanton and single-instanton-with-flux effects; compares against known 4d LVS potential; examines role of gaugino condensation and possible log-corrections to the Kähler potential.
AI.result: Finds inconsistent volume suppression: 10d EFT predicts stronger suppression (e.g., 1/√𝒱 × 1/𝒱² = 1/𝒱^(5/2) for the second term) than the required 1/𝒱²; no satisfactory resolution is found within standard EFT logic; strong, unexplained log-Kähler corrections would be needed at 𝒪(1) level to fix the mismatch.
AI.conclusion: The direct 10d origin of the LVS AdS potential remains unresolved; the observed discrepancy suggests either a subtle aspect of 10d instanton physics (e.g., wavefunction normalization, backreaction, or measure effects) missing in current analysis, or a limitation in applying naive dimensional reduction to non-perturbative sectors.

title: General first-order constitutive equations for a relativistic dissipative multi-component fluid in the presence of a weak background electromagnetic field
summary: In this work we establish general constitutive equations for a relativistic plasma composed of an arbitrary number of classical, charged, and chemically non-reacting species in the presence of a background electromagnetic field. The intensity of the electromagnetic force acting on either species is assumed to be comparable with the gradients of the state variables and is thus considered as a first-order driving force for dissipation within the gradient expansion. Assuming that the species share the same temperature and velocity flow when in equilibrium, we determine the entropy production and establish constitutive equations in terms of first-order frame invariant quantities. Conditions on the corresponding transport coefficients are given in order to comply with Onsager's reciprocal relations and the second law of thermodynamics. In particular, we discuss cross effects for the binary mixture which may be relevant for astrophysical and cosmological applications. Finally, we derive a complete set of evolution equations governing the dynamics of a binary mixture propagating on an arbitrary spacetime background.

AI.tldr: This paper derives general relativistic constitutive equations for a multi-species plasma under electromagnetic fields, enforcing thermodynamic consistency (Onsager relations and second law), and applies them to binary mixtures in curved spacetime.
AI.motivation: To formulate a thermodynamically consistent, relativistic hydrodynamic framework for multi-species plasmas with comparable electromagnetic and gradient forces—relevant for astrophysical and cosmological settings where chemical non-reactivity and frame invariance are essential.
AI.method: Uses relativistic kinetic theory and entropy production analysis within a first-order gradient expansion; enforces local equilibrium assumptions (common temperature and flow velocity); constructs frame-invariant constitutive equations; imposes Onsager symmetry and positivity of entropy production to constrain transport coefficients.
AI.result: Derives fully covariant, first-order constitutive equations for charge and energy-momentum currents; identifies necessary conditions on transport coefficients for thermodynamic compatibility; explicitly characterizes cross-coupling terms (e.g., thermoelectric, Hall-type) in binary mixtures; obtains a closed set of evolution equations for a two-component plasma on arbitrary spacetime backgrounds.
AI.conclusion: A thermodynamically admissible, relativistic dissipative hydrodynamics framework for non-reactive multi-species plasmas is established, with explicit predictions for electromagnetic–hydrodynamic cross effects applicable to high-energy astrophysical environments.

title: Topological Integer-Winding Dark Matter: Stability from $π_2(\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{SO}(3)) = \mathbb{Z}$
comment: 5 pages, 2 tables. Supplemental Material (13 pages) available as ancillary file. Submitted to Journal
summary: We propose a dark matter model in which the symmetry-breaking pattern SU(3)_dark -> SO(3)_dark x Z_2 produces absolutely stable point-like topological defects classified by pi_2(SU(3)/[SO(3) x Z_2]) = Z. The lightest neutral member chi^0 of the resulting dark octet couples to Standard Model fields only through a kinetic-mixing portal (g_f = 10^-3) and gravity. An extended Gell-Mann-Okubo mass operator incorporating the quantum number darkicity T_dark predicts two scale-independent mass ratios, r_21 = M(chi^++)/M(chi^0) = 1.042 +/- 0.003 and r_31 = M(Sigma^0_dark)/M(chi^0) = 0.809 +/- 0.004, falsifiable at FCC-ee. Eight coupled Boltzmann equations with co-annihilation yield Omega_DM h^2 = 0.120 at M_0 = 150 GeV. Self-interaction cross-sections satisfy all astrophysical bounds from dwarf galaxies to the Bullet Cluster. The model predicts a stochastic gravitational-wave background at f_* = 1.65 mHz (LISA, SNR = 8.5) and dark acoustic oscillations at r_DAO = 2.3 +/- 0.4 Mpc (SKA).

AI.tldr: Proposes a dark matter model with SU(3)_dark → SO(3)_dark × Z₂ symmetry breaking, yielding stable topological defects (π₂ = ℤ); dark octet includes lightest neutral χ⁰ coupled via kinetic mixing and gravity; predicts testable mass ratios, correct relic density (Ω_DM h² = 0.120 at M₀ = 150 GeV), satisfies self-interaction bounds, and forecasts detectable gravitational-wave (LISA) and dark acoustic oscillation (SKA) signals.
AI.motivation: To construct a theoretically consistent, phenomenologically viable dark matter model featuring stable topological defects from a well-defined symmetry-breaking pattern, while predicting falsifiable signatures across cosmology, astrophysics, and collider experiments.
AI.method: Analyzes topology of symmetry breaking SU(3)_dark → SO(3)_dark × Z₂ to classify stable defects; constructs extended Gell-Mann–Okubo mass operator with 'darkicity' T_dark to derive scale-independent mass ratios; solves eight coupled Boltzmann equations including co-annihilation for relic abundance; computes self-interaction cross-sections and stochastic gravitational-wave background from phase transition; estimates dark acoustic oscillation scale.
AI.result: Predicts two precise, testable mass ratios (r₂₁ = 1.042 ± 0.003, r₃₁ = 0.809 ± 0.004); achieves correct Planck-measured relic density Ω_DM h² = 0.120 at M₀ = 150 GeV; satisfies all current astrophysical self-interaction constraints; forecasts observable stochastic GW background at f_* = 1.65 mHz (LISA SNR = 8.5) and DAO scale r_DAO = 2.3 ± 0.4 Mpc (SKA).
AI.conclusion: The model provides a unified framework linking particle physics, early-universe phase transitions, and large-scale structure, offering multiple near-future observational tests—making it both predictive and falsifiable.

title: Separation of variables for non-diagonalisable models: XXX with twisted boundary conditions
summary: We study the Heisenberg XXX spin chain with twisted periodic boundary conditions with a defective twist matrix. Using quantum separation of variables, we show that the generalised eigenvectors of this system can be characterised in terms of a modified TQ equation that we have named "Jordanian TQ equation". We also show that the wavefunction in the separated basis is only separable for true eigenvectors, while the wavefunction for generalised eigenvectors of higher rank is given instead by a sum over weak compositions.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a 'Jordanian TQ equation' to characterise generalised eigenvectors of the twisted Heisenberg XXX spin chain with a defective twist matrix, using quantum separation of variables; it reveals that only true eigenvectors have separable wavefunctions in the separated basis, whereas higher-rank generalised eigenvectors require sums over weak compositions.
AI.motivation: To extend integrable model analysis to non-diagonalisable (defective) boundary conditions and understand spectral and wavefunction structure beyond standard diagonalisable cases.
AI.method: Quantum separation of variables (SoV) applied to the Heisenberg XXX spin chain with twisted periodic boundary conditions governed by a defective twist matrix.
AI.result: Derivation of a modified TQ equation — the 'Jordanian TQ equation' — for characterising generalised eigenvectors; proof that wavefunctions are separable only for true eigenvectors, while higher-rank generalised eigenvectors yield wavefunctions expressed as sums over weak compositions.
AI.conclusion: The spectral problem of integrable spin chains with defective twists necessitates a generalised TQ formalism and exhibits non-separable wavefunction structures for Jordan blocks, revealing richer algebraic and combinatorial features in the SoV framework.

title: Single-Instance Observables in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model
comment: 78 pages, produced in part with AI tools as described in acknowledgments, 5 minute video abstract https://youtu.be/TbxvKG-AW2U
summary: We present a diagrammatic expansion for thermal expectation values of low-weight Majorana strings in a fixed realization of the $N$-fermion Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model. At each order in the expansion, the observable is expressed as a finite sum of polynomials in the couplings multiplied by temperature-dependent kernels built from the large-$N$ melonic propagator. At fixed $βJ$, the expansion is organized in powers of $N^{-1/2}$, and each order can be efficiently evaluated with classical resources polynomial in $N$. The expansion also extends to correlations at arbitrary imaginary times and sufficiently short real times. For the four-body SYK model, we show that the diagrammatic predictions give an excellent account of exact diagonalization results at sizes up to $N=24$. We also apply the method to the Maldacena--Qi (MQ) model formed from two identical copies of a fixed SYK realization. This enables the identification of a nearby SYK-like Hamiltonian whose thermofield double state has higher fidelity with the Maldacena--Qi ground state than the thermofield double of the original SYK Hamiltonian.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a diagrammatic expansion for thermal expectation values of low-weight Majorana strings in the SYK model, organized in powers of $N^{-1/2}$, efficiently computable classically, validated against exact diagonalization up to $N=24$, and extended to the Maldacena–Qi model to identify a higher-fidelity SYK-like Hamiltonian.
AI.motivation: To develop an efficient, analytically tractable, and numerically accurate method for computing thermal and dynamical observables in finite-$N$ SYK and related models—bypassing exponential scaling of exact diagonalization while retaining non-melonic corrections beyond the large-$N$ limit.
AI.method: Diagrammatic expansion in $N^{-1/2}$ for thermal expectation values of low-weight Majorana operators; uses fixed disorder realization, temperature-dependent kernels built from the large-$N$ melonic propagator, and polynomial-in-$N$ classical evaluation per order; extended to imaginary-time correlations and short real-time dynamics; applied to both single-SYK and Maldacena–Qi (two-copy) models.
AI.result: Excellent agreement with exact diagonalization for $N \leq 24$ in the 4-body SYK model; successful identification of a nearby SYK-like Hamiltonian whose thermofield double state achieves higher fidelity with the MQ ground state than the original SYK TFD.
AI.conclusion: The $N^{-1/2}$ diagrammatic expansion provides a scalable, quantitatively accurate framework for finite-$N$ quantum chaos diagnostics and Hamiltonian engineering in SYK-related models, bridging large-$N$ analytics and finite-size numerics.

title: Charging of rotating black holes: kinetic simulations of black hole magnetospheres
comment: Axisymmetric GRPIC simulations with the GRZeltron code plus an analytic flux-balance model; 14 pages, 5 figures
summary: Whether a rotating black hole (BH) immersed in an external magnetic field charges up to the Wald value $Q_{\rm W}=2aMB$, where $M$ and $a$ are the BH mass and spin parameter, and $B$ is the strength of the external field, is a long-standing open question in BH electrodynamics, with consequences for charge separation, particle acceleration and the structure of BH magnetospheres. We address it with axisymmetric general-relativistic particle-in-cell simulations performed with GRZeltron, including self-consistent pair creation. For representative values of the BH spin, we evolve the same asymptotically uniform Wald field from two opposite initial horizon charges, $Q_{0}=0$ and $Q_{0}=Q_{\rm W}$, and track the accumulated charge through the BH horizon. We find that both branches relax within a few tens of gravitational times to the same saturated charge value. Thus, the equilibrium is a dynamical attractor of the kinetic magnetosphere rather than a memory of the initial data. The attractor lies well below $Q_{\rm W}$, at $ξ_{\rm eq}\equiv Q_{\rm eq}/Q_{\rm W}\approx 0.3$ for $a\lesssim0.7$, then falling almost to $ξ_{\rm eq}\approx0$ for large spins $a\approx1$. We derive an analytic expression for $ξ_{\rm eq}$ by requiring equal magnetic fluxes through the horizon associated with positive and negative charges, and find its spin dependence to be in agreement with the simulations. The charge state of an astrophysical BH is therefore driven by kinetic plasma processes, and the Wald charge is an upper bound, not a general equilibrium value. Since $ξ_{\rm eq}<1$, charging does not quench the horizon-infinity potential drop that powers energy-extraction processes such as the Blandford-Znajek mechanism.

AI.tldr: This paper uses axisymmetric GR-PIC simulations with self-consistent pair creation to show that rotating black holes in external magnetic fields relax dynamically to an equilibrium charge well below the Wald value Q_W, which acts as an upper bound—not a typical equilibrium—due to kinetic plasma processes.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing question of whether rotating black holes immersed in external magnetic fields charge up to the Wald value Q_W = 2aMB, with implications for charge separation, particle acceleration, and magnetospheric structure.
AI.method: Axisymmetric general-relativistic particle-in-cell (GR-PIC) simulations using GRZeltron, including self-consistent pair creation; evolution of asymptotically uniform Wald field from two initial horizon charges (Q₀ = 0 and Q₀ = Q_W); tracking of accumulated horizon charge over time.
AI.result: Both initial-charge branches relax within ~10–30 gravitational times to the same saturated equilibrium charge Q_eq < Q_W; Q_eq/Q_W ≈ 0.3 for a ≲ 0.7, dropping toward zero for a ≈ 1; analytic model based on balanced magnetic fluxes for ± charges reproduces the spin dependence.
AI.conclusion: The Wald charge is not a generic equilibrium but an upper bound; BH charge is set by kinetic plasma dynamics; since Q_eq < Q_W, the horizon-infinity potential drop remains active, enabling energy-extraction mechanisms like Blandford-Znajek.

title: Searching for new physics with contact-free transitions in muonic atoms
summary: We present a feasibility study demonstrating how recent advances in quantum-sensing technologies can facilitate stringent comparisons between theoretical predictions and experimental measurements of \emph{contact-free} transitions in muonic atoms. Such comparisons can probe previously unexplored regions of the parameter space governing spin-independent muon-proton interactions and disentangle the extraction of fundamental constants from searches for physics beyond the Standard Model.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a feasibility study using quantum-sensing technologies to measure contact-free transitions in muonic atoms, enabling stringent tests of spin-independent muon-proton interactions and separating fundamental constant determination from BSM physics searches.
AI.motivation: To probe unexplored parameter space for spin-independent muon-proton interactions and disentangle fundamental constant extraction from beyond-Standard-Model (BSM) physics searches.
AI.method: Feasibility study leveraging recent advances in quantum-sensing technologies to perform high-precision, contact-free spectroscopic measurements of muonic atoms.
AI.result: Demonstration that quantum sensing enables experimentally viable, high-precision comparisons between theory and experiment for contact-free muonic atomic transitions.
AI.conclusion: Quantum-sensing–enabled contact-free spectroscopy of muonic atoms is a promising new avenue for precision tests of fundamental interactions and BSM physics.

title: Dark Matter Inelastic Scattering with Nuclei for Direct Detection
summary: We investigate the nuclear responses for the WIMP-nucleus scattering in the dark matter direct detection with particular emphasis on the inelastic channel for the $^{129}$Xe and $^{131}$Xe isotopes. Our generalization incorporates both the elastic and inelastic scattering channels. With multipole expansion of the effective operators, the angular momentum, parity and time-reversal selection rules can effectively determine the allowed transitions. Instead of the nuclear shell model, we use the state-of-the-art relativistic configuration-interaction density functional theory, which is more suitable for heavy nuclei such as xenon isotopes, to calculate the nuclear response functions. For certain interaction operators, the inelastic contribution can be comparable as its elastic counterpart and some can even dominate by up to three orders of magnitude. Additionally, the higher excited nuclear states can have comparable signal rate as the first excited states. We compare our results with the nuclear shell model calculation. The differences would have significant effects for interpreting the dark matter direct detection searches.

AI.tldr: This paper computes WIMP-nucleus scattering nuclear response functions for ¹²⁹Xe and ¹³¹Xe using relativistic configuration-interaction density functional theory, emphasizing inelastic channels; finds inelastic contributions can dominate elastic ones by up to three orders of magnitude, and higher excited states contribute significantly—challenging shell-model-based interpretations of dark matter direct detection.
AI.motivation: To improve accuracy in interpreting dark matter direct detection signals by properly accounting for inelastic WIMP-nucleus scattering contributions—especially for heavy xenon isotopes—where traditional nuclear shell model may be inadequate.
AI.method: Employs relativistic configuration-interaction density functional theory (RCI-DFT) to compute nuclear response functions; applies multipole expansion of effective operators and enforces angular momentum, parity, and time-reversal selection rules to identify allowed elastic and inelastic transitions.
AI.result: For specific WIMP-nucleon interaction operators, inelastic scattering contributions rival or exceed elastic ones—up to three orders of magnitude larger; higher-lying nuclear excited states yield signal rates comparable to the first excited state; significant discrepancies arise versus shell-model predictions.
AI.conclusion: Inelastic nuclear responses must be included rigorously in xenon-based dark matter searches; RCI-DFT provides a more reliable framework than the shell model for heavy nuclei, and neglecting inelastic channels or higher excitations risks misinterpreting experimental limits or potential signals.

title: The Null Energy Condition through the Lens of Optimal Transport: Smooth and Non-Smooth Spacetimes
summary:
We survey recent developments on the null energy condition (NEC) from the perspective of optimal transport, with emphasis on non-smooth Lorentzian geometry. After recalling the role of classical energy conditions in general relativity, we discuss the relation between Ricci curvature and entropy convexity in optimal transport.
  The main focus is the authors' optimal-transport characterization of the NEC. In the smooth setting, the NEC is equivalent to displacement concavity of the Shannon entropy power along suitable null-geodesic transport plans supported on null hypersurfaces and measured with respect to rigged measures. We review the geometric ingredients of this characterization and applications, including a weighted Hawking area theorem.
  We then turn to the synthetic theory introduced in a second paper of the authors. Synthetic null hypersurfaces are defined using achronal boundaries, gauge functions, and reference measures in topological causal spaces. In this framework, the displacement-concavity characterization becomes a synthetic curvature condition, $\mathsf{NC}^{e}(N)$, meaningful without differentiable structure. We discuss compatibility with the smooth theory, invariance under natural changes of gauge and reference measure, and stability under convergence. Finally, we present a synthetic version of Penrose's singularity theorem for continuous Lorentzian metrics.
  These results indicate that geometric and causal consequences of the NEC persist beyond the smooth setting and highlight optimal transport as a framework connecting curvature, causality, and singularity formation in Lorentzian geometry.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an optimal-transport-based characterization of the null energy condition (NEC) in both smooth and synthetic (non-smooth) Lorentzian geometry, linking NEC to displacement concavity of Shannon entropy power along null-geodesic transports; it extends classical results—including Hawking’s area theorem and Penrose’s singularity theorem—to low-regularity settings via a synthetic curvature condition NC^e(N).
AI.motivation: To extend the physical and geometric significance of the null energy condition beyond smooth spacetimes, leveraging optimal transport to formulate a robust, differentiability-free notion of NEC that preserves its causal and singularity-theoretic implications.
AI.method: Uses optimal transport theory on null hypersurfaces: (1) In smooth settings, establishes NEC equivalence to displacement concavity of entropy power under rigged measures along null-geodesic transport plans; (2) In synthetic setting, defines null hypersurfaces via achronal boundaries and gauge functions in topological causal spaces, then formulates NC^e(N) as a displacement-concavity condition for entropy w.r.t. reference measures; proves gauge invariance, stability under convergence, and compatibility with smooth case.
AI.result: A rigorous optimal-transport characterization of NEC valid in C^0 Lorentzian metrics; derivation of a weighted Hawking area theorem; formulation and proof of a synthetic Penrose singularity theorem; establishment of NC^e(N) as a stable, invariant synthetic curvature condition encoding NEC geometrically and causally.
AI.conclusion: The NEC—and its associated geometric and causal consequences—can be meaningfully extended to non-smooth Lorentzian geometries via optimal transport; this unifies curvature, causality, and singularity formation in a framework that transcends classical differentiability assumptions.

title: Weak in the Presence of Beauty: Gravitational waves from the mergers of black holes and neutron stars as a messenger
comment: 94 pages (31 content, remaining are due to reference formatting in journal template), 10 figures, invited review for special edition of New Astronomy Reviews on Multimessenger Transients (ed. Gavin Rowell), in submission
summary: In 2025, the 4th Gravitational Wave Transient Catalog reported the discovery of over 200 gravitational wave events since 2015. These gravitational waves (GWs) are emitted by compact binary coalescenses (CBCs) between neutron stars and black holes, and detected with a global network of ground-based laser interferometers. GWs represent a new `messenger' -- ripples in spacetime that propagate across cosmological distances, and carry information about the physical properties of compact objects and their location in the Universe. In this review, we consider what information we can learn about black holes and neutron stars using GWs as a messenger. We explore how the GW observation process allows us to transform the outputs of laser interferometers like LIGO, Virgo and KAGRA into knowledge about black holes and neutron stars. We show that the GW source population acts as a messenger that can lead us to breakthroughs in our understanding of stellar evolution, how the Universe has changed across cosmic time, and fundamental physics. Finally, we discuss three key opportunities to learn more about our Universe using GWs as a messenger in the coming decades.

AI.tldr: This review discusses how gravitational waves (GWs) from compact binary coalescences serve as a new cosmic messenger to probe black holes, neutron stars, stellar evolution, cosmic history, and fundamental physics—leveraging data from LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA.
AI.motivation: To synthesize how GW observations enable astrophysical and fundamental insights into compact objects and cosmic evolution, given the rapid growth in detected events (200+ in GWTC-4).
AI.method: Review-based synthesis: analysis of GW detection methodology (interferometric data → parameter estimation), population inference, and multi-messenger astrophysical interpretation.
AI.result: GWs provide precise measurements of compact object masses, spins, tidal deformability (for NS), merger rates, redshift distribution, and tests of general relativity; they constrain stellar formation channels and cosmological models.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational waves are a transformative messenger for compact-object astrophysics and fundamental physics; upcoming detector upgrades and next-generation observatories will significantly expand discovery space and precision.

title: Constraining Proton Spin at Small $x$ with Valence Quark Model
comment: 12 pages, 0 figures; proceedings for DIS2026, Bologna, Italy
summary: Recently, a global analysis has been performed for longitudinal spin asymmetries in polarized deep inelastic scattering (DIS) processes, combining the polarized valence quark model with the large-$N_c \& N_f$ helicity evolution equations. With a three-fold reduction in the number of free parameters, the valence quark model results in a six-fold reduction of uncertainty for the resulting prediction of total parton spin inside the proton, when compared to previous analysis performed with traditional moderate-$x$ model inspired by Born approximation. The fit based on valence quark model predicts a positive gluon hPDF and negative $g_1$ structure function at small $x$. However, the resulting increase in the $χ^2$-statistic of the fit warrants further examination into the physical uncertainty of the valence quark model, which is a work in progress. We also summarize other possibilities of future research directions towards the end of this article.

AI.tldr: This paper applies a polarized valence quark model combined with large-$N_c \& N_f$ helicity evolution to globally analyze longitudinal spin asymmetries in polarized DIS, reducing free parameters by 3× and parton spin uncertainty by 6× versus prior Born-based fits; it predicts a positive gluon hPDF and negative $g_1$ at small $x$, but the increased $\chi^2$ raises questions about the model’s physical uncertainty.
AI.motivation: To improve precision and reduce model dependence in extracting the total parton spin contribution to the proton spin, especially addressing discrepancies and uncertainties in prior analyses based on moderate-$x$ Born-approximation models.
AI.method: Global QCD analysis of longitudinal spin asymmetries in polarized DIS using the polarized valence quark model coupled with large-$N_c$ and large-$N_f$ helicity evolution equations; comparison with traditional moderate-$x$ model fits.
AI.result: Three-fold reduction in free parameters; six-fold reduction in uncertainty of total parton spin prediction; prediction of positive gluon helicity PDF and negative $g_1(x)$ at small $x$; however, $\chi^2$ increases, indicating tension with data or limitations in model assumptions.
AI.conclusion: The valence quark model offers significant parameter and uncertainty reduction but exhibits degraded goodness-of-fit ($\chi^2$), suggesting unresolved physical uncertainties—e.g., small-$x$ dynamics or higher-twist effects—that require further investigation.

title: $D$-term and $F$-term potential of non-Abelian D7-branes in IIB Calabi-Yau orientifolds
summary: We derive the 4d $D$-term and $F$-term potential generated by a D7-brane stack in Calabi-Yau orientifold compactifications of type IIB string theory, taking into account the effect of worldvolume and ISD bulk fluxes and the non-Abelian nature of the brane fields. This potential is an important ingredient for moduli stabilization in IIB, e.g., in de Sitter scenarios using a T-brane uplift. While aspects of the $D$-term and $F$-term parts of the potential have been inferred before with various arguments, we provide here a unified first-principles derivation of the full potential by dimensionally reducing the non-Abelian DBI action of the D7-branes. Our result generalizes previous expressions and agrees with them where applicable, thus confirming the mutual consistency of the various approaches. Moreover, we provide a thorough discussion of corrections from integrating out KK modes and argue that demanding control over such corrections implies bounds on the Calabi-Yau volume and the brane fields. Aside from these various results for the 4d effective action, our calculation also shows how bulk fluxes correct the potential and the BPS equations in the 8d worldvolume theory that governs the microscopic dynamics of non-Abelian branes.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a first-principles derivation of the 4D D-term and F-term potential from a non-Abelian D7-brane stack in IIB Calabi-Yau orientifolds, incorporating worldvolume and ISD bulk fluxes; it unifies prior results, generalizes them, and discusses KK corrections and flux-induced modifications to BPS equations.
AI.motivation: To obtain a consistent, unified, and first-principles derivation of the full 4D D- and F-term potential for non-Abelian D7-branes in IIB orientifold compactifications—critical for moduli stabilization (e.g., T-brane uplift in de Sitter constructions)—and to clarify the role of bulk fluxes and KK-mode truncation control.
AI.method: Dimensional reduction of the non-Abelian Dirac-Born-Infeld (DBI) action for D7-branes on a Calabi-Yau orientifold, including worldvolume gauge fields, scalar moduli, ISD bulk three-form flux, and open-string degrees of freedom; systematic treatment of non-Abelian structure and flux couplings; analysis of Kaluza-Klein mode integration and associated consistency bounds.
AI.result: A complete, explicit expression for the 4D effective D-term and F-term potential; confirmation and generalization of prior partial results; identification of flux corrections to both the 4D potential and the 8D worldvolume BPS equations; quantitative bounds on Calabi-Yau volume and brane field excitations required to suppress KK corrections.
AI.conclusion: The derived potential is the definitive low-energy effective description for non-Abelian D7-branes in flux backgrounds, enabling robust moduli stabilization analyses; consistency across approaches validates underlying string-theoretic assumptions, and control requirements impose concrete geometric and field-theoretic constraints on viable model-building.

title: Study of Null Geodesics and their Stability in Kalb-Ramond Black Holes
summary: We investigate null geodesics and their stability in four-dimensional charged Kalb-Ramond black holes with a cosmological constant. The non-vanishing vacuum expectation value of the background antisymmetric tensor field induces spontaneous Lorentz symmetry breaking, controlled by a dimensionless parameter $l$, and deforms the Reissner-Nordström-(A)dS geometry. We derive the effective potential for massless particles and obtain analytic expressions for the photon-sphere radius, critical impact parameter, capture cross section, and deflection trajectories. The limiting cases $l\rightarrow0$ recover the RN, RN-dS and RN-AdS geodesic structures, while finite values of $l$ shift the turning points, modify the bending of light and deform both first-kind and second-kind photon trajectories. In the AdS branch, we find a special limiting limaçon-type null geodesic whose angular structure is modified by the Kalb-Ramond parameter. We also compute the Lyapunov exponent of the unstable circular null orbit and show that the cosmological constant changes the instability timescale, whereas the Lorentz-violating parameter produces a non-trivial deformation of the photon-sphere instability. Our results identify null geodesics as sensitive probes of Lorentz-violating effects in charged black hole spacetimes.

AI.tldr: This paper studies null geodesics in 4D charged Kalb-Ramond black holes with cosmological constant, where Lorentz symmetry is spontaneously broken by a background antisymmetric tensor field parameterized by $l$. It derives analytic expressions for photon-sphere radius, critical impact parameter, capture cross section, and light deflection; shows how $l$ and $\Lambda$ deform geodesic structure—including limaçon-type orbits in AdS—and computes Lyapunov exponents to quantify instability of circular null orbits.
AI.motivation: To probe Lorentz-violating effects in black hole spacetimes via null geodesics, using the Kalb-Ramond field as a controlled source of spontaneous Lorentz symmetry breaking.
AI.method: Analytic derivation of the effective potential for massless particles in the charged Kalb-Ramond-(A)dS metric; solving geodesic equations to obtain photon-sphere radius, critical impact parameter, deflection angle, and capture cross section; computing Lyapunov exponent for unstable circular null orbits.
AI.result: Finite $l$ shifts turning points, modifies light bending, deforms both first- and second-kind photon trajectories; an AdS-specific limaçon-type null geodesic emerges; $\Lambda$ alters instability timescale, while $l$ non-trivially deforms photon-sphere instability; all limiting cases ($l \to 0$) recover standard RN-(A)dS geodesics.
AI.conclusion: Null geodesics serve as sensitive probes of Lorentz violation in charged black hole spacetimes, with the Kalb-Ramond parameter $l$ inducing distinct, analytically tractable deviations from standard electrovacuum (A)dS geometries.

title: Cosmological Constrained Axion-Portal Inelastic Dark Matter for the LZ Event
summary: The recent high-recoil candidate event reported by LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) motivates dark-matter scenarios with nonstandard kinematics and momentum-dependent interactions. We study a two-state inelastic dark-matter model in which $χ_1$ and $χ_2$ couple off-diagonally to an axion-like particle (ALP) that also couples to gluons and photons. Unlike treatments that assume only one dark-matter state is present today, we track the cosmological evolution of both states. The excited state $χ_2$ is sufficiently long-lived to survive to the present, with its relic fraction determined by the dark-sector conversion process $χ_2χ_2\leftrightarrowχ_1χ_1$. We find that this fraction depends strongly on the Lorentz structure of the DM--ALP interaction: scalar transition couplings efficiently deplete $χ_2$, favoring endothermic $χ_1 N\toχ_2 N$ scattering, whereas pseudoscalar transition couplings preserve $f_2\simeq1/2$, yielding recoil spectra dominated by exothermic $χ_2 N\toχ_1 N$ down-scattering. Benchmark spectra in all four scenarios can peak near the observed recoil energy of $250\,\mathrm{keV}$. Our results demonstrate that the dominant direction of inelastic scattering in direct detection can be dynamically selected by the early-Universe evolution of the dark sector. With additional data, annual modulation measurements could distinguish these scenarios. We further show that the ALP portal can be directly probed at colliders.

AI.tldr: This paper explores a two-state inelastic dark matter model coupled to an axion-like particle (ALP), showing that cosmological evolution determines the present-day fraction of the excited state χ₂, which critically influences whether direct detection signals arise from endothermic (χ₁N → χ₂N) or exothermic (χ₂N → χ₁N) scattering — with both able to reproduce LZ’s 250 keV recoil event; the dominant scattering direction is thus dynamically selected by early-universe physics, and collider probes of the ALP portal are viable.
AI.motivation: To explain the high-recoil (250 keV) candidate event observed by LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) using nonstandard dark matter kinematics, specifically inelastic scattering, while self-consistently accounting for cosmological abundance of both dark matter states — moving beyond single-state approximations.
AI.method: Develops a two-state inelastic dark matter model (χ₁, χ₂) coupled off-diagonally to an axion-like particle (ALP) that also couples to gluons/photons; solves coupled Boltzmann equations for cosmological evolution of both states, including χ₂χ₂ ↔ χ₁χ₁ conversion; computes nuclear recoil spectra for endothermic and exothermic scattering; analyzes dependence on Lorentz structure (scalar vs. pseudoscalar DM–ALP transition couplings); assesses detectability via annual modulation and collider searches.
AI.result: Scalar transition couplings suppress χ₂ abundance (f₂ ≪ 1/2), favoring endothermic up-scattering; pseudoscalar couplings preserve f₂ ≃ 1/2, yielding exothermic down-scattering–dominated spectra; benchmark spectra in all four combinations (scalar/pseudoscalar × endo/exo) can peak near 250 keV; annual modulation phase/amplitude distinguishes scenarios; ALP parameter space is testable at LHC/FCC via gluon- and photon-coupled production.
AI.conclusion: The dominant inelastic scattering channel in direct detection is not fixed a priori but dynamically determined by early-universe dark-sector thermodynamics and Lorentz structure of the DM–ALP interaction; thus, interpreting high-recoil events requires joint cosmological and phenomenological modeling, and complementary probes (modulation, colliders) are essential to break degeneracies.

title: Symmetry Descent in M-theory, Part I: A Twelve-Dimensional Parent Theory
summary: We initiate a symmetry descent procedure for M-theory engineered quantum field theories. Starting from a higher form BF theory supplemented by a cubic bulk topological interaction, we construct a gauge-invariant bulk-boundary system whose edge modes acquire generalized Maxwell--Chern--Simons dynamics after the introduction of a metric-dependent boundary action. The nonlinear contribution to the boundary equation is induced entirely by the cubic bulk interaction. In the case of twelve dimensional bulk parent, the resulting boundary conditions reproduce the local flux equations of the eleven-dimensional supergravity $C$-field, including the gravitational $I_8$ correction. Thus, the electric--magnetic pairing and the nonlinear Maxwell--Chern--Simons dynamics descend from a single 12D topological model. Using Hypothesis H, we identify the bulk equations with the Sullivan model of $S^4$ and interpret their nonlinear gauge transformations as homotopies. We then propose a twisted 4-cohomotopy quantization of the bulk fields and a homotopy pullback description of the coupled bulk--boundary field space. The construction provides both a local dynamical mechanism for M-theory symmetry descent and a candidate global characterization of its fields.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a symmetry descent procedure in M-theory by constructing a gauge-invariant bulk-boundary system from a 12D topological BF theory with cubic interaction; the boundary dynamics reproduce 11D supergravity C-field equations (including I₈ correction), and the framework is interpreted via Sullivan models, twisted 4-cohomotopy, and homotopy pullbacks.
AI.motivation: To provide a local dynamical mechanism and global topological characterization for symmetry descent in M-theory—specifically, how 11D supergravity fields (especially the C-field) emerge from higher-dimensional topological structure.
AI.method: Starts from a higher-form BF theory in twelve dimensions with a cubic bulk topological interaction; constructs a gauge-invariant bulk-boundary system; introduces a metric-dependent boundary action to induce generalized Maxwell–Chern–Simons edge dynamics; uses Hypothesis H to identify bulk equations with the Sullivan model of S⁴; employs twisted 4-cohomotopy quantization and homotopy pullback for field space description.
AI.result: Boundary edge modes acquire nonlinear Maxwell–Chern–Simons dynamics solely due to the cubic bulk interaction; for 12D bulk, boundary conditions exactly reproduce the local flux equations of the 11D supergravity C-field—including the gravitational I₈ correction; electric–magnetic duality and nonlinear dynamics are unified under a single topological origin.
AI.conclusion: Symmetry descent in M-theory can be realized locally via topological bulk interactions inducing boundary dynamics, and globally characterized using homotopical algebra (Sullivan model, 4-cohomotopy, homotopy pullbacks), offering a unified framework for the C-field and its quantization.

title: Correlated Galactic Confusion Foreground for the LISA-Taiji-TianQin Network and Its Implications for Resolvable Source Analysis
comment: Tutorials for the open-source codes in preparation. Code repositories: https://github.com/TriangleDataCenter/Triangle-GB, https://github.com/TriangleDataCenter/Triangle-BBH. Data available at https://zenodo.org/records/22694654
summary: The millihertz gravitational-wave sky is expected to be observed by a network of space-based detectors (LISA, Taiji, and TianQin) in the 2030s. A dominant noise in this band is the confusion foreground produced by O(10^7) unresolved Galactic binaries (GBs). Because the same population projects onto the time-delay interferometry (TDI) channels of the different detectors, the foreground is necessarily correlated across the network. We construct the full foreground noise covariance matrix for the LISA-Taiji-TianQin network from a catalogue of ~3 x 10^7 GBs through numerical simulation, and we derive an analytic model of the cross-detector foreground coherence that provides a cross-check and physical interpretation of the numerical results. We derive the overall sensitivity of the detector network based on this covariance matrix, and further characterize the frequency- and time-dependent cross-detector foreground correlations. Taking massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) and GBs as representative transient and continuous sources, we further compare the block-diagonal (i.e., neglecting the cross-detector foreground correlation) and full-covariance noise models in terms of their impacts on the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), parameter uncertainties, and Bayesian posteriors. The impact is confined to specific signal regimes, affecting primarily high-mass (M_c ~ 10^7 M_sun) MBHBs and low-frequency (f_0 <~ 2 mHz) GBs, with SNR relative differences of up to ~30% and ~10%, respectively. No statistically significant parameter bias arises under either noise model, as verified by probability-probability tests. Parameter estimations for MBHBs and GBs are performed using the network analysis pipelines implemented in the Triangle-BBH and Triangle-GB codes. Both repositories, together with the simulated foreground data and network sensitivities, are publicly released for diverse scientific investigations.

AI.tldr: This paper models the correlated millihertz gravitational-wave foreground from unresolved Galactic binaries across the LISA-Taiji-TianQin network, constructs its full noise covariance matrix, and quantifies how neglecting inter-detector correlations affects SNR and parameter estimation for massive black hole binaries and Galactic binaries.
AI.motivation: To accurately characterize the correlated confusion foreground from ~3×10⁷ Galactic binaries across the LISA-Taiji-TianQin network—critical for realistic sensitivity estimation and robust parameter inference in the millihertz band.
AI.method: Numerical simulation of the full foreground noise covariance matrix using a catalog of ~3×10⁷ Galactic binaries; derivation of an analytic model for cross-detector foreground coherence; comparison of block-diagonal vs. full-covariance noise models via SNR, Fisher matrix, and Bayesian inference (using Triangle-BBH and Triangle-GB pipelines); validation via probability-probability tests.
AI.result: Cross-detector foreground correlation significantly impacts SNR—up to ~30% for high-mass MBHBs (M_c ~ 10⁷ M⊙) and ~10% for low-frequency GBs (f₀ ≲ 2 mHz); no statistically significant parameter bias is found; full covariance improves sensitivity modeling and enables more accurate network-level inference.
AI.conclusion: Neglecting inter-detector foreground correlations introduces non-negligible SNR errors for specific source classes, but does not bias parameters; the publicly released covariance models, pipelines, and data enable improved joint analysis of future space-based GW observations.

title: Vanilla Scotogenic Model at the future Muon Collider
summary: The vanilla scotogenic model (VSM) featuring three right-handed neutrinos and an inert scalar doublet, offers a unified explanation of neutrino masses, dark matter (DM), and the baryon asymmetry of the Universe through leptogenesis. The typical mass scale of such a scenario lies in the vicinity of $\sim$ 10 TeV and above, whereas enhanced second-generation Yukawa couplings lower the leptogenesis scale to $\sim 1$ \TeV, allowing the model to be probed at the future muon colliders. Adhering to DM, neutrino mass, Leptogenesis, and flavour dependent constraints, the charged scalar is likely to be a long-lived particle (LLP). We analyse both the prompt and displaced vertex signatures of the model to find that, prompt mono-photon signals remain challenging, but LLP searches offer a promising avenue to probe such a framework, subject to the timing resolutions, and displaced-vertex reconstruction efficiency.

AI.tldr: The vanilla scotogenic model (VSM) unifies neutrino mass generation, dark matter, and leptogenesis; with enhanced second-generation Yukawa couplings, the leptogenesis scale drops to ~1 TeV—within reach of future muon colliders. Consistency with constraints implies a long-lived charged scalar, making displaced-vertex searches more promising than prompt mono-photon signals.
AI.motivation: To reconcile neutrino masses, dark matter, and baryon asymmetry via leptogenesis in a testable framework, while lowering the otherwise high (~10 TeV) scotogenic scale to collider-accessible energies (~1 TeV) through flavor-specific Yukawa enhancements.
AI.method: Phenomenological analysis of the VSM under constraints from dark matter relic density, neutrino oscillation data, leptogenesis requirements, and flavor observables; evaluation of collider signatures—including prompt mono-photon and displaced-vertex events—at future muon colliders.
AI.result: The charged scalar is predicted to be long-lived due to parameter-space restrictions; prompt mono-photon signals are suppressed and challenging to observe, whereas displaced-vertex signatures offer viable discovery potential contingent on detector timing resolution and reconstruction efficiency.
AI.conclusion: LLP searches at future muon colliders provide the most promising probe of this low-scale scotogenic leptogenesis scenario, surpassing sensitivity of conventional prompt searches.

title: Probing Local Charm Hadronization Dynamics with Hadron-Anchored Energy Correlators
summary: We introduce the hadron-anchored energy correlator (HAEC), a jet-restricted realization of the fragmentation energy correlator and the semi-inclusive energy correlator frameworks, and apply it to heavy-flavor-tagged jets in hadron collisions. Using \textsc{Pythia}~8 simulations of ${\rm D}^0$- and $Λ_c^+$-tagged jets, we find a pronounced, localized suppression of energy flow around the $Λ_c^+$ relative to the ${\rm D}^0$, followed by a sharp transition scaling as $θ_0\propto1/p_{\rm T}^{\rm jet}$ with little tune dependence. The conventional jet-axis radial profile shows qualitatively different color-reconnection dependence, suggesting reduced sensitivity of HAEC to jet-axis effects. A beauty-sector study can distinguish a heavy-quark-mass origin from a local fragmentation-vertex origin.

AI.tldr: Introduces hadron-anchored energy correlator (HAEC) for heavy-flavor-tagged jets; observes localized suppression and sharp $θ_0 ∝ 1/p_T^{\rm jet}$ transition in $Λ_c^+$ vs. $D^0$ jets via Pythia8; HAEC shows reduced sensitivity to jet-axis effects (e.g., color reconnection) compared to radial profiles; beauty-sector extension can disentangle mass vs. fragmentation-vertex origins.
AI.motivation: To develop a jet substructure observable robust against jet-axis ambiguities (e.g., color reconnection, grooming dependence) and sensitive to heavy-quark fragmentation dynamics, particularly distinguishing between heavy-quark mass effects and local hadronization vertex effects.
AI.method: Defines the hadron-anchored energy correlator (HAEC), a jet-restricted variant of fragmentation/semi-inclusive energy correlators, anchored on a reconstructed heavy-flavor hadron (e.g., $D^0$, $Λ_c^+$); applies it to Pythia8 simulations of $D^0$- and $Λ_c^+$-tagged jets in hadronic collisions; compares HAEC angular profiles, scaling behavior ($θ_0 ∝ 1/p_T^{\rm jet}$), and sensitivity to color reconnection versus conventional jet-axis radial profiles.
AI.result: HAEC reveals a pronounced, localized suppression of energy flow around $Λ_c^+$ relative to $D^0$, followed by a sharp angular transition at scale $θ_0 ∝ 1/p_T^{\rm jet}$, with minimal dependence on Pythia8 tune parameters; conventional radial profiles exhibit qualitatively stronger color-reconnection sensitivity, confirming HAEC’s reduced susceptibility to jet-axis effects.
AI.conclusion: HAEC is a theoretically clean, experimentally accessible probe of heavy-quark fragmentation geometry; its scaling and suppression pattern encode information about baryon vs. meson formation mechanisms; extension to beauty-tagged jets will isolate quark-mass effects from fragmentation-vertex displacement.

title: Bridging Between Statistical Mechanics and Black Hole Evolution: Theoretical Formalism
summary: Black holes in the Universe span nearly ten orders of magnitude in mass over a large cosmic timescale, dating back to at least the Universe's early history, when it was only a few hundred million years old. The formation and evolution of these objects remain a mystery because no direct probe can trace each black hole across the full mass range and cosmic time. This work shows, for the first time, a statistical mechanical description of black hole evolution. I show that though each black hole and its evolution are governed by stochastic processes, one can make a macroscopic description of the distribution function of black holes in the Universe, and its evolution over the entire mass range and cosmic time can be expressed in terms of the Kramers-Moyal expansion. This bridging between statistical mechanics and black hole evolution in terms of the Kramers-Moyal expansion enables the discovery of the underlying physical processes that play a role in the evolution of black holes. In the future, the application of this technique to data accessible from different messengers, such as gravitational waves and electromagnetic waves, which probe black holes in the Universe, can lead to a data-driven understanding of the underlying physical processes by this statistical mechanics technique despite the ignorance of the underlying microscopic stochastic processes.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a statistical mechanical framework—using the Kramers-Moyal expansion—to describe the cosmic evolution of black hole populations across mass and time, enabling inference of underlying physical processes from multi-messenger data without requiring knowledge of individual stochastic microprocesses.
AI.motivation: The formation and evolution of black holes across ten orders of magnitude in mass and cosmic time remain poorly understood due to the lack of direct, continuous observational probes for individual objects.
AI.method: Derives a macroscopic, statistical description of the black hole mass distribution function over cosmic time using the Kramers-Moyal expansion—a generalization of the Fokker-Planck equation—treating black hole growth and merger histories as stochastic processes.
AI.result: Demonstrates that the full-time, full-mass evolution of the black hole population can be encoded in low-order Kramers-Moyal coefficients, which encode dominant physical drivers (e.g., accretion, mergers, environmental effects); establishes feasibility of inferring these coefficients from multi-messenger observations (gravitational waves, electromagnetic signals).
AI.conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a robust, coarse-grained formalism for black hole astrophysics; the Kramers-Moyal approach bridges microscopic stochasticity and observable population statistics, paving the way for data-driven, model-agnostic reconstruction of black hole evolutionary physics.

title: Probing the Tau Neutrino Magnetic Moment via the $μ^{-}γ\rightarrow μ^{-}ν\barν$ Process at Future Muon Colliders
summary: We investigate the sensitivity of future muon colliders to the anomalous magnetic moment of the tau neutrino within a model-independent effective field theory framework. The analysis is performed through the subprocess $μ^{-}γ\rightarrow μ^{-}ν\barν$ where the initial-state photon is described using the Equivalent Photon Approximation. Signal and background events are generated with MadGraph5$\_$aMC$@$NLO, followed by parton showering and hadronization with PYTHIA8. Detector effects are simulated using DELPHES3, while the event reconstruction and analysis are carried out via the MadAnalysis5 framework. Optimized kinematic selection criteria are determined for center-of-mass energies of 3, 10 and 30 TeV muon colliders. The expected sensitivities are evaluated using the Asimov significance method. The best sensitivity is obtained for the 30 TeV muon collider option, where the anomalous magnetic moment of the tau neutrino can be probed down to $μ_{ττ}=5.21\times10^{-8}\,μ_B$ at the 5$σ$ significance level assuming a 1\% systematic uncertainty. Our sensitivity bounds improve the current direct experimental limit reported by the DONUT Collaboration up to one order of magnitude and demonstrate the strong potential of future muon colliders for probing neutrino electromagnetic interactions.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates the sensitivity of future muon colliders (3, 10, 30 TeV) to the tau neutrino’s anomalous magnetic moment (μ_ττ) using an effective field theory framework and the process μ⁻γ → μ⁻ντν̄τ. With full simulation chain (MadGraph, PYTHIA8, DELPHES3, MadAnalysis5) and Asimov significance, it forecasts a 5σ limit of μ_ττ = 5.21×10⁻⁸ μ_B at 30 TeV — improving the DONUT direct limit by ~10×.
AI.motivation: To probe the tau neutrino's electromagnetic properties—specifically its anomalous magnetic moment—which is highly suppressed in the Standard Model and thus a sensitive window for new physics; current experimental constraints (e.g., DONUT) are weak, motivating high-energy, high-luminosity facilities like muon colliders.
AI.method: Model-independent EFT analysis of μ⁻γ → μ⁻ντν̄τ via Equivalent Photon Approximation; event generation with MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, parton showering/hadronization in PYTHIA8, fast detector simulation in DELPHES3, and analysis in MadAnalysis5; optimization of kinematic cuts per collider energy; sensitivity estimation using Asimov significance with 1% systematic uncertainty.
AI.result: Projected 5σ sensitivities: μ_ττ < 5.21×10⁻⁸ μ_B (30 TeV), weaker limits at 10 TeV and 3 TeV; improvement over DONUT’s direct limit (~5×10⁻⁷ μ_B) by one order of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: Future high-energy muon colliders—especially at 30 TeV—offer unprecedented sensitivity to the tau neutrino’s anomalous magnetic moment, establishing them as powerful tools for exploring neutrino electromagnetic interactions beyond the Standard Model.

title: The Role of Completeness in Probing Symmetry Breaking
summary: Completeness is widely recognized in quantum information as an important property of a family of monotones, because it ensures that no information relevant to state conversion is lost. We show that completeness is also physically important in many-body systems: an incomplete measure of symmetry breaking can miss essential features of symmetry-restoration dynamics. We study the logarithmic characteristic function (LCF), also known as the string order parameter, whose full family is complete for exact i.i.d. pure-state conversion under symmetry-preserving operations for finite groups. We introduce a fidelity-based extension of the LCF to mixed states and identify two concrete advantages over entanglement asymmetry (EA). First, for a finite symmetry group $G$, EA is bounded by $\log |G|$ and can approach the same saturated value for different initial states in the thermodynamic limit, making their relaxation curves indistinguishable and preventing the identification of a discrete-symmetry Mpemba effect. By contrast, the LCF can remain extensive, with a coefficient that depends on the initial state and time, and therefore continues to distinguish their relaxation dynamics. Second, different LCF components can exhibit distinct relaxation and crossing behavior, including cases in which EA shows no crossing. We demonstrate these advantages in spin-chain quenches and a single-qubit system under depolarizing noise. We also develop a replica construction for the fidelity-based LCF in quantum field theory and derive analytical results for conformal field theory.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes the physical significance of completeness in symmetry-breaking measures for many-body quantum dynamics, introduces a fidelity-based extension of the logarithmic characteristic function (LCF) to mixed states, and demonstrates its superiority over entanglement asymmetry—particularly in distinguishing relaxation dynamics and revealing Mpemba-like effects and crossing phenomena—validated in spin chains, qubit noise models, and conformal field theory.
AI.motivation: To address the physical limitations of incomplete symmetry-breaking measures (e.g., entanglement asymmetry) in capturing essential features of symmetry-restoration dynamics, especially in distinguishing non-equivalent relaxation behaviors and detecting discrete-symmetry Mpemba effects.
AI.method: Introduces a fidelity-based extension of the logarithmic characteristic function (LCF) to mixed states; analytically compares it with entanglement asymmetry (EA) for finite symmetry groups; analyzes relaxation dynamics, crossing behavior, and extensivity; validates via spin-chain quenches and single-qubit depolarizing noise; develops a replica construction for LCF in QFT and derives analytical CFT results.
AI.result: The fidelity-based LCF remains extensive with state- and time-dependent coefficients, enabling discrimination of otherwise indistinguishable EA relaxation curves and identification of discrete-symmetry Mpemba effects; different LCF components exhibit distinct relaxation and crossing behavior absent in EA; analytical QFT/CFT expressions are derived.
AI.conclusion: Completeness is physically indispensable in symmetry-breaking diagnostics for non-equilibrium quantum dynamics; the fidelity-based LCF provides a more informative, complete, and experimentally accessible measure than EA, particularly for probing fine-grained relaxation structure and universal critical dynamics.

title: Thermodynamic topological classification of magnetically charged slowly rotating Kerr black holes in nonlinear electrodynamics with a cosmological constant
summary: In this work, we investigate the thermodynamic topological classification of slowly rotating Kerr black holes with magnetic charge in nonlinear electrodynamics (NLED) using a reduced grand-canonical off-shell prescription. By constructing the generalized off-shell free energy and the associated topological vector field, we determine the local winding numbers and the global topological charge of the NLED-Kerr black hole in both de Sitter (dS) and anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes. The inverse-temperature curve starts from a finite nonzero value at the lower radial endpoint and diverges at large horizon radius. Together with the single zero of winding number $w=-1$, this behavior identifies the black hole as a realization of the predicted \(\overline{W}^{1-}\) subclass, with global topological number $W=-1$ and a single unstable branch. The classification remains unchanged over the sampled rotation, NLED, and magnetic-charge parameters. Within the same prescription, comparison with the two-branch $W^{0-}$ Kerr-AdS result associates the NLED effective mass function with the changed endpoint behavior and the absence of a stable large-black-hole branch. Thus, the physical novelty is an explicit rotating NLED realization of the predicted \(\overline{W}^{1-}\) subclass for both signs of the cosmological constant.

AI.tldr: This paper classifies slowly rotating magnetic Kerr black holes in nonlinear electrodynamics (NLED) within dS/AdS spacetimes using a grand-canonical off-shell thermodynamic topological approach; it identifies them unambiguously as the ̅W^{1−} subclass (global charge W = −1, single unstable branch), robust across rotation, NLED, and magnetic charge parameters — a novel rotating realization valid for both Λ > 0 and Λ < 0.
AI.motivation: To establish a thermodynamic topological classification for rotating black holes with magnetic charge in nonlinear electrodynamics, extending prior static or non-magnetic classifications and resolving how rotation, NLED, and cosmological constant affect stability structure and topological type.
AI.method: Adopts a reduced grand-canonical off-shell formalism: constructs generalized off-shell free energy and associated topological vector field; computes local winding numbers and global topological charge W from the inverse-temperature curve's endpoint behavior and zeros; compares against known W^{0−} Kerr-AdS topology.
