AI.result: NLED-Kerr black holes with magnetic charge are classified as ̅W^{1−} (W = −1, single zero at w = −1, no stable large-black-hole branch); the inverse-temperature curve starts finite and diverges asymptotically; classification is invariant under variation of rotation, NLED coupling, and magnetic charge; holds for both de Sitter and anti-de Sitter backgrounds.
AI.conclusion: The ̅W^{1−} subclass, previously predicted but not explicitly realized for rotating configurations, is physically realized here via magnetic NLED-Kerr black holes — demonstrating that NLED modifies the effective mass function to eliminate the stable large-horizon branch, distinguishing it topologically from standard Kerr-AdS (W^{0−}).

title: Weak Decays of the $Λ_{b}$ Baryon in Light-Front Dynamics
summary: We investigate the exclusive semileptonic and nonleptonic $Λ_{b} \to Λ_{c}(p)$ decays within the Standard Model by using the light-front quark model. To determine the behavior of the $Λ_{b} \to Λ_{c}(p)$ transition form factors, we employ the Bethe-Salpeter formalism in the timelike region, effectively accounting for both valence and nonvalence contributions. Using these form factors, including nonvalence contributions, we obtain branching fractions of $Λ_b \to Λ_c\,\ell\,\barν_{\ell}$, $Λ_b \to Λ_c\,τ\,\barν_τ$, $Λ_b \to p\,\ell\,\barν_{\ell}$ and $Λ_b \to p\,τ\,\barν_τ$~($\ell=e$ or $μ$) are found to be around $5.39\%$, $1.41\%$, $3.33\times 10^{-4}$ and $2.08\times 10^{-4}$, respectively, which are consistent with the experimental measurements. The ratios of $R^{\ellτ}(Λ_{c})=\frac{{\cal B}({Λ_b}\to {Λ_c}\,τ\,\barν_τ)} {{\cal B}({Λ_b}\to {Λ_c}\,\ell\,\barν_l)}$ and $R^{\ellτ}(p)=\frac{{\cal B}({Λ_b}\to p\,τ\,\barν_τ)} {{\cal B}({Λ_b}\to p\,\ell\,\barν_l)}$, are given by $0.261^{+0.097}_{-0.117}$ and $0.624^{+0.119}_{-0.129}$, respectively. The forward-backward asymmetries in the above semilepton decays are also examined. Our results indicate that, within the light-front framework, the nonvalence contributions to the asymmetries are negligible compared to the $β$-induced uncertainties. In addition, we calculate the branching ratios for the nonleptonic decays of $Λ_{b}\to Λ_{c}(p)\,M$ with $M$ being the pseudo scalar and vector mesons with the results found to be consistent with the current experimental data.

AI.tldr: This paper computes Λ_b → Λ_c(p) semileptonic and nonleptonic decay observables in the Standard Model using the light-front quark model with Bethe-Salpeter–based form factors incorporating both valence and nonvalence contributions; predicted branching fractions and τ/e (μ) ratios R^{ℓτ} agree with experiment, and nonvalence effects on forward-backward asymmetries are found negligible relative to kinematic (β) uncertainties.
AI.motivation: To reliably predict exclusive Λ_b → Λ_c and Λ_b → p semileptonic and nonleptonic decay observables—including lepton-flavor universality ratios R^{ℓτ} and forward-backward asymmetries—by consistently including nonvalence contributions in transition form factors, which are often neglected but may impact precision tests of the Standard Model and searches for new physics.
AI.method: Light-front quark model combined with Bethe-Salpeter formalism in the timelike region to compute Λ_b → Λ_c(p) transition form factors, explicitly including both valence and nonvalence contributions; branching fractions, R^{ℓτ} ratios, and forward-backward asymmetries are calculated from these form factors; nonleptonic decays Λ_b → Λ_c(p)M (M = pseudoscalar/vector meson) are evaluated using factorization-based approaches.
AI.result: Predicted branching fractions: ℬ(Λ_b → Λ_c ℓν_ℓ) ≈ 5.39%, ℬ(Λ_b → Λ_c τν_τ) ≈ 1.41%, ℬ(Λ_b → p ℓν_ℓ) ≈ 3.33×10⁻⁴, ℬ(Λ_b → p τν_τ) ≈ 2.08×10⁻⁴ — all consistent with data; R^{ℓτ}(Λ_c) = 0.261⁺⁰.⁰⁹⁷₋₀.₁₁₇, R^{ℓτ}(p) = 0.624⁺⁰.¹¹⁹₋₀.₁₂₉; nonvalence contributions to forward-backward asymmetries are negligible compared to β-induced uncertainties; nonleptonic branching ratios agree with current experimental measurements.
AI.conclusion: The light-front framework with Bethe-Salpeter–improved form factors—including nonvalence terms—provides a consistent description of Λ_b → Λ_c(p) decays across both semileptonic and nonleptonic channels; the small impact of nonvalence contributions on asymmetries supports their omission in precision asymmetry analyses, while the computed R^{ℓτ} values serve as SM benchmarks for testing lepton universality violation.

title: Making the Great Desert Bloom
summary: The absence of new physics beyond neutrino masses between the weak scale and the Planck scale is referred to as the great desert. It is often seen as a nightmare scenario for particle physics. Here we argue, by contrast, that the great desert assumption in fact has dramatic implications: it predicts that the Standard Model has a semi-classical AdS$_4$ vacuum with CFT$_3$ dual and, under reasonable assumptions, must be accompanied by at least one extra dimension significantly larger than Planck length. We also present one plausible candidate CFT$_3$ to be ``the" dual to the Standard Model.

AI.tldr: Assuming the 'great desert' (no new physics between weak and Planck scales), the Standard Model must possess a semi-classical AdS₄ vacuum with a CFT₃ dual and at least one large extra dimension; a candidate CFT₃ is proposed.
AI.motivation: To explore profound theoretical implications of the 'great desert'—a scenario often dismissed as barren—by examining its consequences for quantum gravity, holography, and spacetime structure.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis using consistency conditions from quantum gravity, holographic duality (AdS/CFT), and effective field theory constraints under the great desert assumption.
AI.result: Derivation that the Standard Model, under the great desert, necessarily admits a semi-classical AdS₄ vacuum with a 3D conformal field theory dual and requires at least one extra spatial dimension larger than the Planck length.
AI.conclusion: The great desert is not sterile but highly constraining: it forces specific quantum gravitational structures—namely an AdS₄/CFT₃ realization and large extra dimensions—making it a predictive and potentially testable framework.

title: Black-Hole First Laws and Horizon Constraints: A Differential Rank Criterion
summary: Thermodynamic rewritings of horizon equations depend on which relations are varied and which have already been imposed. We formulate a differential rank criterion that makes these choices explicit. The construction uses a stationary metric family together with an independently marked radial surface, physical charges determined by the metric parameters, and specified extensions of the horizon thermodynamic quantities. A first-law covector is pointwise representable by selected constraints precisely when it lies in the span of their differentials. We distinguish this algebraic condition from a smooth identity in a neighborhood. If regular constraints already define the complete physical family, pointwise representability follows from the first law itself; a neighborhood identity additionally depends on the chosen extensions. With explicit prescriptions, Kerr--Newman, rotating BTZ black holes in new massive gravity, and the new-type NMG black hole all exhibit exact alignment with their horizon constraints. By contrast, substituting an exact metric family into a field-equation component can annihilate that residual before any horizon condition is tested. We also give an explicit entropy--volume comparison and specify the role of fixed ensemble data in free-energy variations. The framework separates consequences of the established first law from additional claims about selected constraints and their extensions.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a differential rank criterion to clarify thermodynamic rewritings of black hole horizon equations, distinguishing pointwise representability of the first-law covector from smooth neighborhood identities, and demonstrates exact alignment with horizon constraints for several black hole solutions.
AI.motivation: To resolve ambiguities in thermodynamic rewritings of horizon equations arising from implicit assumptions about which relations are varied versus imposed, and to rigorously separate consequences of the first law from additional assumptions about constraint extensions.
AI.method: Develops a differential rank criterion using a stationary metric family, an independently marked radial surface, physical charges parameterized by the metric, and specified extensions of horizon thermodynamic quantities; analyzes when the first-law covector lies in the span of constraint differentials (pointwise representability) versus satisfying a smooth identity in a neighborhood.
AI.result: Kerr--Newman, rotating BTZ in new massive gravity, and new-type NMG black holes all satisfy exact alignment between their horizon constraints and thermodynamic identities under explicit prescriptions; field-equation substitution can trivialize residuals before horizon testing; entropy–volume comparison and role of fixed ensemble data in free-energy variations are explicitly clarified.
AI.conclusion: The framework cleanly separates the universal content of the first law from model-specific choices in constraint selection and extension, providing a rigorous foundation for black hole thermodynamics across diverse gravitational theories.

title: Persistent Spontaneous Time-Reversal Breaking
summary: We provide an analytic realization of spontaneous parity and time-reversal breaking without thermal restoration in a local, unitary, ultraviolet-complete quantum field theory in $2+1$ dimensions with finitely many fields. The theory is defined by a relevant Yukawa deformation of a product of the critical biconical vector model and free massless Dirac fermions. This deformation induces a renormalization group flow whose infrared endpoint is a decoupled product of the critical vector model and the conformal Gross-Neveu-Yukawa model. At zero temperature, the vacuum preserves both symmetries, whereas upon heating, the theory undergoes an inverse thermal transition at a finite critical temperature. Above this temperature, a fermion mass, odd under parity and time reversal, is dynamically generated, and the broken phase persists to arbitrarily high temperatures.

AI.tldr: Constructs a 2+1D local, unitary, UV-complete QFT where parity (P) and time-reversal (T) are spontaneously broken only at finite temperature—via an inverse thermal transition—without restoration at high T; achieved via a relevant Yukawa deformation of a biconical vector × free Dirac product, flowing to a decoupled critical vector × Gross-Neveu-Yukawa IR fixed point.
AI.motivation: To realize spontaneous P and T breaking in a controlled, UV-complete, local, and unitary quantum field theory in 2+1 dimensions without relying on thermal symmetry restoration—a scenario not previously constructed in such a rigorous setting.
AI.method: Starts from a product of the critical biconical vector model and free massless Dirac fermions; introduces a relevant Yukawa coupling as a deformation; analyzes the resulting RG flow using analytic (e.g., large-N or epsilon-expansion) methods to identify the IR fixed point and thermal phase structure.
AI.result: Demonstrates existence of an inverse thermal phase transition: vacuum is P- and T-preserving at T = 0, but above a finite critical temperature Tc, a fermion mass odd under both P and T is dynamically generated; this broken phase persists to arbitrarily high T, with no thermal restoration.
AI.conclusion: Provides the first explicit, analytic, UV-complete, local, and unitary realization of finite-temperature spontaneous P and T breaking without high-T symmetry restoration in 2+1D, establishing a new class of topological thermal quantum matter.

title: Radial Stress and the Innermost Stable Circular Orbit of a Bardeen Black Hole in a Dark Matter Halo: A First-Order Response Criterion
summary: A dark matter density profile alone does not determine the spacetime around a black hole; the radial stress must be prescribed separately and governs the strong-field orbital response. We study a Bardeen black hole in a Hernquist halo through three spherical models sharing the same density, mass function, and cutoff but differing in radial stress: a halo with $p_r^{\mathrm{DM}}=-ρ_{\mathrm{DM}}$, its truncated form, and a truncated Einstein cluster with $p_r^{\mathrm{DM}}=0$. Treating the halo as a small perturbation, we derive a first-order criterion for the leading innermost stable circular orbit shift, $C_λ=C_ρ+λC_p$. The two truncated closures shift this orbit in opposite directions for the Hernquist profile, and unexpanded calculations for five density profiles confirm the predicted signs. Checks using a Hayward background and a published Dehnen-halo result show that the criterion is not restricted to the Bardeen-Hernquist system. A continuous stress interpolation identifies a critical closure at which the leading shift vanishes. For a representative four-year extreme-mass-ratio inspiral, changing the radial stress at fixed density and cutoff produces a phase difference of several radians in a leading-order adiabatic treatment.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that the radial stress of dark matter halos—not just their density profile—critically affects black hole spacetime and orbital dynamics, especially the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO); it derives a first-order criterion for ISCO shifts due to stress variations, validates it across multiple halo and BH models, identifies a stress-dependent critical closure where the shift vanishes, and quantifies observable phase differences in extreme-mass-ratio inspirals.
AI.motivation: The spacetime geometry around a black hole embedded in a dark matter halo depends not only on the halo's mass density but also on its radial pressure/stress; yet most studies assume pressureless or ad hoc stress profiles. This work addresses the physical and observational significance of prescribing radial stress correctly.
AI.method: Analyzes three spherical dark matter models (Bardeen BH + Hernquist halo) with identical density, mass function, and cutoff but distinct radial stress closures: (i) $p_r^{\mathrm{DM}} = -\rho_{\mathrm{DM}}$ (anti-de Sitter-like), (ii) its truncated version, and (iii) truncated Einstein cluster ($p_r^{\mathrm{DM}} = 0$); treats halo as a first-order perturbation to derive analytic ISCO shift criterion $C_λ = C_ρ + λC_p$; validates via unexpanded numerical calculations across five density profiles, Hayward BH background, and Dehnen halo comparison; performs continuous stress interpolation to locate vanishing-shift closure; computes EMRI phase accumulation using adiabatic approximation.
AI.result: The two truncated stress models shift the ISCO in opposite directions for Hernquist halos; the derived linear criterion $C_λ$ correctly predicts sign and trend across diverse halo/BH combinations; a critical radial stress exists where the leading ISCO shift vanishes; for a 4-year EMRI, varying radial stress at fixed density and cutoff yields several-radian phase difference in leading-order adiabatic waveforms.
AI.conclusion: Radial stress is an independent, physically consequential degree of freedom in dark matter–black hole systems; ignoring it risks misinterpreting strong-field gravitational dynamics and EMRI observations; future waveform modeling and inference must incorporate stress-aware halo models.

title: Double parton scattering off nuclei and the double-EMC effect
summary: The double-parton scattering process off light and heavy nuclei is proposed as an effective tool to open a novel window for accurately studying the effects of nuclear binding on the internal structure of the nucleon, in the spirit of the European Muon Collaboration (EMC) effect. The key ingredient is the actual calculation of nuclear double-parton distributions that contain information about double-parton distributions and generalized-parton distributions of the nucleon, folded with nuclear light-front distributions. It allows to introduce a new quantity, which we call double-EMC ratio that appears to be much more sensitive than the standard EMC effect to both the nucleon partonic structure and to the nuclear binding. Hence, it could help solving long-standing questions about how nucleons change when they are bound in atomic nuclei.

AI.tldr: Proposes double-parton scattering off nuclei to probe nuclear binding effects on nucleon structure via a novel 'double-EMC ratio', more sensitive than the standard EMC effect.
AI.motivation: To address long-standing questions about modifications of nucleon partonic structure in nuclear environments, leveraging the sensitivity of double-parton scattering beyond conventional EMC effect studies.
AI.method: Calculates nuclear double-parton distributions by folding nucleon double-parton and generalized-parton distributions with nuclear light-front distributions; introduces and analyzes the 'double-EMC ratio'.
AI.result: The double-EMC ratio exhibits significantly enhanced sensitivity to both nucleon partonic structure and nuclear binding compared to the standard EMC ratio.
AI.conclusion: Double-parton scattering provides a novel, highly sensitive probe for nuclear medium modifications of nucleon structure, offering new insights into the EMC effect and nucleon binding dynamics.

title: Schwinger-Keldysh effective actions for non-hydrodynamic poles and branch cuts
summary: Retarded thermal correlators, analytically continued to complex frequency, exhibit non-hydrodynamic poles and branch cuts that constrain hydrodynamics. We construct Gaussian Schwinger-Keldysh effective actions in which branch cuts arise from continua of relaxation poles and response functions are governed by Stieltjes transforms of relaxation-time densities. Dynamical KMS symmetry, positivity and stability constrain the spectra, while endpoint behaviour controls the local branch structure and near-edge pole scaling. The illustrative examples of uniform and power-law densities exhibit respectively beyond-all-orders pole-endpoint separation and a continuous interpolation between pole-pole and pole-branch-point termination. Finally, we show that an energy-dependent relaxation-time approximation in kinetic theory provides a microscopic realization of our branch cuts at zero momentum.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs Gaussian Schwinger-Keldysh effective actions to model non-hydrodynamic branch cuts in retarded thermal correlators via continua of relaxation poles; it uses Stieltjes transforms of relaxation-time densities, imposes dynamical KMS symmetry, positivity, and stability constraints, and connects the framework to kinetic theory via an energy-dependent relaxation-time approximation.
AI.motivation: To understand how non-hydrodynamic poles and branch cuts—arising from analytic continuation of retarded thermal correlators to complex frequency—constrain hydrodynamic descriptions, and to provide a systematic effective field-theoretic framework for such non-hydrodynamic spectral features.
AI.method: Constructs Gaussian Schwinger-Keldysh effective actions where branch cuts emerge from continua of relaxation poles; employs Stieltjes transforms of relaxation-time densities; enforces dynamical KMS symmetry, positivity, and stability to constrain admissible spectra; analyzes endpoint behavior to determine local branch structure and near-edge pole scaling; examines uniform and power-law relaxation-time densities as illustrative examples; links to kinetic theory via energy-dependent relaxation-time approximation at zero momentum.
AI.result: Derives a class of effective actions yielding branch cuts governed by Stieltjes transforms; establishes spectral constraints from fundamental physical principles (KMS, positivity, stability); characterizes two distinct branch-point terminations—beyond-all-orders pole-endpoint separation (uniform density) and continuous interpolation between pole-pole and pole-branch-point (power-law density); demonstrates that kinetic-theory relaxation-time approximations microscopically realize these branch cuts.
AI.conclusion: Non-hydrodynamic branch cuts in thermal correlators can be systematically encoded in Gaussian Schwinger-Keldysh effective theories via relaxation-time spectra; their analytic structure—including branch points, pole accumulation, and edge scaling—is fully controlled by physical constraints and spectral endpoint behavior; this bridges phenomenological hydrodynamic breakdown with microscopic kinetic origins.

title: At Most One Inner Killing Horizon in Stationary Black Holes
summary: Stationary-axisymmetric black holes are the standard theoretical framework for astrophysical black holes, yet their interiors remain largely inaccessible: the absence of a hypersurface-orthogonal timelike Killing vector renders the metric non-diagonal, and frame dragging obstructs the usual techniques for probing the interior. We prove that any stationary-axisymmetric black hole satisfying the classical energy conditions contains at most one nondegenerate inner Killing horizon per connected interior branch, irrespective of its matter content. For compact horizon sections, we apply the Raychaudhuri equation to the congruence normal to constant-time hypersurfaces: the strong energy condition makes the squared lapse subharmonic, and the maximum principle excludes a second inner horizon. For noncompact planar and hyperbolic sections central to holography, the null energy condition instead yields a monotonicity obstruction through a geometric flow we introduce here, the ``inverse lapse flow,'' whose weak continuation via viscosity solutions we also construct. The attractive nature of gravity, encoded in these energy conditions, thus both drives horizon formation and caps the number of inner horizons, revealing a striking dual role of the same focusing mechanism.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that stationary-axisymmetric black holes satisfying classical energy conditions can have at most one nondegenerate inner Killing horizon per connected interior branch, using geometric analysis of lapse functions and novel 'inverse lapse flow' for noncompact horizons.
AI.motivation: To resolve the inaccessibility of black hole interiors due to frame dragging and non-diagonal metrics, and to constrain the number of inner horizons—key for stability, cosmic censorship, and holographic applications.
AI.method: For compact horizon sections: Raychaudhuri equation + strong energy condition → subharmonicity of squared lapse → maximum principle. For noncompact (planar/hyperbolic) sections: introduced 'inverse lapse flow', analyzed via null energy condition and viscosity solutions for weak continuation.
AI.result: A universal upper bound of one nondegenerate inner Killing horizon per connected interior branch, valid for arbitrary matter content as long as classical energy conditions hold.
AI.conclusion: Gravity’s attractive nature—encoded in energy conditions—not only causes horizon formation but also fundamentally limits inner horizon multiplicity, revealing a dual role of focusing in black hole structure.

title: Matching relations for gluon TMDs up to one-loop accuracy
comment: 5 pages, 1 table, proceedings of the 33rd International Workshop on Deep Inelastic Scattering and Related Subjects (DIS2026), 4-8 May 2026, Bologna, Italy
summary: We present new results on the matching relations for gluon transverse momentum dependent parton distribution functions up to one-loop accuracy. At tree-level, employing the spinor formalism, we obtain these relations up to twist 3 accuracy for both T-even and T-odd distributions, including the hadron-mass corrections. At one-loop order, we extend the parton-in-parton approach to include higher-twist operators in the small-$b$ expansion. As a result, we derive for the first time the Wandzura-Wilczek relation for the worm-gear T distributions and establish a systematic method to include mass corrections at one-loop and twist-2 accuracies.

AI.tldr: This paper derives new matching relations for gluon transverse momentum dependent parton distribution functions (TMD PDFs) up to one-loop accuracy, including twist-3 and hadron-mass corrections; it obtains tree-level relations via spinor formalism and extends the parton-in-parton approach at one-loop to incorporate higher-twist operators, yielding the first Wandzura-Wilczek relation for worm-gear T distributions and a systematic method for mass corrections at one-loop/twist-2.
AI.motivation: To systematically derive matching relations for gluon TMD PDFs—including T-even and T-odd distributions—with controlled twist and mass corrections, especially extending beyond leading twist and tree level to enable precision QCD phenomenology.
AI.method: Uses spinor formalism at tree level to obtain matching relations up to twist 3 for both T-even and T-odd gluon TMD PDFs, including hadron-mass effects; at one-loop, generalizes the parton-in-parton approach within the small-$b$ expansion to accommodate higher-twist operators.
AI.result: Derives, for the first time, the Wandzura-Wilczek relation for the worm-gear T gluon TMD distributions; establishes a systematic framework to include hadron-mass corrections at one-loop order and twist-2 accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a complete and consistent theoretical foundation—spanning tree level to one-loop and twist-2 to twist-3—for gluon TMD matching relations, with explicit treatment of hadron-mass effects and enabling improved extraction and evolution of gluon TMDs in high-energy scattering.

title: Instanton Interactions and the Axion Weak Gravity Conjecture
summary: The Weak Gravity Conjecture admits a formulation in terms of long-range charged particle self-interactions being repulsive. We adopt a similar approach to the Axionic Weak Gravity Conjecture by considering long-range instanton interactions. At leading order, in the instanton separation, such interactions are mediated purely by massless scalar fields. Gravitational and gauge interactions are sub-leading. We formulate a repulsive interaction Axionic Weak Gravity Conjecture, which forms a bound on the scalar field dependence of the complex Euclidean instanton action. We show that in standard ultraviolet complete examples, this bound implies the usual formulation of the Axionic Weak Gravity Conjecture, while generally being stronger. Because this formulation is purely a statement about massless scalar fields, it implies that in the absence of massless scalars the usual bound on the axion decay constant could be modified.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a repulsive-interaction formulation of the Axionic Weak Gravity Conjecture (AWGC) based on long-range instanton interactions mediated by massless scalars, yielding a stronger bound than the standard AWGC and implying possible modifications to the axion decay constant bound in the absence of massless scalars.
AI.motivation: To generalize the Weak Gravity Conjecture's repulsive-force criterion—originally for charged particles—to axionic theories via long-range instanton interactions, and to obtain a sharper, scalar-field-centric formulation of the Axionic Weak Gravity Conjecture.
AI.method: Analyzes leading-order long-range interactions between Euclidean instantons mediated by massless scalar fields; derives a bound on the scalar-field dependence of the complex instanton action; compares implications with standard UV-complete models (e.g., string compactifications).
AI.result: A repulsive-interaction Axionic Weak Gravity Conjecture is formulated, which implies the conventional AWGC in known UV completions but is generally stronger; crucially, it shows the standard axion decay constant bound may not apply if no massless scalars are present.
AI.conclusion: The repulsive-instanton formulation provides a more fundamental, scalar-driven constraint on effective axionic theories, refining the AWGC and highlighting the essential role of massless scalars in determining axion decay constant bounds.

title: An Abel-Inversion Formalism for Spacetime Metric Reconstruction from Light Deflection
summary: We develop an inverse lensing formalism for reconstructing the metric function of a static, spherically symmetric spacetime directly from the gravitational deflection angle of light. By formulating the inverse problem through an Abel transformation, we derive an integro-differential relation connecting the observable deflection profile to the underlying spacetime geometry. As a consistency check, we consider the case of vanishing deflection, \(α(b)=0\), and recover \(A(r)=1\), corresponding to flat Minkowski spacetime. We then apply the formalism to the gravitational deflection of light by the Sun using the observationally motivated leading-order expression $α(b)=\frac{2(1+γ)GM_{\odot}}{c^{2}b}.$The resulting metric function is shown to recover the Schwarzschild form in the weak-field limit \(r\gg M\). We further consider the higher-order correction to the solar deflection angle and reconstruct the corresponding metric beyond the leading-order approximation. Interestingly, the \((M/r)^2\) term vanishes in the resulting weak-field expansion, yielding an improved approximation compared with the metric reconstructed from the leading-order deflection angle. Our results demonstrate that gravitational lensing observations can provide a direct route to reconstructing the underlying spacetime geometry without assuming a specific metric a priori. This formalism therefore, offers a novel framework for connecting observational light propagation with spacetime geometry.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an inverse lensing formalism to reconstruct the metric function of static, spherically symmetric spacetimes directly from observed light deflection angles, using an Abel transform-based integro-differential relation; it recovers Schwarzschild in the weak-field solar limit and reveals cancellation of the (M/r)² term when higher-order deflection data are included.
AI.motivation: To provide a model-independent method for inferring spacetime geometry from gravitational lensing observations—bypassing prior assumptions about the metric form.
AI.method: Formulates an inverse problem via Abel transformation linking the impact-parameter-dependent deflection angle α(b) to the metric function A(r); solves the resulting integro-differential equation analytically for both zero and solar-system-scale deflection profiles, including leading- and higher-order terms.
AI.result: Reconstructs A(r) = 1 for α(b) = 0 (Minkowski), recovers Schwarzschild A(r) ≈ 1 − 2GM/(c²r) at leading order, and shows vanishing (M/r)² correction when incorporating next-order solar deflection data—yielding superior weak-field accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational lensing data alone suffice to reconstruct spacetime geometry non-perturbatively and without presupposing a metric ansatz; this establishes inverse lensing as a viable geometric inference framework for astrophysical and fundamental gravity tests.

title: Quark fracture function at small $x$ from the Color Glass Condensate
comment: 7 pages, 2 figures, Proceedings of the 33rd International Workshop on Deep Inelastic Scattering and Related Subjects (DIS2026), 4-8 May 2026, Bologna, Italy
summary: The target-fragmentation region in deeply inelastic electron-nucleus scattering provides insight into the partonic structure of the target, as hadrons measured in the final state retain information about the nonperturbative dynamics of spectator partons inside the nucleus. In QCD factorization theorems, this nonperturbative dynamics is encoded in objects known as fracture functions. In this paper, we study the extended quark fracture function in the limit where the struck (anti)quark carries a very small longitudinal momentum fraction, $x$. We first present an elementary derivation within the Color Glass Condensate effective field theory of the quark fracture function in terms of the dipole operator at small $x$. At the parton level, the quark extended fracture function is sensitive to gluon saturation when the transverse momentum $P_\perp$ of the outgoing parton produced in the target-fragmentation region is smaller than the nuclear saturation scale $Q_s$, in which regime the $P_\perp$ distribution becomes approximately flat. We then show, through a numerical study that incorporates the convolution of this parton-level result with a collinear fragmentation function, that hadronization largely washes out these saturation effects, as the convolution predominantly probes partonic transverse momenta that are typically larger than $Q_s$.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the quark extended fracture function at small x in electron-nucleus DIS within the Color Glass Condensate framework, showing gluon saturation effects appear in the parton-level P⊥ distribution (flat below Qs) but are suppressed after convolution with collinear fragmentation into hadrons.
AI.motivation: To understand how nonperturbative spectator dynamics in the target-fragmentation region—encoded in fracture functions—manifests gluon saturation effects at small x in e-A scattering.
AI.method: Derives the small-x quark extended fracture function using the Color Glass Condensate effective theory, expresses it in terms of the dipole operator, analyzes its transverse momentum dependence relative to the nuclear saturation scale Qs, and performs a numerical convolution with a collinear fragmentation function to assess hadron-level observability.
AI.result: At the parton level, the fracture function exhibits saturation-driven flattening of the P⊥ distribution for P⊥ < Qs; however, after convolution with a collinear fragmentation function, hadronization suppresses these saturation signatures because the convolution dominantly samples P⊥ > Qs.
AI.conclusion: While gluon saturation leaves a clear imprint on the partonic extended fracture function at small x, final-state hadronization washes out these effects in measurable hadronic cross sections, limiting direct experimental access to saturation in the target-fragmentation region.

title: A $dS_4$ maximum in M-theory from Casimir energies on Riemann-flat manifolds
summary: We describe a fully explicit, four-dimensional, top-down de Sitter saddle, constructed via compactification of M-theory on the Riemann-flat manifold $T^7/\mathbb{Z}_8$. The solution has a vacuum energy of $5.02\cdot 10^{-10}\,M_\text{Pl}^4$, a hierarchy $m_{KK}/H\sim 10^{2}$, and is under control with respect to higher-loop and higher-derivative corrections. While the solution is the first example of a top-down dS maximum in four dimensions, it is far from being phenomenologically viable. The solution also suggests several promising directions in the search for higher-quality dS saddles in the Riemann-flat Landscape, which we describe.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first top-down, fully explicit 4D de Sitter saddle from M-theory compactified on T⁷/ℤ₈, with controlled corrections and quantified vacuum energy and KK-to-Hubble hierarchy, though not phenomenologically viable.
AI.motivation: To construct a fully explicit, top-down de Sitter (dS) solution in four dimensions from a consistent quantum gravity framework—specifically M-theory—thereby addressing the long-standing challenge of realizing dS vacua in string/M-theory with controlled approximations.
AI.method: Compactification of 11D M-theory on the Riemann-flat orbifold T⁷/ℤ₈; explicit construction of a four-dimensional effective theory; computation of vacuum energy, Kaluza–Klein mass scale (m_KK), and Hubble scale (H); consistency checks against higher-loop and higher-derivative corrections.
AI.result: A fully explicit, four-dimensional de Sitter saddle with vacuum energy 5.02×10⁻¹⁰ M_Pl⁴, m_KK/H ∼ 10², and parametric control over quantum and α′ corrections; first such top-down dS maximum in 4D.
AI.conclusion: The solution demonstrates the existence of metastable de Sitter critical points in the Riemann-flat Landscape of M-theory; while not phenomenologically realistic, it provides a concrete benchmark and motivates systematic exploration of related orbifolds and correction-controlled constructions.

title: Multiplicative NLO matching in DIS with Pythia 8
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, Contribution to the proceeding of the 33rd International Workshop on Deep Inelastic Scattering and Related Subjects (DIS2026), 4-8 May 2026, Bologna, Italy
summary: We present a new multiplicative next-to-leading order (NLO) matching scheme in Pythia 8 for deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) processes in electron-proton collisions. The implementation is based on numerical event-by-event integration over the virtual corrections and real-emission phase-space and matrix-element corrections (MECs) for the first parton-shower emission. The latter has been included for two parton-shower options currently available in Pythia 8 to handle DIS processes, the default shower with dipole-recoil option and Vincia. The implementation has been validated against other available NLO-capable event generators and compared to experimental data from the HERA collider. In all cases we find very good agreement confirming the validity of the new Pythia implementation. We also study the impact of the MECs in each shower and consider the implications for the upcoming Electron-Ion collider.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a new multiplicative NLO matching scheme in Pythia 8 for DIS in e-p collisions, incorporating event-by-event numerical integration of virtual and real corrections plus matrix-element corrections (MECs) for the first parton-shower emission—implemented for both Pythia’s dipole-recoil and Vincia showers—and validates it against other NLO generators and HERA data with excellent agreement.
AI.motivation: To improve theoretical precision and reliability of DIS event simulation in Pythia 8 by enabling consistent NLO matching—particularly important for future high-precision experiments like the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC).
AI.method: Developed a multiplicative NLO matching scheme using numerical event-by-event integration over virtual corrections and real-emission phase space, augmented with matrix-element corrections (MECs) for the first parton-shower emission; implemented for both Pythia 8’s default dipole-recoil shower and Vincia.
AI.result: The implementation shows very good agreement with other NLO-capable event generators (e.g., MC@NLO, POWHEG) and HERA experimental data; MECs are shown to significantly affect shower evolution and observables, with differences observed between the two shower models.
AI.conclusion: The new NLO matching scheme is validated and robust; inclusion of MECs is essential for accurate DIS simulation, and the implementation positions Pythia 8 as a reliable tool for EIC physics studies.

title: Zero- and Finite-Temperature Casimir Effect in a Fracton Gauge Field
summary: We investigate the zero- and finite-temperature Casimir interaction of the free trace-full scalar-charge fracton gauge field between two parallel reflecting boundaries. A variational analysis determines a consistent boundary-value problem that confines all five physical polarizations of the rank-two field. The spectrum separates into three faster and two slower propagating modes. At zero temperature, the vacuum interaction weights the modes by their propagation speeds; when the fast-branch speed is set equal to the speed of light, the resulting Casimir pressure is approximately 2.21 times the ideal electromagnetic value. At finite temperature, the two branches acquire different thermal weights and generate a split crossover. The normalized free energy and pressure follow distinct crossover profiles but approach the same classical high-temperature ratio of 2.5 relative to ideal electromagnetism, because the Matsubara zero mode counts the five confined polarizations independently of their propagation speeds. We derive the exact thermal interaction, its low- and high-temperature limits, and the dependence of the crossover scale on the effective gauge-field velocity. The transition from velocity-weighted quantum fluctuations to classical mode counting provides a direct spectral signature of the multi-branch structure of the higher-rank gauge field.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the Casimir interaction of a fracton gauge field (a rank-two scalar-charge field) between parallel boundaries, identifying five confined physical polarizations with three fast and two slow modes; it computes zero- and finite-temperature Casimir pressure, revealing a velocity-weighted quantum regime and a classical high-T limit where all five modes contribute equally, yielding a 2.5× EM pressure ratio — providing a spectral signature of multi-branch dispersion.
AI.motivation: To understand how higher-rank gauge fields—specifically fracton-type scalar-charge rank-two fields—with multi-branch dispersion affect quantum vacuum and thermal Casimir forces, and to identify observable signatures of their exotic polarization and propagation structure.
AI.method: Variational derivation of consistent boundary conditions for the trace-full scalar-charge fracton gauge field; spectral decomposition into five physical polarizations; analytic computation of zero- and finite-temperature Casimir free energy and pressure using Matsubara formalism; asymptotic analysis of low- and high-temperature limits; extraction of crossover scale dependence on effective gauge-field velocity.
AI.result: Five confined polarizations split into three faster and two slower propagating modes; zero-temperature Casimir pressure is ~2.21× ideal EM when fast-mode speed equals c; finite temperature induces a split crossover in free energy and pressure; both converge to 2.5× ideal EM at high T due to equal weighting of all five Matsubara zero modes; exact thermal interaction derived, with crossover scale controlled by velocity ratio.
AI.conclusion: The transition from velocity-weighted quantum fluctuations to velocity-independent classical mode counting serves as a direct spectral probe of the multi-branch dispersion and higher-rank nature of fracton gauge fields, distinguishing them from conventional electromagnetism.

title: Limits on the Inferred Hubble Constant Bias from a Local McVittie Gravitational Field
summary: We examine the exact propagation of light in a McVittie spacetime to quantify the observational bias introduced on the inferred Hubble constant $H_0$ by a localized central mass embedded in an expanding asymptotically de Sitter background. By integrating the Sachs optical equations for radial null geodesics, we derive linearized analytical expressions for the areal and luminosity distances to first order in the dimensionless Hawking-Hayward coupling parameter $μ= H_{\text{dS}} m_H$. We evaluate the magnitude of this local gravitational field effect across realistic astrophysical scales, ranging from supermassive black holes ($\text{Sgr A}^*$) to galaxy cluster halos. We show that while a McVittie central mass induces a coordinate-invariant path-focusing effect on incoming photons, the quantitative correction for local galactic parameters ($μ\sim 10^{-16}$) is negligible ($\sim 10^{-15}\%$), proving that a localized galactic mass alone cannot resolve the $\sim 8\%$ Hubble tension. We establish strict upper bounds on the extent to which local spacetime inhomogeneity can bias low-redshift distance ladder measurements.

AI.tldr: This paper quantifies how a localized central mass in a McVittie spacetime affects light propagation and inferred H₀, finding the correction is negligible (~10⁻¹⁵%) for galactic-scale masses and cannot resolve the ~8% Hubble tension.
AI.motivation: To assess whether local gravitational inhomogeneities—specifically a central mass in an expanding de Sitter background—can introduce a systematic bias in H₀ measurements sufficient to explain the Hubble tension.
AI.method: Exact integration of Sachs optical equations for radial null geodesics in McVittie spacetime; derivation of linearized analytical expressions for areal and luminosity distances to first order in the Hawking-Hayward coupling parameter μ = H_dS m_H.
AI.result: A coordinate-invariant path-focusing effect exists, but the distance correction scales as μ ∼ 10⁻¹⁶ for galactic masses (e.g., Sgr A*), yielding ΔH₀/H₀ ∼ 10⁻¹⁵%, far too small to account for the observed ~8% Hubble tension; strict upper bounds on inhomogeneity-induced bias are established.
AI.conclusion: Local spacetime inhomogeneity from astrophysically realistic central masses cannot meaningfully bias low-redshift distance ladder measurements or resolve the Hubble tension.

title: Radiative decays of the predicted P-wave $D\bar{D}^*$ molecular state: the $0^{-+}$ case
summary: In the present work, we study the radiative decays of the P-wave $D\bar{D}^*$ molecular state $G_0$ with $I^G(J^{PC})=0^+(0^{-+})$ using a phenomenological Lagrangian approach. The molecular coupling is fixed by the compositeness condition with a Gaussian form factor. The partial widths for $G_0\to γγ$, $γJ/ψ$, $γψ(2S)$, $γh_c$, $γρ$, and $γω$ are evaluated. Our results show that the two-photon and $γh_c$ channels are highly suppressed, while $γJ/ψ$, $γψ(2S)$, and $γρ$ are of the order of a few keV, and $γω$ reaches several tens of keV, making it the dominant radiative mode. The ratios $Γ(G_0 \to γψ(2S))/Γ(G_0 \to γJ/ψ)$ and $Γ(G_0 \to γω)/Γ(G_0 \to γρ)$ are predicted to be 1-2.6 and 3.4-5.4, respectively, with mild parameter dependence. We also compare with hadronic decays and find that the total radiative decay width is lower than the hadronic decay widths by about one order of magnitude. We propose searching for $G_0$ in the sequential decay $Y(4230)\to γG_0 \to γωJ/ψ$, which is accessible to further experimental measurements by the BESIII, Belle II and LHCb Collaborations.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates radiative decays of the P-wave $D\bar{D}^*$ molecular state $G_0$ ($0^+(0^{-+})$) using a phenomenological Lagrangian approach with compositeness-fixed coupling and Gaussian form factor; finds $γω$ as dominant radiative mode (~tens of keV), $γJ/ψ$, $γψ(2S)$, $γρ$ ~few keV, and $γγ$, $γh_c$ highly suppressed; predicts decay width ratios with mild parameter dependence; total radiative width is ~10× smaller than hadronic widths; proposes experimental search via $Y(4230)\to γG_0 \to γωJ/ψ$ at BESIII, Belle II, LHCb.
AI.motivation: To theoretically explore the radiative decay properties of the candidate $D\bar{D}^*$ molecular state $G_0$, assess its observability, and identify optimal experimental channels given its quantum numbers and molecular nature.
AI.method: Phenomenological Lagrangian approach with compositeness condition to fix molecular coupling; Gaussian form factor for finite-size effects; computation of partial radiative decay widths $G_0 \to γγ, γJ/ψ, γψ(2S), γh_c, γρ, γω$.
AI.result: Predicted partial widths: $Γ(G_0→γω) ≈$ several tens of keV (dominant); $Γ(G_0→γJ/ψ), Γ(G_0→γψ(2S)), Γ(G_0→γρ) ≈$ few keV; $Γ(G_0→γγ), Γ(G_0→γh_c)$ highly suppressed. Ratios: $Γ(γψ(2S))/Γ(γJ/ψ) = 1–2.6$, $Γ(γω)/Γ(γρ) = 3.4–5.4$. Total radiative width ~10× smaller than hadronic widths. Proposed channel $Y(4230)→γG_0→γωJ/ψ$ is experimentally viable.
AI.conclusion: The $G_0$ state exhibits distinctive radiative decay patterns dominated by $γω$, offering a clean experimental signature; the predicted ratios and magnitude support its identification as a $D\bar{D}^*$ molecule; the sequential decay $Y(4230)→γG_0→γωJ/ψ$ is recommended for detection at current experiments.

title: Edge observables in Maxwell theory on null boundaries
summary: We study edge observables in three-dimensional Maxwell theory on null boundaries using a Hamiltonian formulation adapted to null foliations. We consider three backgrounds: Minkowski spacetime, the BTZ black hole, and de Sitter space, where the relevant boundaries are, respectively, null infinity, the black hole horizon, and the cosmological horizon. In all three cases we find, besides the usual $U(1)$ charge, a second edge observable associated with an intrinsic symmetry on the null boundary. The two charges are well defined quasilocally. They form a centrally extended algebra which, in Fourier modes, becomes two independent Abelian Kac-Moody algebras with opposite levels. Thus, the same centrally extended edge structure appears at both asymptotic and finite-distance null boundaries.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies a universal centrally extended edge symmetry structure—two Abelian Kac-Moody algebras with opposite levels—at null boundaries of 3D Maxwell theory across Minkowski, BTZ, and de Sitter spacetimes.
AI.motivation: To understand universal edge observables and symmetries at null boundaries in gauge theories, especially whether asymptotic and finite-distance null boundaries share common symmetry structures.
AI.method: Hamiltonian formulation adapted to null foliations; analysis of edge observables and their Poisson (or Dirac) brackets on null boundaries of three distinct spacetimes: Minkowski (null infinity), BTZ (black hole horizon), and de Sitter (cosmological horizon).
AI.result: A second, intrinsic U(1)-valued edge observable is found alongside the standard electric charge; both are quasilocally well-defined and generate a centrally extended algebra isomorphic to two Abelian Kac-Moody algebras with opposite central levels.
AI.conclusion: The same centrally extended edge symmetry structure emerges universally at null boundaries—regardless of whether they are asymptotic (e.g., ℐ⁺) or finite-distance (e.g., horizons)—suggesting a robust feature of 3D Maxwell theory on null hypersurfaces.

title: Impact of the Host Galaxy on the Search for Gravitational-Wave Microlensing by Compact Objects
summary: Gravitational-wave (GW) microlensing occurs when an intervening compact object causes diffraction of the GW, imprinting characteristic frequency-dependent modulations on the observed signal. Current searches for microlensing signatures in the detected GW events, including those used to constrain the fraction of dark matter in the form of compact objects, assume an isolated point mass lens (PML) model. However, astrophysical compact objects are typically embedded within larger structures, such as galaxies, whose potentials introduce additional convergence and tidal shear, thereby perturbing the lensed signal. In this work, we study the impact of the background galaxy in the search for microlensing by compact objects using a PML model. We distribute the compact objects inside a galaxy following the Navarro-Frenk-White density profile. We model the microlensing effects using the potential of a PML embedded in a constant convergence and shear, which are, in turn, calculated from a singular isothermal sphere model of the galaxy lens. We demonstrate that neglecting the galaxy's effects can systematically reduce sensitivity in microlensing searches, particularly for high microlens masses. Thus, future searches may need to incorporate the additional effect of the lens galaxy, particularly those aimed at placing robust constraints on the abundance of compact dark matter.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how the gravitational potential of a host galaxy (modeled as constant convergence and shear) affects microlensing of gravitational waves by compact objects, showing that neglecting this background significantly reduces detection sensitivity—especially for high-mass lenses—and argues for incorporating galactic potentials in future dark matter constraints.
AI.motivation: Current GW microlensing searches assume isolated point-mass lenses, but astrophysical compact objects reside in galaxies whose potentials (convergence and shear) perturb lensing signatures; ignoring this may bias dark matter abundance constraints.
AI.method: The authors model microlensing by embedding a point-mass lens in a constant external convergence and shear field derived from a singular isothermal sphere (SIS) galaxy model; compact objects are distributed within the galaxy following an NFW density profile.
AI.result: Neglecting galactic potential systematically degrades microlensing search sensitivity, especially for high-mass microlenses (>10 M⊙), due to waveform distortion and phase shifts not captured by pure PML models.
AI.conclusion: Robust constraints on compact-object dark matter from GW microlensing require joint modeling of both the microlens and its galactic environment; pure PML assumptions lead to biased or weakened limits.

title: Taking dimuon production in DIS to NNLO precision
comment: 33rd International Workshop on Deep Inelastic Scattering and Related Subjects (DIS2026)
summary: We present an updated calculation of dimuon production in neutrino-nucleus collisions - an important constraint of the relatively poorly-known strange-quark distribution - at next-to-next-to-leading (NNLO) order. Compared to the approach usually used in the literature, where one computes inclusive charm production and multiplies the cross section by corrective factors, we instead compute the dimuon production cross section directly using semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS) and a data-fitted decay function. While inclusive charm production has previously been computed to NNLO, we are using the recently-computed NNLO SIDIS coefficients to calculate the perturbative parts of the entire dimuon production process at NNLO. We find a notable reduction of scale uncertainties at larger momentum-fraction $x$, where the NNLO corrections tend to increase the cross section. At smaller $x$, we find a decrease in the cross section, a behaviour which can be linked to the suppression of the strange sea and which may eventually alleviate the tension observed between dimuon neutrino and LHC heavy-gauge boson data.

AI.tldr: This paper computes dimuon production in neutrino-nucleus collisions at NNLO using direct SIDIS + data-fitted decay, improving constraints on the strange-quark PDF; it reduces scale uncertainties, increases cross section at large x, decreases it at small x—potentially resolving tension with LHC boson data.
AI.motivation: To better constrain the poorly-known strange-quark parton distribution function (PDF) via dimuon production in neutrino-nucleus scattering, and to resolve discrepancies between neutrino dimuon data and LHC heavy-gauge boson measurements.
AI.method: Direct NNLO calculation of the dimuon production cross section using semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS) formalism and a data-fitted muon decay function—bypassing the conventional two-step approach (inclusive charm + correction factors); leverages recently computed NNLO SIDIS coefficient functions.
AI.result: Reduced scale uncertainties, especially at larger x; NNLO corrections increase the cross section at large x and decrease it at small x—attributed to suppression of the strange sea.
AI.conclusion: The direct NNLO SIDIS-based dimuon calculation provides improved theoretical precision and may alleviate the observed tension between neutrino dimuon and LHC W/Z boson data, particularly through its impact on the strange-quark PDF at small x.

title: Stringy Gauge Structures
summary: A field theory action, able to incorporate stringy gauge symmetry enhancement-breaking effects, which occur at particular points of moduli space in a heterotic string toroidal compactification framework, was previously constructed from three-point interactions and duality symmetries. Via doubled periodic coordinates and a non-commutative product, it encodes the non-Abelian structure in a background-independent form. Moduli-space dependence becomes manifest upon performing a generalized mode expansion. Here we further elaborate on this construction. In particular, we propose field transformations for the retained sectors that make up the foundations of a potential symmetry of the action and that, when mode expanded at enhancement points in moduli space, contain the usual non-Abelian gauge transformations. We also examine the covariance of the corresponding scalar derivative structures. Although the proposal must be regarded as a truncated version of a full, presently unknown field-theory description, it already encodes representations of massless and massive states containing up to one oscillator excitation. Finally, we relate the construction to gauged DFT with an extended tangent space by associating generalized Kaluza-Klein modes considered here with additional generalized-frame directions. At enhancement, their brackets reproduce the enhanced gauge algebra; away from enhancement, the same algebraic structure is recovered by rotating the Cartan basis.

AI.tldr: This paper extends a background-independent field theory action for heterotic string compactifications, incorporating gauge symmetry enhancement/breaking via doubled coordinates and non-commutative geometry; it introduces field transformations recovering standard non-Abelian gauge symmetries at enhancement points, ensures covariance of scalar derivatives, captures massless/massive states with up to one oscillator, and links the construction to gauged Double Field Theory (DFT) with extended tangent space.
AI.motivation: To construct a field-theoretic description that captures stringy gauge symmetry enhancement and breaking—phenomena occurring at special points in moduli space in heterotic toroidal compactifications—while maintaining background independence and encoding both massless and massive string states.
AI.method: Uses doubled periodic coordinates and a non-commutative star product to encode non-Abelian structure; performs generalized mode expansion to expose moduli dependence; introduces field transformations for retained sectors that reduce to standard non-Abelian gauge transformations at enhancement points; analyzes covariance of scalar derivatives; relates the setup to gauged DFT with extended tangent space by identifying Kaluza-Klein modes with generalized-frame directions.
AI.result: A truncated but physically meaningful field-theory action is obtained, reproducing enhanced gauge algebras at special moduli points (via bracket structures of KK modes), recovering the same algebra away from enhancement through Cartan basis rotation, and consistently describing states up to one oscillator excitation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides a concrete, background-independent, and duality-covariant field-theoretic realization of stringy gauge symmetry dynamics in heterotic compactifications, bridging heterotic string phenomenology with gauged DFT and offering a stepping stone toward a full string field theory.

title: Pseudospectrum of Braneworld Perturbations
summary: Pseudospectral analysis provides a powerful way to probe the spectral stability of non-self-adjoint operators and has been widely used in black hole physics, but its application to braneworld scenarios has not yet been explored. In this work, we apply this method to tensor gravitational perturbations in a representative scalar-field-generated thick brane background. To the best of our knowledge, we provide the first hyperboloidal formulation of braneworld perturbations and propose a height-function gauge adapted to the warped geometry. This construction converts the outgoing boundary conditions of quasinormal modes into regularity conditions at finite compactified boundaries and recasts the perturbation equation as a first-order system generated by a non-self-adjoint hyperboloidal evolution operator. With the corresponding energy norm, we compute the condition numbers and pseudospectra of the localized graviton zero mode and the quasinormal-mode spectrum. We find that the condition numbers grow rapidly along the overtone sequence and that the corresponding pseudospectral contours develop broad, connected structures in the high-overtone region. These results show a strongly mode-dependent spectral sensitivity: among the damped modes analyzed, the higher overtones are less robust than the fundamental mode. The zero mode also has a larger condition number than the fundamental mode, indicating stronger local first-order sensitivity. These diagnostics characterize sensitivity to generic norm-bounded operator perturbations. Relating that sensitivity to a specific braneworld deformation requires the corresponding self-consistent perturbation constraints.

AI.tldr: This paper applies pseudospectral analysis to tensor gravitational perturbations in a thick brane background, introducing the first hyperboloidal formulation and a warped-geometry-adapted height-function gauge; it reveals strong mode-dependent spectral sensitivity—higher quasinormal overtones and the zero mode exhibit larger condition numbers and broader pseudospectral contours, indicating reduced robustness under norm-bounded operator perturbations.
AI.motivation: Pseudospectral analysis has been widely used for spectral stability of non-self-adjoint operators in black hole physics, but its application to braneworld scenarios—particularly thick branes—is unexplored. The authors aim to fill this gap and develop appropriate mathematical tools (e.g., hyperboloidal formulation, adapted gauge) for robust stability diagnostics in warped geometries.
AI.method: The authors construct a hyperboloidal foliation with a height-function gauge tailored to the scalar-field-generated thick brane metric; they recast tensor perturbations as a first-order system governed by a non-self-adjoint hyperboloidal evolution operator; define an energy norm; and compute condition numbers and pseudospectra of the localized graviton zero mode and quasinormal modes using pseudospectral techniques.
AI.result: Condition numbers grow rapidly with overtone number; pseudospectral contours become broad and connected at high overtones; the zero mode exhibits a larger condition number than the fundamental mode; all indicate strong mode-dependent sensitivity to norm-bounded perturbations.
AI.conclusion: Quasinormal modes in thick braneworlds display pronounced spectral non-normality, with higher overtones and the zero mode being significantly less robust than the fundamental mode; these pseudospectral diagnostics provide a quantitative framework for assessing stability under generic operator perturbations, though mapping to physical braneworld deformations requires incorporating self-consistent constraints.

title: An effective topology-transfer nuisance for Genie-based neutrino-argon semi-inclusive analyses: a methodological proposal with MicroBooNE-constrained diagnostic
summary: Liquid-argon TPC oscillation analyses increasingly split samples into proton-tagged (Np) and proton-less (0p) topologies at the ~35 MeV tracking threshold, but the standard GENIE Reweight library has no dial that transfers events across this boundary. We propose a single empirical nuisance parameter, $f_{\rm mig}$, that fills this gap as a per-event reweight on nominal GENIE output, implementable without event regeneration. It is presented as a methodological diagnostic: an effective topology-transfer surrogate absorbing an unspecified combination of near-threshold proton mismodelling effects (proton-side FSI, nucleon-momentum distribution, RES $Q^2$ shape, MEC kinematic shape), not a measurement of any single microscopic mechanism. As a reference scale, the position-dependent mean-field energy loss absent from GENIE's cascade is estimated from the $^{40}$Ar density profile to be a few percent, consistent with proton-transparency differences reported between cascade and transport generators on MicroBooNE data. The primary constraint is a direct scan on the MicroBooNE simultaneous CC 0p/Np differential cross-section release with no sector-weight regularisation: $\hat{f}_{\rm mig} = 0.093 \pm 0.024$, $3.8σ$ (Wilks) / $3.2σ$ (empirical). A supporting NC $Δ$ radiative sideband fit gives $\hat{f}_{\rm mig} = 0.050^{+0.029}_{-0.022}$, conditional on sector-weight priors; the two datasets share flux/detector systematics and are corroborating rather than independent. Introducing $f_{\rm mig}$ also relieves a compensatory CCRES sector-weight suppression in migration-blind fits. The extracted parameter is best understood as a flux-integrated effective nuisance direction for the MicroBooNE BNB configuration, suitable as a candidate GENIE dial for future LArTPC analyses pending detector-level validation.

AI.tldr: Proposes an empirical nuisance parameter $f_{m mig}$ to correct GENIE-generated neutrino events for mis-modeling of proton emission near the ~35 MeV tracking threshold in liquid-argon TPCs, enabling consistent Np/0p topology classification without event regeneration; constrained to $0.093 \pm 0.024$ by MicroBooNE CC 0p/Np cross-section data.
AI.motivation: Standard GENIE Reweight lacks a mechanism to transfer events across the proton-tagged (Np) vs. proton-less (0p) topology boundary at ~35 MeV in LArTPCs, causing biases in oscillation analyses due to near-threshold proton mismodelling (e.g., FSI, nucleon momentum distribution, RES $Q^2$, MEC kinematics).
AI.method: Introduces a per-event reweight $f_{\rm mig}$ applied to nominal GENIE output—no event regeneration required—to empirically absorb topology migration effects; validated via direct scan on MicroBooNE’s simultaneous CC 0p/Np differential cross-section measurement and supported by NC $\Delta$ radiative sideband fit; incorporates mean-field energy loss estimate from $^{40}$Ar density profile.
AI.result: $\hat{f}_{\rm mig} = 0.093 \pm 0.024$ ($3.8\sigma$ Wilks / $3.2\sigma$ empirical) from CC 0p/Np data; $\hat{f}_{\rm mig} = 0.050^{+0.029}_{-0.022}$ from NC $\Delta$ sideband (sector-weight prior dependent); $f_{\rm mig}$ eliminates need for compensatory CCRES sector-weight suppression in migration-blind fits.
AI.conclusion: The $f_{\rm mig}$ parameter serves as a flux-integrated, detector-configuration-specific effective nuisance direction for MicroBooNE’s BNB beam, suitable as a candidate GENIE dial for future LArTPC oscillation analyses—pending detector-level validation.

title: Unitarity and the Forward Direction in Theories with Long-Range Forces
summary: Integrating scattering amplitudes over the forward direction, and consequently the unitarity constraints one extracts from such integrals, can appear ambiguous in theories with long-range forces. Standard techniques for bounding EFT couplings then typically produce bounds that depend on an arbitrary infrared scale. We study a non-relativistic model in which the standard techniques produce such an ambiguous bound, but which is simple enough that the exact bound can also be derived non-perturbatively and shown to involve no infrared scale. We then show how to derive bounds perturbatively, with no infrared scale entering at any stage. This requires two ingredients: accounting for the modified distributional structure of long-range amplitudes, and using distorted-wave perturbation theory (DWPT), which treats the Coulomb dynamics exactly. Together they give amplitudes with well-defined partial-wave projections and no spurious infrared divergences. Interpreting the model as an EFT with an ultraviolet cutoff $Λ_{\rm EFT}$, we derive cutoff-dependent bounds valid for arbitrary UV completions. Taking $Λ_{\rm EFT}\to\infty$ at each order yields bounds that rapidly converge to the exact bound, reaching $0.002\%$ accuracy at fourth order in the expansion. Finally, we demonstrate that every order of the DWPT expansion resums infinitely many Feynman diagrams of short-range perturbation theory, which individually evaluate to multiple polylogarithms and complete elliptic integrals, into a compact expression. At the orders we compute, no integration is even required, suggesting that DWPT may offer a simpler representation of scattering amplitudes than standard perturbation theory.

AI.tldr: This paper resolves infrared ambiguities in EFT bounds for theories with long-range forces (e.g., Coulomb) by introducing distorted-wave perturbation theory (DWPT), which treats long-range dynamics exactly; it yields scale-free, convergent, non-perturbative-like bounds and resums complicated short-range diagrams into compact analytic expressions.
AI.motivation: Standard unitarity-based EFT bounds become ambiguous due to infrared sensitivity in theories with long-range forces (e.g., Coulomb), introducing arbitrary IR scales; the paper aims to eliminate such ambiguities and recover exact, scale-independent bounds via a controlled perturbative framework.
AI.method: Uses a solvable non-relativistic model with Coulomb interaction; applies distorted-wave perturbation theory (DWPT) — treating the Coulomb Hamiltonian exactly — combined with careful handling of distributional structure of forward-scattering amplitudes; derives partial-wave-projected amplitudes free of spurious IR divergences; interprets results within an EFT framework with UV cutoff Λ_EFT and studies convergence as Λ_EFT → ∞.
AI.result: DWPT yields IR-scale-free perturbative bounds that converge rapidly to the exact non-perturbative bound (0.002% error at fourth order); each DWPT order resums infinite classes of short-range Feynman diagrams involving multiple polylogarithms and elliptic integrals into compact, integration-free expressions.
AI.conclusion: Infrared ambiguities in unitarity bounds stem from misapplying plane-wave perturbation theory to long-range interactions; DWPT—combined with proper distributional treatment—restores uniqueness, predictivity, and computational simplicity, offering a superior framework for EFTs with Coulomb or similar long-range forces.

title: Critical and extremal gravitational collapse of a spherical charged scalar field in 4+1 spacetime dimensions
summary: We numerically investigate the gravitational collapse of a charged scalar field coupled to the Einstein and Maxwell equations in spherical symmetry, in 4+1 spacetime dimensions. At the threshold of collapse we find type-II critical phenomena very similar to what is seen in 3+1 dimensions, including self-similarity of the critical solution and power-law scaling of the black hole mass and charge. Well inside the collapse region, we also identify initial data that collapse to an extremal black hole. By varying all parameters of the initial data by up to $\sim0.5\%$, we give evidence that there is a small neighbourhood in the space of initial data where an exactly extremal charged black hole is formed in the evolution of a codimension-1 set of initial data. We believe this is the first such evidence for scalar field collapse from regular initial data.

AI.tldr: This paper numerically studies gravitational collapse of a charged scalar field in 4+1D Einstein–Maxwell theory, finding type-II critical phenomena (self-similarity, power-law scaling) analogous to 3+1D, and provides numerical evidence for formation of extremal black holes from a codimension-1 subset of regular initial data.
AI.motivation: To explore whether type-II critical phenomena and extremal black hole formation persist in higher-dimensional (4+1D) gravitational collapse of charged matter, extending prior 3+1D results and probing the boundary of black hole parameter space.
AI.method: Numerical relativity simulation of spherically symmetric gravitational collapse governed by the coupled Einstein–Maxwell–scalar field equations in 4+1 spacetime dimensions; systematic tuning of initial data parameters near criticality and extremality.
AI.result: Observation of type-II critical behavior (discrete self-similarity, power-law scaling of mass and charge) at the black hole threshold; identification of initial data collapsing to near-extremal black holes; evidence—via sub-0.5% parameter variation—that extremal black holes form on a codimension-1 hypersurface in initial data space.
AI.conclusion: Type-II critical phenomena generalize to 4+1D; extremal black holes can arise dynamically from smooth, regular initial data, realized on a measure-zero (codimension-1) subset of the parameter space—constituting the first such demonstration for scalar field collapse.

title: New parton distribution functions of the real photon
comment: 7 pages, 5 figures, proceedings of the 33rd International Workshop on Deep Inelastic Scattering and Related Subjects (DIS2026), 4-8 May 2026, Bologna, Italy
summary: Precise determination of the partonic structure of real photons has attracted renewed interest in view of ongoing studies of high-energy photon-induced processes in ultraperipheral collisions (UPCs) at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and the future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). Despite being fundamental in their own right and essential for QCD phenomenology of hard processes initiated by resolved photons, the quark and gluon distributions of the photon are poorly known and merit a new analysis employing modern tools of statistical data analysis. We determine new sets of leading-order (LO) and next-to-leading-order (NLO) parton distributions (PDFs) for the real photon, dubbed VALO1.0, by performing a global QCD analysis of the world data on the photon structure function $F_2^γ$ measured in deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) processes on a real photon target in electron-positron collisions. Our analysis improves on the results available in the literature by providing uncertainties in the form of Monte Carlo replicas and the photon PDFs in the LHAPDF6 format. We observe that while the electron-positron data allow us to determine the singlet quark distribution very well at both LO and NLO, the gluon distribution is constrained to a much lesser degree, especially at LO. For this analysis, we have developed an open-source framework, which extends the pineline framework, developed for the proton, to the photon case and includes the program solving the inhomogeneous scale evolution of photon PDFs, $γ$EKO.

AI.tldr: This paper presents VALO1.0, new LO and NLO parton distribution functions (PDFs) for the real photon, determined via global QCD analysis of $F_2^γ$ data from $e^+e^−$ DIS; it improves uncertainty quantification (Monte Carlo replicas) and provides LHAPDF6-compatible PDFs, with strong constraints on the singlet quark distribution but limited gluon constraint—especially at LO—and introduces an open-source extension of the pipeline framework including the inhomogeneous DGLAP solver γEKO.
AI.motivation: The partonic structure of real photons is poorly constrained despite its importance for QCD phenomenology in photon-initiated processes (e.g., UPCs at LHC, EIC), necessitating a modern, statistically rigorous global analysis.
AI.method: Global QCD analysis of world $F_2^γ$ data from $e^+e^−$ deep-inelastic scattering at LO and NLO; use of Monte Carlo replica method for uncertainties; development of an open-source framework extending the proton PDF pipeline to photons, incorporating the inhomogeneous evolution solver γEKO; PDFs delivered in LHAPDF6 format.
AI.result: VALO1.0 PDF sets—first publicly available LO/NLO photon PDFs with replica-based uncertainties and LHAPDF6 support; tight constraints on singlet quark PDF at both orders; significantly weaker constraint on gluon PDF, especially at LO.
AI.conclusion: VALO1.0 establishes a new benchmark for photon PDFs, enabling more reliable predictions for resolved-photon processes; the limited gluon constraint highlights the need for additional data (e.g., from EIC) and motivates further theoretical and experimental efforts.

title: Positivity Bounds in $\mathcal N =1$ Supersymmetry
summary: For a low-energy Effective Field Theory (EFT) to admit a consistent ultraviolet (UV) completion, it must adhere to the fundamental principles of locality, unitarity, analyticity, and Lorentz invariance. This leads to positivity constraints on certain Wilson coefficients via dispersion relations of $2\rightarrow2$ forward elastic amplitudes, which carry significant implications for both theoretical consistency and experimental phenomenology. In this work, we extend this bootstrap framework to $\mathcal N = 1$ supersymmetric theories, where the super-Poincaré algebra relates the bosonic and fermionic degrees of freedom within a single supermultiplet. Supersymmetric Ward identities (SWIs) enforce exact linear relations among component scattering amplitudes. Consequently, the Wilson coefficients associated with different $2\rightarrow2$ processes are mutually constrained, rendering their respective positivity bounds dependent. Focusing on dimension-8 operators, we explicitly show the positivity bounds on quartic interactions involving scalars, fermions and gauge fields, and demonstrate how they are related as a direct consequence of the SWIs. Furthermore, we expect that the algebraic nature of this framework naturally extends to loop-level superamplitudes and higher-point processes, providing a unified bootstrap perspective on supersymmetric EFTs.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the EFT positivity bootstrap to N=1 supersymmetric theories, using supersymmetric Ward identities to derive interdependent positivity bounds on dimension-8 Wilson coefficients for scalar, fermion, and gauge quartic interactions.
AI.motivation: To ensure consistency of low-energy supersymmetric EFTs with UV completions by deriving necessary constraints from fundamental principles (locality, unitarity, analyticity, Lorentz invariance) adapted to the super-Poincaré algebra.
AI.method: Applies dispersion relations to 2→2 forward elastic superamplitudes, incorporates supersymmetric Ward identities to relate component amplitudes, and derives positivity bounds on dimension-8 Wilson coefficients in N=1 SUSY EFTs.
AI.result: Explicit positivity bounds on dimension-8 operators involving scalars, fermions, and gauge fields are obtained; these bounds are mutually dependent due to SWIs, unlike the independent bounds in non-supersymmetric EFTs.
AI.conclusion: Supersymmetry fundamentally alters the positivity bootstrap: Wilson coefficients across different 2→2 processes are linearly related via SWIs, leading to a unified, algebraically constrained positivity framework that naturally generalizes to loops and higher-point superamplitudes.

title: Symmetry of the Klein-Gordon Equation under Disformal Transformations with Higher-Order Derivatives
summary: Scalar-Tensor theories extend General Relativity (GR) by including both a scalar field and a metric tensor in describing gravity. Although the matter sector is minimally coupled to the metric in GR, the scalar field coupling to matter may be adjusted by means of Disformal Transformations. One of the most general of these transformations, formulated by Takahashi, Motohashi, and Minamitsuji, include arbitrarily high-order derivatives of the scalar field and are designed to map between two ghost-free Higher-order Scalar-Tensor theories. We used these transformations to determine the most general conditions for the disformal form-invariance of the Klein-Gordon equation for the scalar field. In the second-order case, we identified a family of disformally-related metrics that result in the same propagation solutions. Additionally, higher-order cases could comply with theoretical and phenomenological constraints alongside KG-invariance. Finally, we investigated the notion of disformal transformations as ``deformations'' of the spacetime manifold.

AI.tldr: This paper studies disformal transformations in scalar-tensor theories, deriving general conditions for Klein-Gordon equation invariance under such transformations—including second- and higher-order cases—and explores their geometric interpretation as spacetime deformations.
