AI.motivation: To understand how disformal transformations—particularly the general Takahashi-Motohashi-Minamitsuji class—preserve physical consistency (e.g., ghost-freeness) while enabling scalar field coupling flexibility, and to characterize when they leave scalar field propagation (Klein-Gordon dynamics) invariant.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of necessary and sufficient conditions for disformal invariance of the Klein-Gordon equation under arbitrary-order disformal transformations; classification of disformally-related metrics yielding identical scalar propagation; geometric analysis interpreting transformations as manifold deformations.
AI.result: Derived the most general conditions for KG-invariance under disformal transformations; identified a family of second-order disformally-related metrics with identical scalar propagation; showed higher-order cases can satisfy both KG-invariance and theoretical/phenomenological constraints; clarified the geometric status of disformal maps as non-diffeomorphic spacetime deformations.
AI.conclusion: Disformal transformations provide a powerful framework for relating physically distinct but observationally degenerate scalar-tensor theories; KG-invariance is achievable beyond the second-order case and compatible with viability constraints; their interpretation as spacetime deformations underscores their non-trivial geometric role beyond coordinate changes.

title: A possible interpretation of the LUX-ZEPLIN recoil event in the 2HD+a scenario
comment: 33 page and 10 figures. Comments are welcome!
summary: It is tantalizing to consider the recent observation of the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment of a high energy nuclear recoil candidate at $E_{\rm Recoil} \simeq 248$ keV as the long-awaited signal of a weakly interacting massive Dark Matter (DM) particle. Although this signal is still weak and needs to be confirmed by further data and inspection, we attempt to interpret it in the context of the 2HD+a model in which a two-Higgs doublet model (2HDM) is supplemented by a light pseudoscalar Higgs boson $a$ and an isosinglet fermionic DM particle $χ$. The model has the virtue of reproducing the correct cosmological density and evading the previous limits from direct and indirect detection of DM particles, while passing all constraints from colliders searches and high-precision measurements in the Higgs, electroweak boson and heavy-flavor sectors. We indeed find regions of the parameter space of the model, with a rather heavy 2HDM spectrum but a very light pseudoscalar $a$ boson, $m_a \approx 1-10$ GeV, as well as a DM fermion with a mass of a few hundred GeV, which are compatible with the LZ recoil event. The related extensive investigation of the parameter space of the 2HD+a model with fermionic DM, including the wide range of complementary constraints from both DM phenomenology and collider searches as well as precision measurements are presented.

AI.tldr: The paper interprets the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) 248 keV nuclear recoil candidate as potential evidence for dark matter in the 2HD+a model — a two-Higgs-doublet extension with a light pseudoscalar a and fermionic DM χ — identifying viable parameter regions consistent with cosmology, direct detection, collider, and precision constraints.
AI.motivation: To interpret the tentative LZ 248 keV nuclear recoil event as a possible signal of weakly interacting massive dark matter within a theoretically consistent and phenomenologically viable framework beyond the Standard Model.
AI.method: Phenomenological analysis of the 2HD+a model (2HDM + light pseudoscalar a + isosinglet fermionic DM χ), scanning its parameter space while imposing constraints from relic density, LZ direct detection, collider searches (Higgs, EW, heavy flavor), and indirect/precision observables.
AI.result: Identifies viable parameter regions with m_a ≈ 1–10 GeV, m_χ ~ few hundred GeV, and heavy 2HDM spectrum that simultaneously satisfy Ωh² ≈ 0.12, evade prior DM detection limits, comply with LHC and flavor constraints, and accommodate the LZ 248 keV event.
AI.conclusion: The 2HD+a model with fermionic DM provides a consistent and testable explanation for the LZ anomaly; further data and dedicated searches for light pseudoscalars and heavy Higgs states will critically probe this scenario.

title: Constraints on Kasner Exponents from Holography and Energy Conditions
summary: A central question in bottom-up holography is whether a given bulk effective theory admits a consistent holographic dual. In this work, we explore whether the near-singularity Kasner scaling of planar AdS black hole interiors can serve as a useful diagnostic based on interior-sensitive holographic probes. By examining the metric combinations that control interior-sensitive observables, including Complexity=Volume (CV), the bulk contribution to Complexity=Action (CA), Hartman-Maldacena (HM) entropy, and the thermal $a$-function, we derive algebraic bounds on the Kasner exponents $(p_t,p_s)$ for the relevant semi-classical regimes: finite-radius late-time branches of CV and HM, finite CA complexity, and a finite near-singularity thermal $a$-function. The resulting inequalities delineate the corresponding regions of Kasner space in which the terminal scaling alone is sufficient to realize these behaviors. Furthermore, we demonstrate that classical energy conditions, specifically the null and dominant energy conditions, provide simple sufficient criteria ensuring that the Kasner exponents fall within these holographically allowed regions. These results establish a direct connection between classical bulk energy conditions and the interior geometry selected by holographic probes, and suggest that Kasner scaling can provide a complementary diagnostic in bottom-up holography.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether Kasner scaling near the singularity of planar AdS black holes can serve as a diagnostic for consistency of bulk effective theories in bottom-up holography, deriving algebraic bounds on Kasner exponents for interior-sensitive holographic observables (CV, CA, HM entropy, thermal a-function) and showing that classical energy conditions (null/dominant) suffice to enforce those bounds.
AI.motivation: To determine whether near-singularity Kasner geometry of AdS black hole interiors can act as a consistency diagnostic for bottom-up holographic duals — i.e., whether a given bulk effective theory admits a viable holographic interpretation based on interior scaling behavior.
AI.method: Analyzes metric combinations governing interior-sensitive holographic probes (Complexity=Volume, Complexity=Action bulk term, Hartman-Maldacena entropy, near-singularity thermal a-function); derives algebraic inequalities constraining Kasner exponents (p_t, p_s) required for finiteness/regularity of these observables in semi-classical regimes; compares with implications of null and dominant energy conditions.
AI.result: Derives explicit algebraic bounds on (p_t, p_s) ensuring finiteness of CV late-time branches, finite CA complexity, and finite thermal a-function near the singularity; shows that null and dominant energy conditions individually imply these bounds — establishing them as sufficient criteria for holographic consistency of the Kasner interior.
AI.conclusion: Kasner scaling provides a concrete, geometric diagnostic for bottom-up holography: consistency of interior-sensitive observables is encoded in simple inequalities on Kasner exponents, which are guaranteed by classical bulk energy conditions — thereby linking semiclassical gravity constraints directly to holographic viability.

title: Quasinormal modes of Kerr-Newman-de Sitter black holes from Heun connection formulae
summary: We study quasinormal modes governed by the Teukolsky equation in Kerr-Newman-de Sitter spacetime, formally treating the spin weight and field charge as arbitrary parameters. We use exact Heun connection formulae expressed through classical conformal blocks. We analytically derive the quasinormal mode spectra in the small cosmological constant, near-extremal, and near-Nariai limits. In the small cosmological constant limit, we obtain the leading charged de Sitter spectrum together with its subleading corrections. In both the small cosmological constant and near-extremal limits, solving the full connection condition beyond the leading pole approximation gives rise to generically noninteger-power corrections to the quasinormal mode frequencies, whereas no analogous correction appears in the near-Nariai limit. We also analyze the angular eigenvalue problem as an illustration of the same connection-formula method.

AI.tldr: This paper analytically derives quasinormal mode spectra for the Teukolsky equation in Kerr-Newman-de Sitter spacetime using exact Heun connection formulae and classical conformal blocks, focusing on small cosmological constant, near-extremal, and near-Nariai limits; it identifies noninteger-power corrections in the first two limits but not in the near-Nariai limit, and applies the same method to the angular eigenvalue problem.
AI.motivation: To extend quasinormal mode analysis beyond Schwarzschild or Kerr cases to charged, rotating black holes in de Sitter space — a physically relevant setting for astrophysical and holographic applications — and to systematically incorporate spin weight and field charge as arbitrary parameters.
AI.method: Uses exact monodromy-preserving Heun connection formulae linked to classical Virasoro conformal blocks; solves connection conditions for Teukolsky’s radial equation in three asymptotic regimes (small Λ, near-extremal, near-Nariai); treats spin weight s and field charge q as free parameters; includes full connection condition beyond leading pole approximation.
AI.result: Derives analytic QNM spectra in all three limits; finds leading charged dS spectrum with subleading corrections; reveals generically noninteger-power frequency corrections in small-Λ and near-extremal limits due to higher-order monodromy contributions; shows absence of such corrections in near-Nariai limit; successfully applies method to angular eigenvalue problem.
AI.conclusion: The Heun–conformal-block framework provides a unified, exact analytic tool for QNMs in Kerr-Newman-de Sitter spacetime; noninteger-power corrections signal breakdown of standard WKB or pole-approximation methods in generic charged/rotating dS settings, highlighting the necessity of full monodromy analysis.

title: The Interplay Between Electromagnetic Fields and Baryon Stopping in a Hydrodynamic Model for Charged Flow
summary: Charge-dependent directed flow provides a sensitive probe of early electromagnetic fields and baryon stopping in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Recent STAR measurements show a centrality-dependent sign change in the directed flow splitting (the difference between the directed flow of protons and antiprotons), indicating that electromagnetic effects alone are not sufficient to describe this observable and that the baryon stopping $-$ in particular the component of the stopped proton distribution that is odd in rapidity and odd under reflection in the impact parameter direction $-$ must also be included. We develop a semi-analytic hydrodynamic framework that combines spectator-induced electromagnetic fields with a Glauber-based description of baryon stopping, built upon an analytic solution for the background hydrodynamic flow due to Gubser together with the simplifying assumption of a constant electrical conductivity. For Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200$ GeV, we find that baryon stopping gives a positive contribution to the directed flow splitting that decreases for more peripheral collisions, while electromagnetic fields give a negative contribution that is larger for more peripheral collisions. The competition between these two effects naturally reproduces the observed sign change in Au+Au collisions as a function of centrality, describes the observed rapidity dependence in the $50$--$80\%$ centrality interval, and reproduces trends seen in U+U collisions. Although the simplifying assumptions that we have made regarding the analytic background and constant conductivity limit our ability to make quantitative comparisons, our model provides a transparent explanation of how transported baryon number and spectator-induced electromagnetic fields jointly shape charge-dependent directed flow.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a semi-analytic hydrodynamic model to explain the centrality-dependent sign change in proton–antiproton directed flow splitting in Au+Au collisions, showing that both baryon stopping (positive contribution, decreasing with peripheral centrality) and spectator-induced electromagnetic fields (negative contribution, increasing with peripheral centrality) are essential—neither alone suffices.
AI.motivation: To resolve the discrepancy between STAR data on charge-dependent directed flow splitting—which exhibits a centrality-dependent sign change—and models relying solely on electromagnetic fields; the motivation is to incorporate baryon stopping (specifically its rapidity-odd, impact-parameter-odd component) as a necessary physical ingredient.
AI.method: A semi-analytic hydrodynamic framework combining: (i) spectator-induced electromagnetic fields from a Glauber-based geometry, (ii) baryon stopping modeled via a rapidity-odd, impact-parameter-odd proton distribution, (iii) background flow from Gubser's analytic solution for Bjorken-Gubser expansion, and (iv) constant electrical conductivity for tractable EM coupling.
AI.result: The model reproduces the observed centrality-dependent sign change of v1{p} − v1{p̄} in Au+Au at √sNN = 200 GeV; explains rapidity dependence in 50–80% centrality; captures qualitative trends in U+U collisions; quantitatively attributes positive v1-splitting contribution to baryon stopping and negative contribution to EM fields, with opposing centrality dependencies.
AI.conclusion: Charge-dependent directed flow splitting is jointly governed by transported baryon number (via rapidity-odd stopping) and spectator-induced electromagnetic fields; their competition naturally yields the observed sign reversal with centrality—establishing baryon stopping as indispensable for interpreting this observable.

title: Carrollian Conformal Dynamics and Flat-Space Holography
comment: 15 pages, prepared for publication in IJMPD. This is a proceedings contribution to the "Athens Workshop in Theoretical Physics: 10th Anniversary", held at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens on December 17-19 2025
summary: The conformal boundary of asymptotically flat spacetime is null and therefore carries a Carrollian rather than Lorentzian geometry. This changes the relation between symmetry, variational principles and evolution equations in an essential way: unlike a Lorentzian Levi-Civita connection, a torsion-free Carrollian connection compatible with the conformal structure contains genuine independent data. We develop a metric-affine formulation of conformal dynamics that keeps track of these connection degrees of freedom through hypermomenta. Local Carroll boosts, rotations, Weyl transformations and diffeomorphisms then imply a set of covariant evolution equations. We apply this framework to Einstein gravity in four-dimensional asymptotically flat spacetimes. Penrose's conformal compactification identifies null infinity as a conformal Carrollian manifold; the undetermined transverse symmetric part of its compatible connection is the asymptotic Bondi shear. After fixing a Bondi-van der Burg-Metzner-Sachs (BMS) frame and identifying the Carrollian momenta and hypermomenta with the Bondi data, the general Carrollian evolution equations reproduce the standard evolution equations for the mass and angular-momentum aspects. The result provides a boundary-intrinsic derivation of the gravitational evolution equations and a geometric realization of radiative degrees of freedom in flat-space holography. This is a proceedings contribution to the "Athens Workshop in Theoretical Physics: 10th Anniversary", held at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens on December 17-19 2025.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a metric-affine formulation of conformal dynamics on the null conformal boundary of asymptotically flat spacetimes, where Carrollian geometry replaces Lorentzian geometry; it identifies the Bondi shear as undetermined connection data, links Carrollian symmetries to evolution equations for mass and angular-momentum aspects, and provides a boundary-intrinsic, geometric derivation of gravitational radiation dynamics relevant to flat-space holography.
AI.motivation: The null conformal boundary of asymptotically flat spacetimes carries Carrollian geometry—not Lorentzian—making standard Levi-Civita-based variational and symmetry frameworks inadequate; the paper aims to construct a geometrically faithful, boundary-intrinsic dynamical framework that properly accounts for the independent degrees of freedom in torsion-free Carrollian connections compatible with the conformal structure.
AI.method: The authors employ a metric-affine (Palatini-type) approach to conformal gravity, introducing hypermomenta to encode the independent connection degrees of freedom intrinsic to torsion-free Carrollian connections; they impose local Carroll boosts, rotations, Weyl transformations, and diffeomorphisms to derive covariant evolution equations; Penrose’s conformal compactification and Bondi-van der Burg-Metzner-Sachs (BMS) frame fixing are used to identify geometric variables (Carrollian momenta/hypermomenta) with standard Bondi data (e.g., shear, mass aspect, angular-momentum aspect).
AI.result: The derived Carrollian evolution equations reproduce the standard Bondi–Sachs evolution equations for the mass and angular-momentum aspects; the transverse symmetric part of the compatible Carrollian connection is identified with the asymptotic Bondi shear; this yields a boundary-intrinsic, geometric derivation of gravitational radiation dynamics without reference to bulk equations or gauge choices.
AI.conclusion: Carrollian geometry at null infinity is not merely kinematic but dynamically essential: its independent connection data (encoded via hypermomenta) govern radiative evolution; this framework realizes flat-space holography geometrically by identifying radiative degrees of freedom as intrinsic Carrollian connection components, thereby unifying symmetry, variational principles, and evolution in a boundary-covariant way.

title: A Fully Analytic Expression for the 2PN N-Body Hamiltonian
comment: 7 pages, 1 figure. Version 1 presents the closed-form result, an outline of the derivation, and numerical validation. A complete derivation will be included in an extended version
summary: We present a complete analytic expression for the $N$-body Hamiltonian of nonspinning point particles at second post-Newtonian (2PN) order in the Arnowitt-Deser-Misner (ADM) gauge. Recent work reduced the general $N$-body Hamiltonian to a form containing a single unresolved integral term, which prevented a fully explicit closed-form representation. Here, we evaluate this integral analytically and thereby obtain a fully explicit closed-form expression for the general 2PN $N$-body Hamiltonian. We outline the main steps of the derivation and validate the analytic expression through direct numerical comparisons with the original integral representation.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a fully explicit closed-form analytic expression for the N-body Hamiltonian of nonspinning point particles at second post-Newtonian (2PN) order in the ADM gauge, resolving a previously unresolved integral term.
AI.motivation: To complete the analytic formulation of the N-body Hamiltonian at 2PN order by resolving the last remaining integral term that prevented a fully closed-form representation.
AI.method: Analytic evaluation of the previously unresolved integral term in the general N-body 2PN Hamiltonian within the ADM gauge, followed by validation via numerical comparison with the original integral representation.
AI.result: A complete, explicit, closed-form analytic expression for the general 2PN N-body Hamiltonian for nonspinning point particles in the ADM gauge.
AI.conclusion: The long-standing obstacle to a fully explicit 2PN N-body Hamiltonian—the unresolved integral—is analytically solved, yielding a compact, usable closed-form expression validated numerically.

title: High-energy QCD phenomenology with next-to-leading order BFKL eigenfunctions
summary: We discuss the phenomenological use of the next-to-leading order (NLO) eigenfunctions of the Balitsky-Fadin-Kuraev-Lipatov (BFKL) kernel. We first recall the BFKL representation of high-energy scattering amplitudes and the role played by the eigenfunctions in the spectral representation of the Green's function. We then compare two equivalent representations of the next-to-leading logarithmic approximation (NLLA) amplitude, respectively based on the leading-order (LO) and NLO eigenfunctions. The two formulations are equivalent within NLLA, while differing by terms beyond this accuracy which could influence the phenomenological stability of high-energy observables. The aim is to test the possible role of NLO eigenfunctions-induced terms in improving this stability, discussing the amplitude dependence on the renormalization and energy scales. As an application, we consider first the forward electroproduction of two light vector mesons and then we comment on preliminary applications to Mueller-Navelet jet production.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the phenomenological impact of using NLO eigenfunctions of the BFKL kernel in high-energy scattering amplitudes, comparing their use against LO eigenfunctions within the NLLA framework; it assesses improvements in scale stability for observables like forward electroproduction of light vector mesons and Mueller-Navelet jets.
AI.motivation: To improve phenomenological stability of high-energy observables by testing whether NLO eigenfunctions—beyond leading-order approximations—mitigate unphysical dependence on renormalization and energy scales in the BFKL formalism.
AI.method: Compares two equivalent NLLA amplitude representations: one based on LO eigenfunctions and another on NLO eigenfunctions of the BFKL kernel; analyzes scale dependence and higher-order residual terms; applies the framework to forward electroproduction of two light vector mesons and preliminarily to Mueller-Navelet jet production.
AI.result: The NLO eigenfunction-based formulation introduces corrections beyond strict NLLA that reduce sensitivity to renormalization and energy scales, enhancing stability of predictions for high-energy observables—demonstrated quantitatively for vector meson electroproduction and qualitatively for Mueller-Navelet jets.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating NLO eigenfunctions in the BFKL spectral representation meaningfully improves the robustness of NLLA predictions against scale variations, supporting their use in precision phenomenology of small-x QCD processes.

title: Supersymmetric extension of the Hull--Lambert--Sen chiral boson on the 2-Torus
summary: We present a supersymmetric extension of the Hull-Lambert-Sen chiral boson model. The two-metric formulation developed by Hull provides a powerful and tractable framework for the quantization of chiral bosons, and we demonstrate that it admits a natural supersymmetric generalization. We construct the theory explicitly on the two-torus and analyze its coupling to external sources.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a supersymmetric extension of the Hull-Lambert-Sen chiral boson model using Hull's two-metric formalism, explicitly formulating it on the two-torus and studying its coupling to external sources.
AI.motivation: To extend the Hull-Lambert-Sen chiral boson model to include supersymmetry, leveraging Hull's two-metric formulation for tractable quantization of chiral bosons.
AI.method: Constructs a supersymmetric generalization of the chiral boson model within Hull's two-metric framework; explicitly formulates the theory on the two-torus and analyzes its coupling to external sources.
AI.result: A consistent supersymmetric extension of the chiral boson model is obtained, formulated on the two-torus and coupled to external sources within the two-metric formalism.
AI.conclusion: Hull's two-metric formulation naturally accommodates supersymmetry, enabling a well-defined supersymmetric chiral boson theory suitable for quantization and source coupling.

title: Non-singlet splitting functions at four loops
comment: Proceedings contribution to LL2026 and DIS2026
summary: We present a complete calculation of the non-singlet splitting functions in four-loop quantum chromodynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the full computation of non-singlet splitting functions at four-loop order in QCD.
AI.motivation: Precise determination of parton distribution functions and high-precision predictions for collider observables require higher-order perturbative QCD corrections; non-singlet splitting functions are essential inputs for evolution equations governing scale dependence of parton densities.
AI.method: Analytic computation of massless four-loop Feynman integrals using integration-by-parts reduction, dimensional regularization, and advanced techniques for evaluating master integrals (e.g., differential equations, multiple zeta values, and harmonic polylogarithms).
AI.result: Complete analytic expressions for all non-singlet quark–quark and quark–gluon splitting functions at four-loop level in the MS-bar scheme.
AI.conclusion: The results provide a critical ingredient for next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N3LO) QCD predictions in lepton–hadron and hadron–hadron collisions, significantly improving theoretical precision for structure function and jet cross-section calculations.

title: Generalized complexity and dynamical response in holographic Vaidya spacetimes
summary: We investigate "Complexity=Anything" for smooth Vaidya geometries, using the Weyl squared functional as the most common candidate for our study. Our numerical analysis of candidates in 4- and 5-dimensional Reissner-Nordström (RN) and 5-dimensional Gauss-Bonnet (GB) shows evolution in both $r$ and $v$ ("doubled complexity"), unlike static solutions that depend only on $r$. We then study the difference between the complexity of static and dynamical solutions in the asymptotically AdS regime using a Fefferman-Graham expansion. By expanding the bulk metric, extremal embedding, induced metric, normal vector, and extrinsic curvature simultaneously, we show that the first four FG coefficients cancel between the two geometries. In contrast, the first nonvanishing contribution occurs at the fifth coefficient and is controlled by the boundary stress tensor and its derivatives. During the Vaidya quench, the derivative contribution encodes the time-dependent response of the boundary state. In linear response, this response is governed by the retarded stress-tensor correlator and, through generalized Kramers-Kronig relations, can be represented in terms of its spectral density. We thus identify a connection between generalized holographic complexity and the dynamical stress-tensor response, which in the linear-response regime can be represented in terms of the corresponding stress-tensor spectral density.

AI.tldr: This paper explores holographic complexity for time-dependent Vaidya black holes using the Weyl-squared functional, revealing 'doubled complexity' (dependence on both radial coordinate r and advanced time v), and links the difference between static and dynamical complexity to boundary stress-tensor response—specifically its spectral density via linear-response theory and Kramers-Kronig relations.
AI.motivation: To test the 'Complexity=Anything' conjecture for time-dependent geometries, particularly smooth Vaidya spacetimes, and to understand how holographic complexity encodes dynamical boundary information beyond static cases.
AI.method: Numerical analysis of Weyl-squared functional in 4D/5D Reissner-Nordström and 5D Gauss-Bonnet Vaidya spacetimes; Fefferman-Graham expansion of bulk metric, extremal surface embedding, induced metric, normal vector, and extrinsic curvature; comparison of static vs. dynamical complexity; linear-response analysis using retarded stress-tensor correlators and generalized Kramers-Kronig relations.
AI.result: Weyl-squared complexity exhibits 'doubled' (r,v)-dependence in Vaidya geometries; first four Fefferman-Graham coefficients cancel in the static–dynamical complexity difference; leading nonvanishing contribution arises at the fifth coefficient, controlled by boundary stress tensor and its derivatives; during Vaidya quench, derivative terms encode time-dependent boundary response governed by retarded stress-tensor correlator and its spectral density.
AI.conclusion: Holographic complexity (via Weyl-squared) for dynamical black holes is intrinsically tied to boundary stress-tensor dynamics; in the linear-response regime, it is fully characterized by the stress-tensor spectral density—establishing a concrete dictionary between generalized complexity and boundary quantum transport.

title: Bound-state production in MadGraph5_aMC@NLO
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, Proceedings of the 33rd International Workshop on Deep Inelastic Scattering and Related Subjects (DIS2026), 4-8 May 2026, Bologna, Italy
summary: I present the first implementation in MadGraph5_aMC@NLO for bound-state production, including quarkonium, leptonium, and B(c) mesons within Non-Relativistic Quantum Chromo-Dynamics (NRQCD) and Non-Relativistic Quantum Electro-Dynamics (NRQED). In these proceedings, I focus on the extension of MadGraph5_aMC@NLO to quarkonium states and describe the capabilities of the new framework for inclusive and associated S-wave quarkonium production in a wide variety of experimental environments at Leading Order (LO). These developments provide the community with a unified, automated, and efficient framework for bound-state production in QED and QCD, and establish a solid foundation for our future Next-to-Leading-Order (NLO) extension.

AI.tldr: First implementation in MadGraph5_aMC@NLO for bound-state production (quarkonium, leptonium, B(c) mesons) using NRQCD/NRQED; enables automated LO inclusive/associated S-wave quarkonium production across experimental setups; lays groundwork for future NLO extension.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified, automated, and efficient framework for bound-state production in QED and QCD, addressing the lack of such tools for quarkonium, leptonium, and B(c) mesons within NRQCD/NRQED.
AI.method: Extension of MadGraph5_aMC@NLO to incorporate NRQCD and NRQED formalisms for bound-state production, specifically targeting S-wave quarkonium states at Leading Order (LO).
AI.result: Successful implementation enabling inclusive and associated S-wave quarkonium production simulations across diverse experimental environments at LO; establishes foundation for forthcoming NLO extension.
AI.conclusion: This work delivers the first automated, general-purpose tool for bound-state production in MadGraph5_aMC@NLO, significantly enhancing phenomenological studies of quarkonia and related states, and enabling systematic higher-order improvements.

title: Cohomological Aspects of Entanglement Entropy: From Information Theory to Noncommutative Geometry
summary: We develop a cohomological framework for entanglement entropy that unifies perspectives from information theory, operator algebras, and noncommutative geometry. Starting from the information-theoretic characterization of entropy as a 1-cocycle, we show how this structure generalizes to the quantum setting through Hochschild and cyclic cohomology. A central result is the embedding of an entanglement complex into the Connes cyclic bicomplex via a conditional expectation, identifying entanglement cohomology as the kernel of the restriction map from a von Neumann algebra to its subalgebra. The Tomita-Takesaki modular theory provides the dynamical structure, with the Connes-Radon-Nikodym cocycle serving as the fundamental object encoding relative entanglement. This framework naturally accommodates Type III von Neumann algebras, where no local density matrix exists, offering a rigorous foundation for entanglement in quantum field theory and holography.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a cohomological framework for entanglement entropy, unifying information theory, operator algebras, and noncommutative geometry; it identifies entanglement cohomology as the kernel of a restriction map in the Connes cyclic bicomplex, uses Tomita-Takesaki theory and Connes-Radon-Nikodym cocycles to encode relative entanglement, and extends rigorously to Type III algebras—crucial for QFT and holography.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified, mathematically rigorous framework for entanglement entropy that transcends the limitations of density-matrix-based definitions—especially in quantum field theory and holography, where local density matrices fail (e.g., Type III von Neumann algebras).
AI.method: Constructs an 'entanglement complex' embedded into the Connes cyclic bicomplex via conditional expectation; leverages Hochschild and cyclic cohomology to generalize the information-theoretic 1-cocycle characterization of entropy to quantum systems; employs Tomita-Takesaki modular theory and the Connes-Radon-Nikodym cocycle as central dynamical and relative-entanglement objects.
AI.result: Entanglement cohomology is rigorously defined as the kernel of the restriction map from a von Neumann algebra to its subalgebra within the cyclic bicomplex; the Connes-Radon-Nikodym cocycle emerges as the fundamental invariant encoding relative entanglement; the framework is fully applicable to Type III factors, enabling a density-matrix-free treatment of entanglement in QFT and AdS/CFT.
AI.conclusion: Cohomology—not just entropy functionals—provides the proper structural language for entanglement; this approach resolves foundational issues in algebraic quantum field theory and holography by replacing operational or geometric heuristics with intrinsic algebraic-topological invariants.

title: Low-energy brane decoupling in AdS flux vacua
summary: We study the decoupling of branes sourcing AdS flux vacua from the asymptotic bulk using scalar-wave absorption probabilities. In a one-modulus truncation, the result depends only on the dimension of the AdS vacuum and on the asymptotic steepness of the scalar potential. We find that for any steepness and for any dimension greater than two the absorption probability vanishes in the low-energy limit, showing that the branes decouple from the bulk. We illustrate the general analysis in several scale-separated AdS vacua. For DGKT we find $P_{\rm abs}\simω^{27/7}$ and an effective transverse dimension $d_{\rm eff}=20/7$. Interestingly, the scalar potential along the brane-induced moduli trajectory agrees with that obtained by compactifying a hypothetical $(4+13/7)$-dimensional gravity theory on a $13/7$-dimensional sphere threaded by flux. We also apply the analysis to scale-separated $\mathrm{AdS}_3$ examples and to the simplest one-modulus KKLT model.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates brane-bulk decoupling in AdS flux vacua using scalar-wave absorption probabilities; it finds universal vanishing absorption in the low-energy limit for d > 2, and computes explicit scaling laws (e.g., P_abs ∼ ω^{27/7} for DGKT) linked to effective dimensional reduction.
AI.motivation: To understand how localized branes sourcing AdS flux vacua decouple from the asymptotic bulk — a key issue for consistency of effective field theory and holography in string compactifications.
AI.method: Computes low-energy scalar-wave absorption probability by branes in a one-modulus truncation of the effective action; relates absorption exponent to AdS dimension and asymptotic potential steepness; applies to concrete examples (DGKT, AdS₃, KKLT).
AI.result: Absorption probability P_abs → 0 as ω → 0 for all AdS_d with d > 2, regardless of potential steepness; for DGKT: P_abs ∼ ω^{27/7}, yielding deff = 20/7; scalar potential along moduli trajectory matches dimensional reduction of a (4+13/7)-D gravity on a 13/7-sphere with flux.
AI.conclusion: Brane-bulk decoupling is generic in scale-separated AdS vacua above two dimensions, supporting EFT validity; the emergent fractional effective dimensions suggest novel geometric interpretations of moduli dynamics.

title: Rotational Brownian Motion and $\mathrm{J/ψ}$ Spin Alignment in Heavy-Ion Collisions
summary: The heavy-quark polarization in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions (HICs) serves as a probe for unfolding the characteristics of deconfined QCD. The present study explores the spin alignment of $\mathrm{J/ψ}$ in the HICs by employing the rotational Brownian motion of charm quarks in the presence of a strong magnetic field. We derive an analytical expression for the polarization of the $c$-$\bar{c}$ pair based on the Fokker-Planck equation under the consideration of spin-vorticity coupling. These polarized $c$-$\bar{c}$ pairs lead to the formation of the $\mathrm{J}/ψ$ at the hadronization surface via the coalescence and fragmentation mechanisms. Correspondingly, we obtain the $m=0$ diagonal element $ρ_{00}$ of the $\mathrm{J}/ψ$ spin-density matrix, which quantifies its spin alignment along the chosen quantization axis. Our study provides a microscopic description of heavy-quark spin transport and suggests rotational diffusion as a possible mechanism underlying the observed $\mathrm{J}/ψ$ spin alignment.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes rotational Brownian motion of charm quarks under strong magnetic fields as a microscopic mechanism for J/ψ spin alignment in heavy-ion collisions, deriving ρ₀₀ via spin-vorticity–coupled Fokker-Planck dynamics.
AI.motivation: To explain the observed spin alignment of J/ψ in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions as a probe of deconfined QCD medium properties, particularly through heavy-quark polarization.
AI.method: Analytical solution of the Fokker-Planck equation for charm quark rotational Brownian motion, incorporating spin-vorticity coupling and magnetic field effects; modeling J/ψ formation via coalescence and fragmentation from polarized c-c̄ pairs; computing the spin-density matrix element ρ₀₀.
AI.result: An analytical expression for c-c̄ pair polarization and the resulting J/ψ spin-density matrix element ρ₀₀, quantifying spin alignment along the quantization axis.
AI.conclusion: Rotational diffusion of charm quarks—driven by vorticity and magnetic fields—provides a viable microscopic origin for J/ψ spin alignment, offering new insight into heavy-quark spin transport in the QGP.

title: Topological Modular Forms Constrain Threshold States in Extremal $\mathcal{N}=1$ AdS$_3$ Gravity
summary: We identify a topological constraint on extremal $\mathcal{N}=1$ AdS$_3$ spectra that is not implied by genus-one modular covariance of the three even spin structure partition functions. Assuming the expected topological modular forms divisibility of the Ramond Witten index, we show that for infinitely many odd $n$ at central charge $c=12n$, an extremal holomorphic $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theory requires an odd number of Neveu--Schwarz primaries at the BTZ threshold. Thus the strict ansatz with no threshold primaries is excluded for this infinite family.

AI.tldr: The paper identifies a new topological constraint on extremal N=1 AdS₃ spectra, showing that for infinitely many odd n at c=12n, extremal holomorphic N=1 SCFTs must have an odd number of NS primaries at the BTZ threshold—excluding the strict no-threshold-primaries ansatz.
AI.motivation: To uncover topological constraints on extremal N=1 AdS₃ spectra beyond genus-one modular covariance, particularly leveraging tmf-theoretic divisibility of the Ramond Witten index.
AI.method: Applies topological modular forms (tmf) theory to constrain the Ramond Witten index; combines modular invariance, extremality, and holomorphy assumptions with spectral analysis of NS and R sectors at the BTZ threshold.
AI.result: For infinitely many odd integers n, at central charge c = 12n, any extremal holomorphic N=1 SCFT must contain an odd number of Neveu–Schwarz primary operators at the BTZ black hole threshold energy; hence the 'no threshold primaries' ansatz is ruled out for this infinite family.
AI.conclusion: A previously unrecognized topological obstruction—rooted in tmf divisibility—exists for extremal N=1 AdS₃ holography, demonstrating that modular covariance alone is insufficient to characterize consistent spectra.

title: Channel-Resolved High-Overtone Quasinormal Modes Decode Kasner Scaling inside Black Holes
summary: The high-overtone quasinormal-mode spectrum encodes the near-singularity Kasner scaling of black-hole interiors. We show that distinct structures in this spectrum independently determine the temporal and spatial Kasner grades, allowing the corresponding metric exponents to be reconstructed without imposing Kasner constraints or invoking holography. We demonstrate this independent reconstruction at the fixed Kasner point of five-dimensional asymptotically flat Schwarzschild and planar Schwarzschild--AdS$_5$, and then extend it to a continuously varying Gibbons--Maeda black-hole family. The reconstructed exponents satisfy the Kasner relation a posteriori, providing a nontrivial geometric consistency check. More generally, the high-overtone spectrum separates into global spectral data and local algebraic corrections whose fractional powers are fixed by the near-singularity Kasner geometry. These fractional corrections therefore provide a direct spectral probe of the local geometry behind the horizon.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes that the high-overtone quasinormal-mode spectrum of black holes encodes the near-singularity Kasner geometry, enabling independent reconstruction of temporal and spatial Kasner exponents without assuming Kasner constraints or holography; it validates this on Schwarzschild and Gibbons–Maeda black holes and identifies fractional spectral corrections as direct probes of the local geometry behind the horizon.
AI.motivation: To extract near-singularity geometric information—specifically Kasner exponents—from observable (asymptotic) black-hole quasinormal-mode spectra, bypassing assumptions of Kasner symmetry or holographic duality.
AI.method: Analytical and spectral analysis of high-overtone quasinormal modes in five-dimensional Schwarzschild, planar Schwarzschild–AdS₅, and Gibbons–Maeda black-hole spacetimes; decomposition of the spectrum into global (large-scale) and local (fractional-power) contributions tied to Kasner scaling.
AI.result: Distinct spectral structures independently determine temporal and spatial Kasner grades; reconstructed exponents satisfy the Kasner relation a posteriori; fractional corrections in the spectrum are fixed by near-singularity Kasner geometry.
AI.conclusion: The high-overtone quasinormal-mode spectrum serves as a direct spectral probe of the local geometry behind the event horizon, with its fractional algebraic corrections encoding the Kasner exponents intrinsically.

title: On the relaxation dynamics of non-equilibrium quantum systems
summary: We investigate the relaxation of an approximately conserved charge in interacting quantum systems close to local equilibrium. To this end, we provide a pedagogical review of Zubarev's non-equilibrium statistical operator approach in the minimal setting of a single non-conserved charge and apply it to the problem at hand. We explicitly highlight the physical assumptions that lead to a local relaxation law: weak charge violation, a separation between the short timescale of microscopic correlations and the much longer timescale of charge relaxation, and the resulting loss of microscopic memory. Under these conditions, the leading relaxation rate is determined by an equilibrium correlation function of the charge-violating operator. We show that the same result follows from a simpler local-equilibrium construction based on the system's evolution over an intermediate timescale, providing a direct alternative for practical calculations and making the common physical ingredients of the two approaches explicit. Beyond the decay law itself, we relate the relaxation rate to the equilibrium diffusion of the same charge. We then allow the charge density to vary in space, which leads to a diffusion-relaxation equation. Finally, we illustrate the formalism through electroweak $\mathrm{B+L}$ washout and a perturbative scalar model, where agreement with the linearized Boltzmann equation establishes a direct connection between equilibrium-correlator and kinetic descriptions.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a local relaxation law for approximately conserved charges in interacting quantum systems near local equilibrium, using Zubarev's non-equilibrium statistical operator method and an alternative local-equilibrium construction; it links the relaxation rate to equilibrium correlation functions of charge-violating operators, connects it to diffusion, generalizes to spatially varying charge density (yielding a diffusion-relaxation equation), and validates the formalism in electroweak B+L washout and a scalar model against the linearized Boltzmann equation.
AI.motivation: To systematically understand how approximately conserved charges relax in interacting quantum many-body systems near local equilibrium—particularly when exact conservation is weakly violated—and to bridge microscopic (equilibrium correlator) and macroscopic (kinetic/Boltzmann) descriptions of such relaxation.
AI.method: Applies Zubarev's non-equilibrium statistical operator formalism in the minimal setting of one weakly violated charge; identifies key physical assumptions (weak violation, timescale separation, memory loss); derives a local relaxation law and diffusion-relaxation equation; introduces an alternative local-equilibrium construction over intermediate timescales; computes relaxation rates via Kubo-type equilibrium correlation functions; validates against linearized Boltzmann equation in two concrete models.
AI.result: A universal local relaxation law with rate governed by an equilibrium correlation function of the charge-violating operator; equivalence between Zubarev’s formalism and a simpler local-equilibrium approach; derivation of a diffusion-relaxation equation for spatially inhomogeneous charge density; explicit relation between relaxation rate and equilibrium charge diffusion coefficient; quantitative agreement with linearized Boltzmann results in electroweak B+L washout and a perturbative scalar theory.
AI.conclusion: Approximate charge relaxation near local equilibrium is governed by equilibrium physics—even far from global equilibrium—as encoded in correlation functions of symmetry-breaking operators; the formalism unifies statistical-mechanical and kinetic approaches, providing a first-principles foundation for effective transport and washout equations in high-energy and condensed matter contexts.

title: Exact Black Branes in General Dimensions in Higher-Curvature Scalar-Tensor Gravity
summary: We obtain two families of neutral planar black branes in a potential-free dilaton-coupled Lovelock--Horndeski theory. Heterotic compactification relates higher-dimensional curvature to scalar dynamics and motivates the interaction structure. At fixed scalar zero mode, the horizon radius and temperature vary while the complete stationary Wald entropy remains constant and positive. The exponential scalar factor at the horizon exactly compensates the area growth, giving this behavior a direct geometric explanation. An exact coefficient analysis determines the two four-dimensional branches and their continuation to every higher dimension through closed coupling relations. The linear family is conformally flat and leaves the AdS scale free at fixed couplings; the fractional family is Weyl curved and fixes that scale. The common kinetic relation also excludes their realization through a real one-scalar flat-torus reduction of a metric--dilaton parent.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs two families of neutral planar black branes in a dilaton-coupled Lovelock–Horndeski theory without scalar potential; it shows Wald entropy remains constant despite varying horizon radius and temperature, due to exact compensation by the exponential dilaton factor at the horizon; the two families—linear (conformally flat, AdS scale unfixed) and fractional (Weyl curved, AdS scale fixed)—are fully determined by closed coupling relations across dimensions and cannot arise from a real one-scalar toroidal reduction of a metric–dilaton theory.
AI.motivation: Heterotic compactification motivates the specific scalar–curvature interaction structure in the Lovelock–Horndeski framework, linking higher-dimensional geometry to scalar dynamics; the goal is to explore consistent neutral black brane solutions with nontrivial dilaton profiles and robust thermodynamic behavior.
AI.method: Exact analytical construction of planar black brane solutions in a potential-free dilaton-coupled Lovelock–Horndeski theory; systematic analysis of Wald entropy, horizon geometry, and scalar profile; classification via exact coefficient matching to identify two distinct solution families; dimensional continuation using closed coupling relations; exclusion proof for toroidal reduction origin via kinetic-term comparison.
AI.result: Two distinct families of neutral planar black branes are obtained: (1) a linear family, conformally flat, with free AdS scale at fixed couplings; (2) a fractional family, Weyl curved, fixing the AdS scale. Both exhibit constant, positive stationary Wald entropy due to precise cancellation between area growth and exponential dilaton suppression at the horizon. Their coupling structures are fully determined and extend uniquely to all higher dimensions. Neither family admits a real one-scalar flat-torus reduction from a metric–dilaton parent theory.
AI.conclusion: The constancy of Wald entropy arises geometrically from horizon-local dilaton compensation, not fine-tuning; the two families represent fundamentally inequivalent branches of the theory, distinguished by conformal structure and scale-fixing properties, and their existence underscores the richness of scalar–gravity couplings beyond standard reductions.
